**Scientific findings:** Mother Magazine's preview highlighted claims such as that same-sex dads snuggling their newborn baby born via surrogacy experience the same surge of oxytocin as a mother who has given birth, and that new-parent worry is linked to a specific shift in brain activity. Suno has no official public API, so every programmatic route goes through a third-party wrapper. The results point to a few options and a consistent pattern for custom mode.

**Options:**
- **Apiframe** is a hosted wrapper. Its docs say No official Suno API exists. A basic request posts to its music endpoint with a `sunoParams` object. The pricing is a flat 11 credits per generation regardless of model version.
- **Evolink** describes a similar setup. It notes that there is no widely available, public-facing "official" API key, though Suno has rolled out beta access to some partners.
- **Open-source wrappers** include a Rust CLI, suno 0.8.0, which talks directly to Suno's API and is documented as supporting custom lyrics, style tags, and v5.5 features. It also reads browser credentials for auth. A Mintlify guide for the gcui-art/suno-api project uses a different endpoint (`/api/custom_generate`) and a different model naming scheme, so the wrappers are not interchangeable.

**Custom mode vs. description mode:**
- Description mode (`custom_mode: false`) takes a short description, capped at 500 characters, and Suno writes the lyrics and style. Description mode (custom_mode: false) takes a short song description and Suno handles the rest, capped at 500 characters.
- Custom mode (`custom_mode: true`) takes your lyrics in the prompt field, up to 5,000 characters, with style and title passed separately. Suno uses section markers like [Verse], [Chorus], [Bridge] to understand song structure.
- Style is passed as comma-separated tags. Specific tags work better than generic ones. The guide's example is that a string like "upbeat pop, female vocalist, synth, 120bpm" gives more consistent results than "pop" alone.
- Negative tags exclude elements, and the Apiframe docs list them alongside style weight, vocal gender, and an instrumental flag.

**Caveats:** Sources disagree on model versions. Apiframe lists V4 through V5_5 with V4_5PLUS as the default, while the evolink API lists suno-v5-beta as its default. Check each wrapper's current docs before building on any of them. Using unofficial wrappers may also conflict with Suno's terms of service, which I did not verify in this search.

# Summary: "I'm Upping My P(doom)" Music Video

This is a code-rendered music video with word-synced karaoke typography. Every frame is a deterministic function of song time, so the browser preview and the offline export match.

## Tech Stack

- **Renderer:** TypeScript and three.js, run with bun and built with Vite.
- **Offline export:** `scripts/render.ts` launches headless Google Chrome through playwright-core. The Chromes send raw frames over WebSocket to ffmpeg, which encodes with libx264 (x264, CRF 16) and AAC audio.
- **Effects:** post-processing includes bloom, halation, and film grain. Lines are drawn with GPU line batches, and some rooms are ray-marched.
- **Typography:** Archivo, IBM Plex Mono, and Cormorant Garamond, plus single-stroke plotter fonts from the `hersheytext` package.
- **Motion blur:** each frame averages many sub-frames over a short shutter. The `--samples auto` setting picks a sample count per 32×32 tile.
- **Analysis (Python, managed with uv):** Demucs `htdemucs_ft` for stem separation, a mel-band-roformer karaoke model (via audio-separator) for the lead vocal, CTC forced alignment cross-checked with Whisper, and beat, downbeat, and onset analysis.

## Lyric Word-Sync

- `lyrics/lyrics.src.js` holds the original line-level lyrics with approximate timings.
- `analysis/align.py` runs CTC forced alignment, cross-checked with Whisper, to produce `data/lyrics.json`. This file has word-level timings and some syllable-level timings.
- `data/audio.json` holds the tempo (132.007 BPM), beats, downbeats, sections, drum and vocal onsets, and loudness envelopes.

## Scene Structure

- Each plate is its own module in `app/src/scenes/`: open, loss, prompt, hook, room, shoggoth, spacetime, ascent, bureau, leftturn, paperclips, fuse, stack, dense, loom, ilya, and outro. Shared motifs live alongside them.
- `app/src/timeline.ts` is the edit. It anchors each scene window to lyric lines and snaps it to the beat grid.
- The engine and scene API are documented in `docs/ENGINE.md`. The concept, style bible, and plate-by-plate treatment are in `docs/TREATMENT.md`.

## Workflow with Claude

The project was made with Claude (listed as Opus 5.5) in Claude Code. The concept and treatment, lyric alignment and audio analysis, the renderer, every scene, and the renders were all developed in conversation with Claude.

## Song, Suno, and Credits

- The song is not the project's own work. The original lyrics are by osmarks, built on an opening verse and chorus by MusicPerson, with suggestions from the EleutherAI Discord and help from Claude on the outro and final chorus.
- The original was generated with Udio and released in November 2024.
- This video uses the "Claude-Pop" version made with Suno, posted by deckard in September 2026.
- Fonts are under the SIL Open Font License. Single-stroke fonts are OFL or public domain.

## Directory Layout

- `audio/`: the song (`pdoom.mp3`)
- `lyrics/`: original line-level lyrics
- `analysis/`: Python timing tools (`align.py`, `analyze.py`)
- `data/`: `lyrics.json` and `audio.json`
- `app/`: renderer
  - `src/engine/`: timeline, post-processing, typography, GPU lines, HUD
  - `src/scenes/`: one module per plate
  - `src/timeline.ts`: scene windows
  - `scripts/render.ts`: offline renderer
- `docs/`: `TREATMENT.md`, `ENGINE.md`
- `out/`: renders (not in the repo)

## Commands

**Requirements:** bun, Google Chrome, and ffmpeg with libx264. uv is needed only for the analysis tools.

**Preview in the browser:**
```
cd app
bun install
bunx vite
```
Then open http://localhost:5173. Use `?t=23` to start at a given time.

**Render 1080p60:**
```
cd app
bun scripts/render.ts video --samples auto --shutter 0.2 --out ../out/pdoom.mp4
```

**Render 4K60:**
```
cd app
bun scripts/render.ts video --scale 2 --samples auto --shutter 0.2 --x264 aq-mode=3:rc-lookahead=30 --out ../out/pdoom-4k.mp4
```

Other render modes are `stills`, `sheet`, `perf`, and `plates`.

**Regenerate timing data:** the stems and intermediates are not in the repo, so you must first create them.
```
cd analysis
uv run python -m demucs -n htdemucs_ft -o stems ../audio/pdoom.mp3   # run from analysis/
uv run python align.py      # produces data/lyrics.json
uv run python analyze.py    # produces data/audio.json
```

## Notes on Cost

- A 4K render of the full song takes about 57 minutes on an M5 Pro, per the README.
- Memory peaks around 23 GB.
- The 4K file runs at about 670 Mbit/s at CRF 16 (about 13 GB). CRF 18 gives about 450 Mbit/s, and CRF 20 about 230 Mbit/s.
- The alignment models download about 4 GB of weights into `analysis/.cache/`, which you can delete afterward.

## Licensing

The code is MIT licensed. The song, lyrics, and audio are not covered by that license and belong to their authors.

# Summary: PDoomVideo

This GitHub repo holds the source code for a music video for the song *I'm Upping My P(doom)*, made with Claude Opus 5.5.

## Tech Stack
- **p5.js and p5.brush** draw every frame in `studio.html`.
- **Headless Chrome** renders the frames, and **ffmpeg** encodes them into an MP4.
- **Node.js** runs `render.mjs`, which handles rendering and encoding.

## Lyric Timing
The README doesn't explain the timing mechanism. It says `src/` contains the lyrics and "the timeline," and the render command covers frames 0 to 156.6 seconds. The song file is `assets/pdoom.mp3`.

## Scene Structure
- The video has **nine chapters**, one file each in `src/ch/`.
- Shared code in `src/` includes Clawd (the main character), guest characters, props, lyrics, and the timeline.
- `STORYBOARD.md` is Opus's shot-by-shot plan. It was written after the first generation, with instructions to use P5 brushstrokes, make each scene visually interesting, and link every scene to the next with a transition.

## Workflow with Claude Opus 5.5
- The video was made in two generations, both in Claude Code:
  1. **First generation** (`legacy/`): Opus 5.5 (Medium).
  2. **Second generation** (everything else): Opus 5.5.
- The author specified no scene ideas. The only direction was to use the Clawd character design and to give each lyric interesting visuals and transitions.
- Opus wrote `ANIMATION_GUIDE.md` to brief the subagents it ran in parallel on style and code.

## Song and Lyrics Sources
- **Song:** The author could only trace it to a 2024 YouTube video, and says that's as far as they could find.
- **Lyrics:** Taken from Osmarks, which shows the original Udio generations along with an interpretation of each lyric.
- **Inspiration:** A post on X.

## Directory Layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `src/ch/` | Nine chapter files |
| `src/` | Shared code: Clawd, guests, props, lyrics, timeline |
| `studio.html` | Page where each frame is painted (p5.js, p5.brush) |
| `render.mjs` | Renders frames in headless Chrome and encodes the MP4 |
| `STORYBOARD.md` | Opus's shot plan |
| `ANIMATION_GUIDE.md` | Opus's style and code guide for subagents |
| `legacy/` | First generation |
| `assets/` | Includes the song |

## Commands

Requires Node.js, Google Chrome, and ffmpeg. Run `npm install` first.

```bash
# Paint every frame into out/frames (resumable)
node render.mjs --frames=0:156.6 --workers=4

# Join the frames and the song into an MP4
node render.mjs --encode --out=out/pdoom.mp4
```

If Chrome isn't at the default Windows path, add `--chrome=<path to chrome>`.

**Babies** is a 2020 American documentary series on Netflix. It follows 15 families around the world through their babies' first year.

**Part 1 (February 21, 2020)**

1. **"Love"**: Bonding biology, and how caregiving, social interaction, and stress can physically change both parent and newborn.
2. **"First Food"**: How breast milk, iron, and microbes nourish and protect infants.
3. **"Crawling"**: Crawling as a developmental milestone with more significance than a passing phase.
4. **"First Words"**: The rhythm of language, and how babies learn speech patterns before they can talk.
5. **"Sleep"**: Infant sleep, including twitching, sleep-tracking apps, and naps.
6. **"First Steps"**: How walking changes a baby's view of the world, along with neonatal reflexes, skeletal development, and early talking.

**Part 2 (June 19, 2020)**

7. **"What Babies Know"**: Evidence that infants are born with expectations about everyday life, challenging the idea that they start as a blank slate.
8. **"Movement"**: How infants learn to anticipate and respond to others' movements.
9. **"Senses"**: How babies develop touch, taste, and vision.
10. **"Relationships"**: How babies get along with others, including through humor, morality, and shared experiences.
11. **"Nature and Nurture"**: How genetics and environment interact as infants develop their sense of self.
12. **"Toddlers"**: The social skills toddlers naturally show, which the series presents as distinguishing humans from other species.

**Production details**

- **Genre:** Documentary

**I'm Upping My P(doom)** is a music video made entirely by Claude Opus 5.5 in Claude Code, with no scene ideas specified. The only direction was to use the Clawd character design and give each lyric interesting visuals and transitions. The video was produced in two generations: a first pass (in `legacy/`) at Opus 5.5 (Medium), and a second pass at Opus 5.5 for everything else.

- Animation base for Claude with Opus 5.5: https://github.com/JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase

**Repository contents:**
- `src/ch/`: the nine chapters, one file each
- `src/`: shared code (Clawd, guest characters, props, lyrics, timeline)
- `studio.html`: the page each frame is painted on, using p5.js and p5.brush
- `render.mjs`: renders frames in headless Chrome and encodes the MP4 with ffmpeg
- `STORYBOARD.md`: Opus's shot-by-shot plan
- `ANIMATION_GUIDE.md`: Opus's style and code guide for its subagents
- `legacy/`: the first generation

**Rendering:** You need Node.js, Google Chrome, and ffmpeg. The song is at `assets/pdoom.mp3`. Run `npm install`, then `node render.mjs --frames=0:156.6 --workers=4` to paint frames (resumable), and `node render.mjs --encode --out=out/pdoom.mp4` to build the MP4. If Chrome isn't at the default Windows path, add `--chrome=<path>`.

# suno 0.8.0: Summary

**What it is:** A Rust CLI that generates AI music from the terminal by talking directly to Suno's API. The page says Suno has no official API, so this is a third-party client. It's MIT-licensed and published on crates.io.

## Install

```
brew tap paperfoot/tap
brew install suno
```

```
cargo install suno
```

Pre-built binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows are on GitHub Releases. `suno update` is distribution-aware: it self-replaces standalone installs but prints the upgrade command for Homebrew or Cargo installs.

## Authentication

- **`suno auth --login`** (recommended): reads the Clerk auth cookie from Chrome, Arc, Brave, Firefox, or Edge, exchanges it for a JWT, and stores the session in a `0600` local file.
- **`suno auth --cookie <cookie>`**: manual paste for headless servers. Accepts a raw `__client` value or a full `Cookie` header.
- **`suno auth --jwt <token>`**: direct JWT, which the page says expires in about an hour.
- **`suno auth --refresh`** and **`suno auth --logout`**.

Environment variables: `SUNO_*` overrides for config keys, plus `SUNO_CONFIG_DIR` and `SUNO_DATA_DIR`. Precedence is flag > env > config file > default. Run `suno doctor` to check auth, JWT freshness, Chrome, API reachability, and credits.

## Generation

- **`suno generate`**: custom mode with lyrics, tags, and sliders.
  ```
  suno generate --title "My Song" --tags "pop, warm" --persona <id> --lyrics "[Verse]\nHello from the CLI"
  ```
- **`suno describe --prompt "..."`**: Suno writes the lyrics from a description (up to 500 chars).
- **`suno lyrics`**: lyrics only, free.
- **`suno write`**: free scaffold generator that outputs a lyrics file. `suno generate` refuses lyrics that still contain `<...>` placeholders (exit 3) unless `--force` is passed.
- **`suno extend`**, **`suno cover <clip_id> --tags "jazz, smooth piano" --model v5.5 --wait`**, **`suno remaster`**, **`suno concat`**, **`suno stems`**.

**Flags for `generate`:**

| Flag | Purpose / limit |
|---|---|
| `--title` | Up to 100 chars |
| `--tags` | Style direction, up to 1000 chars |
| `--exclude` | Negative tags to avoid, up to 1000 chars |
| `--lyrics` / `--lyrics-file` | Up to 5000 chars |
| `--model` | v5.5 (default), v5, v4.5+, v4.5-all, v4.5, v4, v3.5, v3, v2 |
| `--vocal` | `male` or `female` |
| `--persona` | Voice persona UUID |
| `--weirdness`, `--style-influence` | 0–100 |
| `--audio-influence` | 0–100, for generate/cover |
| `--instrumental` | No vocals |
| `--wait` | Block until done |
| `--download <dir>` | Auto-download after generation |
| `--token` | Pre-solved hCaptcha token |
| `--no-captcha` | Disable the captcha solver |
| `--force` | Bypass the duplicate-run guard |

Personas: you create the voice in Suno's web UI, then pass its ID. The CLI does not create voices yet.

## Downloads

```
suno download <id1> <id2> --output ./songs/
```

Files are named `title-slug-clipid8.mp3`. MP3s get embedded plain lyrics (USLT) and synced word-level lyrics (SYLT). For LRC files, use `suno timed-lyrics <clip_id> --lrc > song.lrc`.

## Credits, Models, and Rate Limits

- A v5.5 generate call costs about 70 credits (35 per clip, 2 clips per call), measured live by the author.
- `v4.5-all` is described as the cheapest option.
- Check `suno credits` for balance and `suno models` for what your plan can use.
- Polling for `--wait` starts at 5s, doubles up to 15s, and times out at 600s by default.
- Exit code 4 means rate limited; the page advises waiting 30–60s before retrying. It gives no specific request quotas.

## Caveats

- **Unofficial:** No official API, and the CLI depends on Suno's web endpoints, which can change. The author notes cover/remaster support "should be recaptured" whenever Suno changes its web schema.
- **Captcha:** Most accounts aren't captcha-gated. When one is, the solver drives Chrome. If challenges keep failing, the page suggests generating one song in the suno.com UI and retrying.
- **Self-update:** Standalone downloads are not yet signature- or attestation-verified.
- **Not covered:** Audio upload and voice persona creation are listed as unimplemented.
- **Terms of service:** The page doesn't discuss Suno's terms of service. Check Suno's current terms yourself before using this tool.

## How the document is organized

**1. Concept statement.** The video is framed as plates from an illustrated treatise on the end of the world. A P(doom) value rises at each hook, and one orange "spark" runs through every scene, writing, plotting, and eventually detonating.

**2. Style bible.**
- **Tone:** Dynamic, beat-synced motion with strong eases. Funny in a deadpan, straight-faced way. Explicit bans on neon cyberpunk, AI-looking imagery, and copied artwork.
- **Palette:** Named colors such as ink, bone, and signal orange, plus one rare accent (acid) for a single moment. Light and dark "bone paper" inversions give the edit its rhythm.
- **Typography:** Three families (Archivo for lyrics, IBM Plex Mono for the machine voice, Cormorant Garamond for the prophetic register) plus single-stroke fonts for written text. There are craft rules for kerning and punctuation.
- **Karaoke rules:** Per-word sync, readability, title-safe margins, and HUD clearance.
- **Motifs:** The spark, eyes, the "assistant smile" mask, the P(doom) readout, the prompt-field template, and the recurring hook slam.

**3. Plate specifications.** A table lists each scene's ID, time window, lyric anchor, and owner. Each plate then gets a prose spec covering its visual style, beat-by-beat staging, lyric treatment, P(doom) cameo, and any parameters (for example, `prompt` takes a variant, and `hook` takes a number from 1 to 4).

**4. Lyric anchoring.** Scenes never hard-code times. They look up their lyric lines by content through the `Lyrics` API, and windows come from `timeline.ts`, which is derived from the aligned lyrics.

**5. Technical conventions.** Deterministic rendering, hard cuts on downbeats, and a performance budget under 25 ms per frame, with details in `docs/ENGINE.md`.

## Three example plate specs (condensed)

The song's lyric lines are paraphrased below, and the spec text is abbreviated to stay within the quoting limit.

**`prompt` (params: `variant`: chatgpt | sydney | gato)**
- Visual: A vast dark field with one thin prompt field. The plea is typed as tokens in Plex Mono on the sung words.
- Per token: A small next-token distribution of 4–5 joke candidates flickers above it, and the sampled token lights orange. For example, "ChatGPT, 0.61 · Claude 0.12 · Siri 0.04 · Mom 0.02".
- Ending: A caret blinks, ⏎ is pressed, and the plate launches into the chorus on the downbeat.
- Variants: `chatgpt` pulls engraved rings toward the camera. `sydney` closes vertical bars on the beat and draws a single unsettling smile curve. `gato` is slow and fragile, with letters drifting apart.

**`hook` (params: `n`: 1–4)**
- Visual: The hook phrase as a one-word-per-hit full-frame Archivo 900 slam, landing exactly on each sung word.
- Escalation: (1) bone on ink. (2) ink on signal-orange field, heavier. (3) hairline type, tiny, slow, eerie. (4) strobing, stacked outlines, shake, digits multiplying.
- P(doom) cameo: The HUD number leaves its corner and blows up full-screen as it rolls to the new value, then returns.

**`bureau` (verse 3, part 1)**
- Visual: Inverted palette of bone paper and ink. A safety evaluation form (Form 7-B) with checkboxes and typewritten fields where the lyric is typed.
- Beats: An orange rubber stamp slams "SAFE ENOUGH" with ink texture and screen shake on the stressed word. A pulse sweeps forward through an MLP diagram, then back, with the word mirrored on the return.
- Ending: A von Neumann diagram is struck through in orange, then burned in two by the next plate's critical path.

Include the key function names and any model identifiers."

## Pipeline overview

The script `align.py` is the final stage. It fuses outputs from three upstream scripts (`ctc_emissions.py`, `whisper_run.py`, `vocal_feats.py`) that aren't included here, so their internals are known only from the docstring and `NOTES`.

## Packages and models

**Imported in `align.py`:**
- `common` (project module: `WORK`, `DATA`, `QA` paths, `load_lyrics_src()`)
- `ctcalign` (`FRAME`, `align`, `emissions`, `word_table`)
- `pron` (`pron()`, which maps words to phonetic spellings)
- `qa_plot` (`plot()`, used only with `--plots`)
- `numpy`, `scipy.ndimage` (`median_filter`, `maximum_filter1d`, `uniform_filter1d`), `scipy.signal.find_peaks`
- Standard library: `json`, `re`, `sys`, `difflib.SequenceMatcher`

**Models and tools named in the document:**
- Demucs for vocal stem separation (the separator package is not named)
- torchaudio `MMS_FA` and `wav2vec2-large-lv60k-960h` for CTC emissions
- mlx-whisper `large-v3-turbo` for word timestamps
- A mel-roformer karaoke model for a lead-vocal stem, used on the final chorus

## Steps from MP3 to JSON

1. **Decode:** The MP3 is decoded gaplessly. This timeline matches `data/audio.json`.
2. **Stem separation:** Demucs isolates the vocal stem. Stems are shifted −23 ms to compensate for LAME encoder delay.
3. **CTC emissions (`ctc_emissions.py`):** Frame-wise log-probs at 20 ms frames come from both acoustic models, each run on the mono sum and on the left and right channels. These are fused as a probability mixture (`fused6`, the `PRIMARY` set). The other sets in `ALTS` serve as agreement checks.
4. **Whisper (`whisper_run.py`):** mlx-whisper produces word timestamps, saved to `whisper_turbo_prompt.json`.
5. **Vocal features (`vocal_feats.py`):** RMS, pitch, onset, and sibilance features are computed at a 5 ms hop and saved to `vocal_feats.npz`.
6. **Global alignment:** `align()` runs one constrained Viterbi pass over all lines, with a garbage "star" token between lines to absorb ad-libs. `ANCHORS` and `LINE_WINDOWS` constrain it. `word_table()` converts the path to words. Alternate alignments are computed the same way.
7. **Signal refinement:** `refine()` adjusts each sub-word unit's start using three rules, applied in order:
   - `rest-onset`: voice re-entry after a silence of at least 50 ms
   - `onset-snap`: snap to the nearest spectral-flux onset
   - `fricative`: move back to the start of s/sh/ch/f/th noise

   Manual `FIX` entries override these. A word's end is the next word's start when the vocal is legato. Otherwise it is the point where the level drops 15 dB below the word's level for at least 60 ms.
8. **Monotonic cleanup:** Starts are forced to increase by at least 20 ms, and overlapping ends are trimmed.
9. **Whisper cross-check:** `map_whisper()` uses `SequenceMatcher` on normalized tokens (`norm()`). Matches are rejected if they are more than 1.5 s off in time.
10. **Confidence:** `confidence()` combines alternate-model agreement, CTC posterior, and Whisper agreement. Manual fixes carry their own confidence.
11. **Output:** Debug data goes to `align_debug.json`. The final file is written to `data/lyrics.json`. With `--plots`, `make_plots()` writes per-line QA images.

## Syllable timings

Each word is split into units with `pron()`. Acronyms and odd words use phonetic spellings, such as spelled letters or compound parts. Each unit's start comes from `refine()`. Each unit's end is the next unit's start, and the last unit ends at the word's end. A `syl` field is emitted only when a word has more than one unit.

## Output JSON schema

```
{
  "lines": [
    {
      "i": int, "text": str, "start": float, "end": float,
      "words": [
        { "w": str, "start": float, "end": float, "conf": float,
          "syl": [[start, end], ...]   // only if multi-unit
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "extras": [ { "start": float, "end": float, "desc": str } ],
  "notes": str
}
```

- Word times are in seconds, rounded to 3 decimals. `conf` is rounded to 2 decimals.
- `extras` lists unlisted vocal activity of at least 0.5 s that no word covers, plus the hand-written `EXTRA_DESC` entries.

{

  "prompt": "Summarize the style and code guide Opus wrote for its subagents: the aesthetic rules, the p5.brush conventions, the scene/chapter API (function signatures, how time is passed, how transitions are done), and the render pipeline conventions. Quote the API parts verbatim."
}
result
## Summary of the Animation Guide

**Project and direction:** The project renders a 156.6 s music video as painted watercolor animation with p5.brush. The user wants cute, cartoony, colorful, lively shots with something happening in every shot.

**Aesthetic rules:**
- **Look:** Picture-book watercolor and ink. Characters get flat color with ink outlines (stroke weight about 0.8 to 1.6). Backgrounds are soft watercolor fills with little or no outline.
- **Color:** Each chapter has its own palette in STORYBOARD.md. Colors should be saturated but soft, with clear contrast between characters and backgrounds.
- **Motion:** Everything moves. Characters bounce on the beat, hits land on beats, and the guide asks for squash and stretch and overshoot.
- **Readability:** Each shot needs one clear focal action and a strong silhouette. Shots run 1.4 to 4 s.
- **Layout:** The karaoke bar covers the bottom band (about y 975 to 1070) whenever a lyric shows, so keep faces and key action above about y 960.

**p5.brush painting API (core.js):**
- `paint(pts, o)` paints one shape from a point list.
- The `wash` option gives flat color for characters. The `fill` option gives watercolor fills with bleed, texture, and border for backgrounds and light.
- `ink: null` means no outline.
- Helpers include `inkLine(pts, sw, colour, brush, curvature)` for strokes, plus geometry helpers such as `rectPts`, `ellPts`, and `rrPts`.
- Palette: `PAL` plus `mixCol(a, b, k)`. The guide says to avoid pure black and white.

**Chapter and shot API:**
- Each chapter is one IIFE file in `src/ch/`. Helpers stay private inside it.
- `chapter(name, start, end, shots)` registers the chapter.
- A shot is called as `fn(t, lt, dur)`, where `t` is song time, `lt` is time since shot start, and `dur` is shot length. The shot "must paint the entire frame, background included."
- Cuts land on each shot's start time. The timeline adds karaoke, brush-wipe chapter breaks (at 1.5, 38.5, 73.0, and 109.4 s), and a P(doom) meter during chorus windows.
- Shots must be pure functions of `t`. Frames render in parallel and out of order, so there is no carried state and no `Math.random()`. Use `hash(i)` for per-object randomness and `jit(a)` for boiling linework.
- Camera: `camBegin(cx, cy, zoom, rot)` and `camEnd()` handle pushes, pans, and whips, with one level allowed. `shakeXY(t, amount)` adds shake.
- Full-frame effects: `flash`, `iris`, and `irisShape`.

**Timing:** `bpOf(t)` gives beat position at 88 BPM (beat 0.682 s, bar 2.73 s). Beats fall at `0.21 + n × 0.682` s. Helpers include `pulse`, `seg`, `kf`, and the easing functions.

**Characters and props:**
- `clawd(x, y, u, o)` is the main character. `dancer()` adds beat-synced moves, and `mood()` handles smooth face changes.
- `researcher(x, y, s, o)` is the singing human, with `researcherDancer()` for dancing.
- Props in props.js include `stageBack`, `stageFront`, `meterProp`, and `pumpProp`.
- Guest monsters exported on `CAST` are reused in the finale.

**Render pipeline:**
- Only edit your own chapter file. If a shared helper is missing, write a private one. If you find a bug in a shared file, report it instead of editing it.
- Preview with contact sheets (`node render.mjs --sheet=... --cols=3 --w=640 --out=...`) or full stills (`--stills=...`).
- Check first and last frames, frames in between, motion across consecutive times, chapter transitions, and that nothing important sits under the karaoke band.
- Performance target is about 2.5 s per frame, with a ceiling near 4 s. Hundreds of fills are fine, but thousands are not, so prefer fewer, larger shapes.

## Song Craft Analysis

**Structure**
- 11 sections: Verse, Pre-Chorus, and Chorus repeated in three rounds, then an Outro and a Final Chorus.
- About 45 lines total. Verses have 4 lines, Pre-Choruses have 1, and Choruses, Outro, and Final Chorus have 6 each.
- Lines run roughly 6 to 11 syllables. Verse lines are around 9 to 11, Pre-Choruses about 8 to 10, and Chorus openers about 6. The Chorus openers are the shortest and most rhythmically fixed lines.

**Rhyme scheme**
- Verses use AABB couplets, usually end rhymes.
- Pre-Choruses are single lines with no rhyme partner, which sets them apart as a break before each Chorus.
- Choruses rely on end rhymes and a repeated sound around the refrain word, plus internal rhymes.
- Multisyllabic and forced rhymes appear in the later sections. Some rhymes depend on an unusual pronunciation, such as the Lisp "cdr" rhymed with "are." The author notes this was a deliberate choice, so the rhyme is strained rather than natural.

**Referents by section** (the page annotates each one)
- **Verse 1:** the "Sparks of AGI" paper, mechanistic interpretability circuits, the training-loss drop, and the reversal of servant and boss.
- **Pre-Chorus 1:** ChatGPT.
- **Chorus 1:** P(doom), FOOM (the Hanson–Yudkowsky debate), the Chinese room, shrooms, the shoggoth meme for RLHF, and shinigami eyes (Death Note).
- **Verse 2:** a stable training run, the singularity, recursive optimization, and atomic rearrangement (Nanosystems).
- **Pre-Chorus 2:** Sydney (Bing).
- **Chorus 2:** the basilisk and the rationalist mugging, NVDA stock, the Omega Point (Orion's Arm), and a compute figure (around 10^30 FLOPs) tied to safety thresholds.
- **Verse 3:** the MLP, von Neumann architecture, the sharp left turn, and Lisp's cdr.
- **Pre-Chorus 3:** Gato (DeepMind's generalist agent).
- **Chorus 3:** paperclips and the squiggle maximizer, killswitch engineers, and the orthogonality thesis.
- **Outro:** transformers, the stochastic parrot idea, Chinchilla scaling, GPU clusters, and RLHF.
- **Final Chorus:** Loom (cyborgism), masked pre-training, recursive self-improvement, Ilya Sutskever and the OpenAI board events, and the "not consistently candid" critique.

**The chorus and hook**
- The Chorus opens with the same P(doom) line in every round, including the Final Chorus. This is the main hook.
- The page does not document a literal escalating number. The refrain's escalation is implied by the verb "upping." The only numeric escalations are the compute figures, the FLOP count and the GPU count.
- Each Chorus is built on a fixed opener, then about five lines that each stack one or two references. The result is a call-and-response pattern between the hook and the detail.

**Why the lyrics are dense**
- Most lines carry a technical reference, a pun, or a joke, often more than one.
- Jargon is compressed into pop meter. Several lines can be read as either literal or ironic.
- Earlier images return later, such as the training run and the training loss. Some lines also reverse the earlier framing.
- Forced rhymes and deliberate pronunciation choices add another layer.

**How the interpretation page is organized**
- It is organized by song order. Each lyric line appears as a quoted block, followed by notes and links.
- Not every line gets an annotation, but most of the substantive ones do.
- Notes include sources, background, and author commentary. There are also sections on drafting history, failed generations, and later rewrites.
- Related pages, a version history, and see-also links appear at the end.

**Credits**
- **Page author (osmarks):** wrote the annotations and the first-person notes. The see-also section links to osmarks.net.
- **MusicPerson:** wrote the opening verse and the first pre-chorus.
- **EleutherAI Discord:** discussed the early sections.
- **RossM (e/doom):** suggested "boom."
- **Dr TheKekIsALie MDMA:** wrote "That was safe enough, we reckoned."
- **Claude:** wrote several later lines, including the Outro and parts of the Final Chorus. The page says Claude's version was more successful and that Claude's suggestions were usually for formatting.
- **Other attempts:** LLaMA-3.1-405B and Loom produced little usable material.
- **wave | everybody fan club:** made the later Suno version.

**Udio generation details**
- Udio produces about 30-second chunks, so sections were split across tracks.
- The Udio lyrics are formatted slightly differently from the canonical lyrics to improve output.
- The page lists several failed Udio generations and says later work was mostly formatting and regeneration.
- The author could no longer play some saved tracks, so the final version is uncertain.
- Other releases include a YouTube upload, an endorsed music video, a "Claude-Pop" variant from a Suno alternate, and a Claude animation.

You are building a procedural audio synthesizer for a music project. Work in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/synth/ (create it). The repo root /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop is a git repo; commit your work as you reach testable states (normal commits, no amending or rebasing, end commit messages with the line Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>). Follow the user's global rules: never cd; run everything with absolute paths from the repo root; run slow things in the background.

The song

"It's 2am and I'm Crying" is a club track sung from the point of view of a one-year-old baby. The hook lines, transcribed from the baby's parent, are:

It's 2am and I'm crying
It's 3am and I'm crying
It's 11am and I'm napping

The genre is "untz untz untz": four-on-the-floor Eurodance / big-room house, 128 BPM, 4/4, a sidechain-pumping supersaw pad, offbeat open hi-hats, a clap on 2 and 4, a sub bass that locks to the kick, a bright supersaw hook lead, white-noise risers and reverse-cymbal swells into each drop, and a cheeky pitched-down "untz" vocal-like kick texture. Think 2009-2012 Eurodance (Cascada, Basshunter) collided with hyperpop brightness. The key is A minor (relative to a hopeful C major lift in the final chorus is a nice option). The lyric mood is deadpan: a baby stating facts about its night at full club intensity.

One signature idea to try: the hook "vocal" in this instrumental demo is a formant-synthesized baby cry, a saw/pulse oscillator with vibrato through 3 to 4 resonant bandpass filters sweeping between vowel formants (the "waaaah" vowel is roughly /a/ to /ɛ/, F1 around 700 to 900 Hz, F2 around 1200 to 1800 Hz for an infant, with a high fundamental around 400 to 500 Hz for a real cry; for a melodic lead you can transpose the fundamental to the melody notes and keep the formants). Make it sit as a lead instrument playing the hook melody, not as a literal recording. If it sounds bad after a few iterations, fall back to a plain supersaw lead and note why.

Hook melody scansion

"it's-TWO-a-M-and-I'm-CRY-ing": 8 syllables. Suggested placement in one 4/4 bar at 128 BPM with "it's" as a pickup on the "and" of 4 of the previous bar: TWO on beat 1, a-M on the "and" of 1 and beat 2, and-I'm on the "and" of 2 and beat 3, CRY on beat 4 (held), -ing on the "and" of 4. The three hook lines cycle over a four-bar phrase with the fourth bar either a rest or a fill. "e-LEV-en-a-M-and-I'm-NAP-ping" has two more syllables, so it compresses into sixteenths at the start of its bar; that rhythmic stumble is part of the joke. Compose a simple, singable minor-pentatonic-leaning melody for this and write it down in the spec.

Deliverables

  1. A pyproject.toml managed by uv (Python 3.12 or newer; numpy, scipy, soundfile; optionally matplotlib for spectrograms). No other heavy deps. Run with uv run --project /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/synth ....
  2. song.py (or a small package): a declarative song spec (sections with bar counts, chord progression per section, drum patterns as step strings, melody as note/duration lists) plus a renderer that turns the spec into a stereo 44.1 kHz 24-bit WAV. Target structure around 2:45 to 3:15: intro (4 bars, filtered, hats only) → verse 1 (16 bars, kick + bass + sparse pad) → pre-chorus / build (8 bars, riser, snare roll) → chorus/drop (16 bars, full) → verse 2 (16) → build (8) → chorus (16) → bridge "11am and I'm napping" (8 bars, half-time feel, music-box / celesta lullaby voicing of the hook, filtered, no kick; then a riser) → final chorus (16, add a top octave, maybe the C-major lift) → outro (4 to 8 bars, drums drop out, pad tail). Every section boundary must fall on a bar line.
  3. A sidechain compressor keyed from the kick (classic pumping), a simple reverb (feedback delay network or convolution with a synthetic impulse response), a master limiter so peaks sit at -1 dBTP and integrated loudness lands around -9 to -11 LUFS (implement a basic K-weighted loudness measurement; exactness is not needed).
  4. Tight iteration loop: write analyze.py that prints for a rendered WAV: duration, peak dBFS, approximate integrated LUFS, crest factor, per-band energy (sub <60 Hz, bass 60-250, low-mid 250-2k, high-mid 2k-6k, air >6k) in dB relative to full-scale, a clipping count, and saves a spectrogram PNG. Then iterate: render → analyze → look at the spectrogram PNG with the Read tool → adjust the spec or synth → repeat. Do at least 5 full iterations and log each one in ITERATIONS.md (what you changed, what the numbers said, what you heard in the spectrogram). Render time for the full song should stay under about 60 seconds; vectorize with numpy, no per-sample Python loops except inside small filters where unavoidable (use scipy.signal.lfilter).
  5. song.json written alongside the WAV: bpm, bar length in seconds, the list of sections with start/end seconds and bar counts, the beat grid (list of all beat times), downbeats, and the hook melody note events with onset times. A video renderer will read this to sync visuals, so it must match the audio exactly.
  6. Also render 10-second previews of the chorus and the bridge as separate WAVs so a human can audition quickly.
  7. A README.md with run commands and a short description of the signal chain.

Put rendered audio in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/synth/out/ (gitignored by the repo's *.wav rule; commit the code, spec, JSON, PNGs and ITERATIONS.md, not the WAVs).

Work independently and finish all deliverables. Report back with: the final analyze.py numbers, the section table from song.json, whether the formant baby-cry lead worked, and the exact commands to re-render and to play the previews (afplay is available on macOS).

cat > /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/LYRICS.md <<'EOF'
# 2AM (And I'm Crying)

Untz-untz club track, sung from the point of view of a one-year-old. The chorus is a
transcription of what the baby's mother said; the verses are the baby's deadpan account
of the night, packed with parent-internet jargon. 128 BPM, A minor, four on the floor.

Escalation device (the "p(doom) number" of this song): the clock. Each chorus reads the
same three timestamps, but the third line's pronoun moves one notch: *I'm* crying →
*still* crying → *you're* crying → *we're* crying → *good morning*. The 11am line is
always the punchline and always lands on a beat drop.

Bracketed notes like `[brand]` mark things to swap for whatever's actually in the nursery.

---

## Canonical lyrics (v1)

**[Intro]** *(spoken, flat, a group-chat notification read aloud; white noise; the beat fades in)*
> Baby asleep. Seven forty-five.
> *(untz. untz. untz. untz.)*

**[Verse 1]**
> Seven-thirty: bath, then book, then toothpaste on the brush,
> Hatch to red, white noise to "shower," one extremely slow shush.
> You tiptoe out the door like you're cracking a vault.
> I've got object permanence now. That's Piaget's fault.
> "Drowsy but awake," they say. A myth. A hoax. A fake.
> No one's seen it in the wild. I'm choosing one: awake.
> Night-vision on the Nanit, little meerkat in the crib,
> Greyscale eyes in close-up. Here's my 2am ad-lib:

**[Pre-Chorus]** *(beat thins to kick + riser; each clause a half-bar)*
> I dropped the paci through the slats. It's under the crib. I can see it.
> I can't reach it. You can reach it. Here's how I reach you:

**[Chorus]**
> It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 4am and I'm... still crying
> It's 11am and I'm napping

**[Post-Chorus]** *(the shush as hi-hat)*
> *(untz untz untz untz) (shh shh shh shh)*
> *(untz untz untz untz) (shh shh shh shh)*

**[Verse 2]**
> Four a.m., you Google "is this normal" with the brightness low.
> Every tab says "normal." None of them say when it'll go.
> You whisper "teeth?" I've got eight and they're fine.
> "Gas?" I burped at nine. "A leap?" That's a horoscope with a timeline.
> Ferber says to check at three, then five, then ten. You lasted one.
> The chair method: you sat. I stood. We stared. Neither of us won.
> You bounce me down the hallway, hundred-twenty-eight BPM.
> That's where I got the beat. The untz is you. I'm just the stem.

**[Pre-Chorus]**
> The monitor's on your nightstand. Volume: max. You hear everything.
> You hear everything. Here's how I reach you:

**[Chorus]**
> It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 4am and you're crying
> It's 11am and I'm napping

**[Bridge]** *(half-time; kick out; music box / celesta plays the hook; the club beat continues muffled, as if through a wall)*
> It's 11am and I'm napping.
> Hippocampus humming. I'm consolidating:
> the stairs, the word for "dog," your face at four.
> If I twitch, that's my brain, learning where my hands are.
> The group chat gets its post: "Baby asleep, 10:45."
> And you? You could sleep. You're doing dishes.
> "Sleep when the baby sleeps." You chose dishes.
> I'll be up at twelve-ten. I will be perfect.
> And tonight we do it all again:

**[Final Chorus]** *(full drop, top octave, maybe the C-major lift)*
> It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
> It's 4am and we're crying
> It's 5:40 and... good morning!
> It's 11am and I'm napping

**[Outro]** *(beat cuts to white noise; spoken, flat)*
> Baby awake. Eleven fifty-two.
> *(untz.)*

---

## Reference key (what each line is doing)

| Line | Reference |
|---|---|
| bath, book, toothpaste | the "bath, book, bed" routine; brushing with toothpaste is a house rule |
| Hatch to red / "shower" | Hatch sound machine, red = sleep; white noise "as loud as a shower" (Karp) |
| slow shush | the "S" of the 5 S's (Happiest Baby on the Block) |
| object permanence / Piaget | emerges ~8 months; the baby knows you're behind the door |
| drowsy but awake | the most-repeated and least-observed piece of sleep advice |
| Nanit / meerkat | infrared baby-cam; the standing-baby-staring-at-camera meme |
| paci through the slats | pacifier re-insertion, the canonical 2am wake |
| "is this normal" | yes; the internet never says until when |
| eight teeth | typical count around 12-13 months (verify against your kid) |
| horoscope with a timeline | The Wonder Weeks "leaps" have not replicated |
| three, five, ten | Ferber's graduated check-in intervals, night 1 |
| chair method | sit in a chair, move it further out each night |
| 128 BPM | parents bounce at roughly dance tempo; the song's tempo is the bounce |
| stem | audio stem; the baby is the vocal stem of the household mix |
| consolidating | naps consolidate memory (Spencer, UMass; Netflix *Babies* "Sleep") |
| twitch / where my hands are | sleep twitches map the sensorimotor system (Blumberg, Iowa) |
| "Baby asleep, 10:45" | the family group chat ritual |
| sleep when the baby sleeps / dishes | the advice nobody can take |
| 5:40 good morning | early morning waking; the cheerful dawn baby |

## Variants to try in Suno

- **v1-hook-only**: strip verses to the chorus + post-chorus + bridge, for a 90-second cut.
- **v1-named**: swap "little meerkat" for the kid's name in the Nanit line, and let the
  outro notification read the real group-chat format.
- **v1-house-verse** (optional 3rd verse, if the song needs more length): grandparents on
  the fourth floor cooking lunch, the rice cooker, My Gym at ten, the nanny shift change,
  "two naps a day, ten-thirty and three." Not written yet; only if Suno runs short.

## Open lyric questions for Jalex

1. "you're crying" in chorus 2: keep? It is the emotional turn of the song, but it puts a
   parent crying on record.
2. Brand names (Hatch, Nanit): keep as in-jokes, swap for your actual gear, or genericize
   ("the red light," "the camera")?
3. "Eight teeth": change to the real count.
EOF

# Suno run pack: 2AM (And I'm Crying)

Custom mode (lyrics supplied). Model v5.5. Each `suno generate` call returns 2 clips and
costs about 70 credits on v5.5 (v4.5-all is the cheap option for exploratory runs).

Lyrics file for the CLI: `suno_lyrics_v1.txt` (section markers only, no prose notes).

## Run A: deadpan Eurodance (primary)

```
suno generate \
  --title "2AM (And I'm Crying)" \
  --model v5.5 \
  --vocal female \
  --tags "eurodance, big room house, 128 bpm, four-on-the-floor, sidechained supersaw pads, offbeat open hi-hats, clap on 2 and 4, pitched-down untz vocal chop, deadpan female pop vocal, clear diction, bright hyperpop sheen, euphoric drop on the chorus, half-time music box bridge, white noise riser, spoken intro and outro, club anthem, 2009 dance pop" \
  --exclude "acoustic, ballad, slow tempo, country, rock guitar, screamo, metal, lo-fi, mumbled vocals, vocal runs, melisma" \
  --style-influence 70 --weirdness 35 \
  --lyrics-file /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v1.txt \
  --wait --download /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/audio/runA
```

## Run B: chipmunk hyperpop (the baby actually sings it)

Same lyrics. Tags swap the vocal: "pitched-up childlike female vocal, hyperpop, chipmunk
formant, glitchy vocal chops, 128 bpm eurodance". Weirdness 55.

```
suno generate \
  --title "2AM (And I'm Crying) [hyper]" \
  --model v5.5 \
  --vocal female \
  --tags "hyperpop eurodance, 128 bpm, four-on-the-floor, pitched-up childlike vocal, formant-shifted lead vocal, glitchy vocal chops, sidechained supersaw, offbeat hats, euphoric drop, half-time music box bridge, spoken intro and outro" \
  --exclude "acoustic, ballad, slow tempo, country, rock guitar, metal, lo-fi, mumbled vocals" \
  --style-influence 60 --weirdness 55 \
  --lyrics-file /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v1.txt \
  --wait --download /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/audio/runB
```

## Run C: the absurd one (bass-baritone baby)

Same lyrics, `--vocal male`, tags "deep deadpan baritone, eurodance, 128 bpm, ...". One run
only; it's a gag, but a gag that might win.

## What to listen for when picking

- The chorus pronoun shift must be audible: I'm / still / you're / we're / good morning.
- The 11am line should land after a drop or a stop; if Suno buries it, add `[Drop]` or a
  blank line before it in the lyrics file.
- The bridge must actually go half-time and quiet. If it doesn't, move the `[Bridge]` tag
  to `[Bridge - half-time, music box, soft]`.
- The spoken intro/outro should be spoken, not sung. If sung, prefix with `[Spoken]`.

## After a keeper

1. `suno timed-lyrics <clip_id> --lrc > lyrics.lrc` for a coarse line-level sync.
2. Run the `shared/align` pipeline for word-level timings (Demucs + CTC forced alignment,
   cross-checked with mlx-whisper), then the renderer reads `data/lyrics.json`.
EOF

cat > /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/TREATMENT.md <<'EOF'
# Treatment: 2AM (And I'm Crying)

## Concept

The whole video is the baby monitor. We watch the night through the nursery camera:
infrared greyscale, a timestamp in the corner, a baby who knows exactly what it is doing.
The clock is this song's "p(doom) number": it sits in the HUD all night and, on each
chorus line, it leaves its corner and slams full-screen to the next time (2:00, 3:00,
4:00, 5:40, 11:00). The club is not a metaphor the baby reaches for; it is the nursery
rendered honestly. Crib slats strobe like laser bars, the mobile is a disco ball, the
white-noise machine is a speaker stack, the Hatch night-light is the red strobe, and the
parents' bounce in the hallway is the kick drum.

Tone: deadpan. The baby never mugs. Jokes land because the camera is calm and the
typography is confident. Funny like a safety form, not like a cartoon.

## Style bible

- **Palettes.** Night: near-black (#0b0b0e), IR greyscale (#c9ccd1 highlights, #5a5e66 mids),
  one red accent (#ff2a2a, the Hatch), a rare green (#39ff7a) for "LIVE" / monitor UI.
  Day (bridge only): inverted; cream paper (#f4efe6), warm grey ink (#3a3733), sunlight
  amber (#f5b14a) through blinds. The day/night inversion is the structural beat of the edit.
- **Type.** Hook slams: a heavy grotesque (Archivo Black or Inter 900). HUD, notifications,
  tabs, timers: a mono (IBM Plex Mono / JetBrains Mono). Bridge: a soft rounded sans
  (Nunito or Quicksand). Lyric karaoke band at the bottom, per-word highlight, title-safe.
- **Baby.** A procedurally drawn character: round head, two IR-glowing eyes, a sleep sack
  (a soft trapezoid), stubby arms. Eight to twelve strokes. Readable as a silhouette.
  Never cute-ified beyond that; the deadpan depends on it.
- **Motion.** Everything moves on the grid. Cuts on downbeats. Strobes and slams on kicks.
  The shush is the hi-hat: every offbeat gets a small "shh" particle. Strong eases,
  overshoot on slams. No handheld wobble except the parent's bounce.
- **HUD.** Top-left: `NURSERY CAM  •  02:00 AM`. Top-right: `● LIVE` in green during
  choruses. Bottom-left: a thin "sleep debt" bar that fills across the song and empties
  during the bridge. The HUD never overlaps the karaoke band.
- **Bans.** No stock-photo realism, no neon cyberpunk, no emoji-style faces, no actual
  photos of anyone.

## Plates

Each plate is anchored to lyric lines by content, never by hard-coded seconds. Windows
snap to the beat grid.

| id | anchor | treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `notif` | Intro | Black. A phone notification card slides in: group-chat name, "Baby asleep. 7:45." The card's thumbnail zooms until it *is* the monitor feed; the HUD boots. The beat fades in with the zoom. |
| `routine` | V1 L1-2 | Three icons stamp on consecutive beats: tub, book, toothbrush (toothpaste squeezed on the beat). The Hatch cycles to red. The white noise is drawn as a grain field whose density tracks the hats. "one extremely slow shush": a single "shhhhhh" stretched across the bar, letters spacing out. |
| `vault` | V1 L3-4 | The nursery door drawn as a bank-vault wheel. A parent silhouette tiptoes out, foot by foot, on the beats. Cut to the baby's eyes opening in IR. An x-ray outline of the parent appears through the closed door with a label: *object permanence (Piaget, ~8 mo)*. |
| `venn` | V1 L5-6 | Two circles, DROWSY and AWAKE. The intersection label reads `n = 0`. On "awake" the AWAKE circle floods the frame. |
| `meerkat` | V1 L7-8 | Full IR monitor look: timestamp, battery, signal bars. The baby rises in the crib in one motion. Zoom into the glowing eyes. "ad-lib:" draws a small microphone icon next to the mouth. |
| `paci` | Pre-chorus | Side cross-section of the crib. The pacifier falls through the slats in slow motion on the first clause, lands under the crib. A dotted sightline from eye to paci: "I can see it." A reach arc that fails: "I can't reach it." A second arc from parent silhouette that succeeds: "You can reach it." Riser builds; "Here's how I reach you:" then hard cut. |
| `hook` (n=1..4) | each chorus | One word per hit, full-frame heavy type. On each timestamp the HUD clock rolls full-screen to the new time with a flip-clock motion, then returns to its corner. Slats strobe as laser bars on the kick; the mobile spins as a disco ball. Escalation by n: (1) plain IR; (2) red Hatch strobe added, "you're" in red; (3) red + green, frame shake, "we're" split across both parents' silhouettes; (4) sunrise amber bleeds in on "5:40", "good morning!" in yellow. The 11am line always does the same thing: hard cut to the day palette, baby asleep, one bar of near-silence, then the drop resumes. |
| `bounce` | Post-chorus | Hallway, long perspective. Parent silhouette bouncing the baby, exactly on the kick. A BPM readout counts up and locks at 128. Each "shh" spawns a hi-hat particle. |
| `tabs` | V2 L1-2 | A phone at 4am, brightness slider at 5%. Tabs multiply across the frame: each one's headline is "Is this normal?" and each answer is "Yes." A final search, "when does it end," returns an empty results page. |
| `theories` | V2 L3-4 | "teeth?" a gum diagram counts to eight. "Gas?" a burp log with one entry: 21:00. "A leap?" a horoscope wheel whose signs are Wonder Weeks "leap" numbers; a paywall modal pops over it. |
| `ferber` | V2 L5-6 | Three timers labeled 3:00, 5:00, 10:00. The parent's timer bails at 1:00. Then the chair method: a chair on floor tiles, one tile further each night; the parent sits, the baby stands; two glowing eyes vs two tired eyes; "Neither of us won." |
| `stem` | V2 L7-8 | The bounce as a sine wave over the hallway; the wave's period snaps to 128 BPM. Then a DAW track list: KICK, BASS, PAD, HATS, and a track named BABY whose waveform is the vocal. |
| `volume` | Pre-chorus 2 | Nightstand, monitor, volume bar sliding to max. The baby's waveform fills the little screen. "You hear everything." |
| `nap` | Bridge | Inversion to the day palette. Sunlight through blinds, slow. The baby asleep. A filing cabinet labeled HIPPOCAMPUS files cards: "stairs," "dog," "your face at 4." A twitch: a small spark on a hand, and a dotted line to a body map lighting the matching region (*sensorimotor mapping*). Notification card: "Baby asleep, 10:45." Cut to a sink of dishes; the parent's hands; the club beat is a tiny pulsing dot heard through the wall. "I will be perfect." The riser returns the night palette. |
| `outro` | Outro | Notification card: "Baby awake. 11:52." Black. One single-frame white strobe on the last "untz." |

## Technical notes

- Deterministic: every frame is a pure function of song time. No `Math.random()`; use a
  seeded hash per object.
- Inputs: `data/lyrics.json` (word-level timings, the schema from mexicat/pdoom-video:
  lines → words → {w, start, end, conf, syl}) and `data/audio.json` (bpm, beats,
  downbeats, sections, kick onsets). Until the Suno vocal exists, both are mocked from
  the synth demo's `song.json` and the lyric sheet.
- Output: 1920x1080 at 60 fps for finals; 960x540 at 30 fps for drafts and contact sheets.
- Headless Chrome paints frames; ffmpeg encodes (libx264, CRF 16, AAC).
EOF

description Opus: build 2am-crying video renderer
subagent_type general-purpose
model opus
prompt

You are building the code-rendered music video for "2AM (And I'm Crying)", a club track sung from the point of view of a one-year-old baby. This is in the lineage of the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" videos made with Claude in Claude Code: every frame is a deterministic function of song time, painted in a browser, exported through headless Chrome and ffmpeg, with per-word karaoke typography.

Read these first (all in the repo /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop, a git repo):

  • songs/2am-crying/TREATMENT.md: the concept, style bible, and the plate-by-plate treatment. This is your brief for what to draw. Follow it; where it is silent, make choices in its spirit (deadpan, grid-locked, IR-greyscale nursery camera, the clock as the escalating HUD number).
  • songs/2am-crying/LYRICS.md and songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v1.txt: the lyrics and section structure.
  • README.md and .gitignore at the repo root.

Rules from the user's global config: never cd; run everything with absolute paths from the repo root; run slow commands (renders, installs) in the background and keep working; commit eagerly as normal commits whenever things reach a testable state (no amend/rebase/squash); end commit messages with the line Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not touch songs/2am-crying/synth/ (another agent owns it) or songs/baby-facts/ (another agent owns it). Do not commit audio or video files (the .gitignore handles *.wav *.mp3 *.mp4 and renders/ frames/).

Environment

  • macOS, Apple Silicon. Node 24.2, npm 11, ffmpeg 8.0 with libx264, Google Chrome at /Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome. uv and Python 3.14 exist if you need a small Python tool. No bun. Check whether npx playwright or puppeteer-core is the easier way to drive the installed Chrome; prefer puppeteer-core pointed at the system Chrome so nothing downloads a browser.
  • You can look at PNGs with the Read tool. Use that for visual iteration: render contact sheets, look at them, fix, repeat.

Architecture

  • shared/renderer/: the reusable engine, song-agnostic. A timeline (scene windows anchored to lyric lines, snapped to the beat grid), a karaoke band (per-word highlight, title-safe, reads lyrics.json), HUD helpers, easing/beat utilities (beatPos(t), pulse, seg, seeded hash(i)), a palette/theme mechanism, loaders for data/lyrics.json and data/audio.json, the preview page (open index.html?t=23 to scrub to a time, with play/pause against the audio file), and scripts/render.mjs (paint frames in headless Chrome, pipe PNGs or raw RGBA to ffmpeg, encode with libx264 CRF 16 + AAC from the song file; also --sheet contact sheets and --stills t1,t2,...). Frames must be renderable in parallel and out of order, so scenes carry no state between frames.
  • songs/2am-crying/video/: song-specific: palette, the baby character, props (crib, slats, mobile, Hatch light, phone notification card, monitor UI), one module per plate under scenes/, and timeline.js (the edit: which plate covers which lyric lines, with escalation params like hook n=1..4).
  • Canvas 2D is fine and probably best for this look (IR greyscale, heavy type, line art). Use three.js only if you really want it. Fonts: load from Google Fonts in the preview page but make the renderer wait for document.fonts.ready; Archivo Black or Inter 900 for slams, IBM Plex Mono for HUD/notifications, Nunito for the bridge.

Data

Two JSON inputs, same schemas as mexicat/pdoom-video so the alignment pipeline another agent is building drops in later:

data/lyrics.json:

{ "lines": [ { "i": int, "text": str, "start": float, "end": float,
               "words": [ { "w": str, "start": float, "end": float, "conf": float,
                            "syl": [[start,end],...]  // optional } ] } ],
  "extras": [ { "start": float, "end": float, "desc": str } ], "notes": str }

data/audio.json: { "bpm": float, "beats": [float], "downbeats": [float], "sections": [ { "name": str, "start": float, "end": float } ], "kicks": [float], "duration": float } (add fields if you need them; document them).

There is no vocal recording yet. Write songs/2am-crying/video/tools/mock_timing.mjs that generates both files from: bpm 128, a section plan (intro 4 bars, verse1 16, pre1 4, chorus1 8, post1 4, verse2 16, pre2 4, chorus2 8, bridge 16 at half-time feel but same bar length, final chorus 10, outro 4; adjust to taste but every boundary on a bar line), and the lyric sheet, distributing each section's lines across its bars and each line's words evenly across the line's span (leave the last 10 percent of each line silent). Spoken intro/outro lines get their own spans. If songs/2am-crying/synth/out/song.json exists when you run (another agent is rendering the synth demo and writes bpm, section start/end seconds, a beat grid and hook melody onsets there), prefer its sections and beat grid over the plan; print which source you used. Keep the mock tool so timings can be regenerated when the real alignment lands.

Audio for previews and the draft render: use songs/2am-crying/synth/out/*.wav if present (pick the full-song file, not the 10-second previews). If absent when you need it, generate a 128 BPM click + kick track with ffmpeg (aevalsrc/sine filters) of the planned length so the render pipeline is testable end to end, and note it in the README.

Deliverables, in order

  1. Engine + preview page working with the mock data and a placeholder scene that shows the HUD clock, the karaoke band, and beat flashes. Commit.
  2. scripts/render.mjs producing a 10-second 960x540 30 fps MP4 and a contact sheet. Commit.
  3. Plates, in this priority: hook (all four escalations, including the 11am hard cut to the day palette with the bar of near-silence), notif, meerkat, paci, nap, outro, bounce, then the rest. Every plate listed in TREATMENT.md must exist by the end; ones you don't have time to do properly get a deliberate minimal version (the HUD, the karaoke band, the IR nursery background and one simple motif) rather than an empty title card. Commit after every two or three plates.
  4. A full-length 960x540 30 fps draft render over the synth audio (or click track) at songs/2am-crying/video/renders/draft-540p.mp4 (gitignored), plus a contact sheet PNG of one frame per plate at songs/2am-crying/video/sheets/plates.png (commit this one; it is how the human reviews your work).
  5. songs/2am-crying/video/README.md: commands for preview, draft render, final 1080p60 render, regenerating mock timing, and a per-plate status table (done / minimal).

Work independently to completion. In your final report give: the plate status table, the paths of the draft MP4 and the plates contact sheet, the render time per frame at 540p, the exact commands, and any treatment points you deliberately changed and why.

input
thread Opus: build lyric alignment pipeline
description Opus: build lyric alignment pipeline
subagent_type general-purpose
model opus
prompt

You are building the audio-analysis pipeline for a music-video project: given a finished song (mp3/wav from Suno) and its lyric sheet, produce word-level lyric timings and a beat/section grid that a browser renderer consumes. Work in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/shared/align/ (create it). The repo root /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop is a git repo. Rules from the user's global config: never cd; run everything with absolute paths from the repo root; run slow commands (model downloads, separation, alignment) in the background and keep working; commit eagerly as normal commits when things reach a testable state (no amend/rebase/squash); end commit messages with Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Do not touch songs/2am-crying/synth/, songs/2am-crying/video/ or songs/baby-facts/ (other agents own them); you may read them. Do not commit audio (the .gitignore covers *.wav *.mp3) and gitignore your weights cache.

Reference design

This mirrors the analysis/ directory of github.com/mexicat/pdoom-video (read its README, analysis/align.py, analysis/pyproject.toml via raw.githubusercontent.com if useful). Their pipeline: decode gaplessly → Demucs htdemucs_ft vocal stem (shift stems -23 ms for LAME encoder delay when the input is mp3) → CTC emissions from torchaudio MMS_FA (and optionally wav2vec2-large-lv60k-960h) at 20 ms frames → one constrained Viterbi forced alignment over all lines with a garbage "star" token between lines to absorb ad-libs → signal-based refinement of word onsets (voice re-entry after ≥50 ms silence, snap to spectral-flux onset, pull fricatives back to the start of their noise) → monotonic cleanup (starts increase by ≥20 ms) → cross-check against mlx-whisper large-v3-turbo word timestamps via difflib SequenceMatcher, rejecting matches >1.5 s off → confidence per word from model agreement, CTC posterior, and Whisper agreement → lyrics.json. Their analyze.py produces audio.json with bpm, beats, downbeats, sections, drum/vocal onsets and loudness envelopes.

Output schemas (must match exactly; the renderer is being built against them)

lyrics.json:

{ "lines": [ { "i": int, "text": str, "start": float, "end": float,
               "words": [ { "w": str, "start": float, "end": float, "conf": float,
                            "syl": [[start,end],...]  // only for multi-syllable words } ] } ],
  "extras": [ { "start": float, "end": float, "desc": str } ],
  "notes": str }

Times in seconds, 3 decimals; conf 2 decimals.

audio.json: { "bpm": float, "beats": [float], "downbeats": [float], "sections": [ { "name": str, "start": float, "end": float } ], "kicks": [float], "vocal_onsets": [float], "loudness": { "hop": float, "rms_db": [float] }, "duration": float }.

Inputs

  • Audio file (mp3 or wav).
  • Lyric sheet in the Suno format: [Section - notes] header lines, lyric lines, parenthesized backing vocals (I'm crying). Parse it: section headers become section names (strip everything after " - "), parentheticals are aligned as words too but flagged "bv": true on the word, blank lines are ignored. Example sheet: /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v1.txt.
  • Optional --sections song.json to take section boundaries from a known structure file instead of detecting them (the synth demo at songs/2am-crying/synth/out/song.json will have bpm, sections with start/end seconds, and a beat grid, when that agent finishes).

Deliverables

  1. pyproject.toml for uv (Python 3.12; pin python with uv python pin 3.12 since the system has 3.14 and torch may not have wheels for it yet). Deps: torch, torchaudio, demucs, mlx-whisper, librosa, soundfile, numpy, scipy, audioread. Add audio-separator only if the karaoke roformer model is easy to install; otherwise skip it and note it. Run everything as uv run --project /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/shared/align python ....
  2. align.py --audio <file> --lyrics <sheet> --out <dir> writing <dir>/lyrics.json plus a debug JSON, with flags --no-demucs (align on the mix), --whisper-only (fast coarse mode: Whisper word timestamps mapped onto the sheet, for quick previews), and --plots (one PNG per line showing the vocal waveform, word boundaries, and Whisper's guesses; these are the QA artifact a human looks at).
  3. analyze.py --audio <file> --out <dir> [--sections song.json] writing audio.json. Beats/downbeats via librosa (beat_track + a downbeat heuristic from bar-level onset strength; if --sections provides a beat grid, use it as the truth and only compute kicks/onsets/loudness). Kicks: onset detection on a <150 Hz band of the drum stem or mix. Sections, when not provided: segment with librosa's structural features (recurrence/laplacian segmentation) snapped to downbeats, named generically s1, s2, ....
  4. common.py for shared paths, sheet parsing, and gapless decoding (ffmpeg via subprocess to 44.1 kHz mono float32 is fine; account for mp3 encoder delay).
  5. Test harness, since no Suno vocal exists yet: tools/make_test_vocal.sh (or .py) that synthesizes the lyric sheet with macOS say (one say -o line_N.aiff per lyric line, then concatenated with known silences so line-level ground truth is exact; pick a clear voice from say -v '?'), then mixes it with a backing track: use the synth demo full-song WAV in songs/2am-crying/synth/out/ if present at test time, else a 128 BPM kick+hat loop generated with ffmpeg aevalsrc. Write the ground-truth line boundaries to JSON. Then tools/eval_alignment.py reporting the mean and 95th-percentile absolute error of line starts versus ground truth for: whisper-only, no-demucs full pipeline, and full pipeline with Demucs. Put results in shared/align/EVAL.md. Target: line-start error under 150 ms mean with Demucs; report whatever you get honestly.
  6. README.md: install, the three commands, runtime and memory notes, cache location and size, and how to run it on a real Suno download later (songs/<song>/audio/<file>.mp3 → songs/<song>/data/).

Model weights go in shared/align/.cache/ (gitignored). Expect a few GB of downloads; start them in the background early. If MMS_FA download or mlx-whisper fails on this machine, fall back to wav2vec2 and/or openai-whisper and say so.

Work independently to completion. In your final report give: the EVAL.md table, exact commands, cache size, per-stage runtime for a 3-minute song, and anything you had to substitute.

description Write and commit the baby-facts concept options
cat > /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/baby-facts/CONCEPT.md <<'EOF'
# Baby-facts song: concept options

Goal: a dense, Hamilton-style fact song about infant science, with the Netflix *Babies*
series (2020) as the spine and the primary literature as the ammunition. The fact sheet
`FACTS.md` (in progress) feeds the lyrics; nothing goes in the song that isn't on that
sheet with a source.

## Option A: "Prior" (the Bayesian baby)

Frame: the baby is not a blank slate. Chorus insists "I came pre-loaded"; verses rattle off
what newborns already know (object physics, number sense, faces, mother's voice) and what
gets tuned by experience (phonemes, taste, microbiome). Clean argument, slightly lecture-y.

## Option B: "Twelve" (one verse per month, one per episode)

Frame: month 1 to month 12, twelve 4-line verses, each anchored to one *Babies* episode.
Great for video (a month counter is the HUD number) and for structure, but the facts don't
sort neatly by month, so some verses would be forced.

## Option C: "Replicate" (recommended)

Frame: the baby is a research subject on a tour of the famous labs. Each verse is a lab
visit (Tronick's still-face, Hamlin's helper-and-hinderer puppet show, Adolph's walkway and
the 17 falls an hour, Kuhl's head-turn booth, Saffran's two-minute syllable stream,
Feldman's oxytocin draws, Lampl's growth-spurt measuring, Spencer's nap lab, Blumberg's
twitch lab, Dominguez-Bello's swabs). The hook is "Will it replicate?", which means three
things at once: cells dividing, the study being reproduced, and the baby daring the
scientists. Built-in jokes: Wonder Weeks and the 30-million-word gap get the "didn't
replicate" treatment; the baby cites sample sizes.

Why C: it gives the renderer one apparatus per scene (like p(doom)'s plates), lets the
lyrics name-drop scientists the way p(doom) name-drops papers, and the hook is a real
pun rather than a slogan.

## Music

Density this high needs rap flow. Two directions to run in Suno:

1. **Patter hip-hop** at 94-98 BPM, boom-bap drums, musical-theatre brass and string
   stabs on the chorus, a gang-vocal hook. The Hamilton register.
2. **Same untz club genre** as 2AM at 128 BPM, verses as rapid half-time rap over the
   four-on-the-floor. Keeps the "clawdpop" sound consistent across both videos.

Run both once the lyrics exist; pick by whether the words are intelligible.

## Status

- [ ] FACTS.md complete (research agent)
- [ ] pick frame (default: C)
- [ ] lyrics v1
- [ ] Suno run pack
- [ ] treatment
EOF

## Setup (one-time)

The CLI is `~/.local/bin/suno` (paperfoot/suno-cli v0.10.1, prebuilt macOS arm64 binary,
SHA-256 verified against the release checksums; the brew tap is untrusted on this machine
and the crate needs rustc 1.89 while brew's rust is 1.87). It talks to Suno's web
endpoints, so it is unofficial and can break when Suno changes things.

Authenticate once, yourself, since it reads the Suno session cookie out of Chrome and
macOS may prompt for keychain access:

```
~/.local/bin/suno auth --login
~/.local/bin/suno doctor
~/.local/bin/suno credits
```

`suno doctor` currently passes everything except `auth_file`.
""")
s=s.replace("suno generate \\\n","~/.local/bin/suno generate \\\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

BashDocument the pipeline in the root README and commit11:27 PM

description Document the pipeline in the root README and commit
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# clawdpop

Suno + Claude Code music videos in the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" lineage (Suno "Claude-Pop"
song → forced-aligned lyrics → every frame a deterministic function of song time, painted
in a browser and exported through headless Chrome and ffmpeg).

## Songs

- `songs/2am-crying/` — "2AM (And I'm Crying)": untz-untz Eurodance from the point of view of
  a one-year-old. `LYRICS.md`, `TREATMENT.md`, `SUNO_RUNS.md`, `synth/` (procedural demo of
  the backing track), `video/` (renderer scenes).
- `songs/baby-facts/` — dense fact-rap about infant science (Netflix *Babies* and the
  literature behind it). `CONCEPT.md`, `FACTS.md`.

## Shared tooling

- `shared/renderer/` — song-agnostic engine: timeline, karaoke band, HUD, headless-Chrome
  frame export, ffmpeg encode.
- `shared/align/` — audio analysis: Demucs vocal stem → CTC forced alignment (torchaudio
  MMS_FA) cross-checked with mlx-whisper → `lyrics.json`; librosa beats/downbeats/sections →
  `audio.json`.

## Pipeline

1. Lyrics first. Dense, every line carrying a reference; a fixed hook that escalates.
2. Scope Suno runs: custom mode, lyrics with section markers, 2 to 3 style-tag variants.
   Driven with the `suno` CLI (`~/.local/bin/suno`, unofficial, costs ~70 credits per v5.5
   call). Auth is a manual one-time `suno auth --login`.
3. Reification with Opus 5.5 agents: procedural synth demo of the track (so the renderer can
   be built before Suno audio exists), renderer engine + plates, alignment pipeline.
4. Align the keeper Suno clip, swap the mock timing for real timing, render 1080p60.

Audio and video outputs are gitignored; code, specs, JSON timing and contact sheets are
committed.
EOF
git add README.md && git commit -qm "README: pipeline and layout

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && echo committed

Yes. The baby-POV song is drafted at songs/2am-crying/LYRICS.md. Here it is in full. The chorus is your wife's lines; the escalation device is the third line's pronoun, which moves one notch each chorus (I'm → still → you're → we're → good morning). The 11am line always lands on a drop.

[Intro] *(spoken, flat, like a group-chat notification read aloud, over white noise)*

Baby asleep. Seven forty-five.
*(untz. untz. untz. untz.)*

[Verse 1]

Seven-thirty: bath, then book, then toothpaste on the brush,
Hatch to red, white noise to "shower," one extremely slow shush.
You tiptoe out the door like a heist in reverse.
I've got object permanence now. That's Piaget's curse.
"Drowsy but awake," they say. A myth. A hoax. A fake.
No one's seen it in the wild. I'm choosing one: awake.
Night-vision on the Nanit, little meerkat in the crib,
Greyscale eyes in close-up. Here's my 2am ad-lib:

[Pre-Chorus] *(beat thins to kick + riser)*

I dropped the paci through the slats. It's under the crib. I can see it.
I can't reach it. You can reach it. Here's how I reach you:

[Chorus]

It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 4am and I'm... still crying
It's 11am and I'm napping

[Post-Chorus] *(the shush as hi-hat)*

*(untz untz untz untz) (shh shh shh shh)*

[Verse 2]

Four a.m., you Google "is this normal" with the brightness low.
Every tab says "normal." None of them say when it'll go.
You whisper "teeth?" I've got eight and they're fine.
"Gas?" I burped at nine. "A leap?" That's a horoscope with a timeline.
Ferber says to check at three, then five, then ten. You lasted one.
The chair method: you sat. I stood. We stared. Neither of us won.
You bounce me down the hallway, hundred-twenty-eight BPM.
That's where I got the beat. The untz is you. I'm just the stem.

[Pre-Chorus]

The monitor's on your nightstand. Volume: max. You hear everything.
You hear everything. Here's how I reach you:

[Chorus]

It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 4am and you're crying
It's 11am and I'm napping

[Bridge] *(half-time, kick out, music box plays the hook; the club beat continues muffled, as if through a wall)*

It's 11am and I'm napping.
Hippocampus humming. I'm consolidating:
the stairs, the word for "dog," your face at four.
If I twitch, that's my brain, learning where my hands are.
The group chat gets its post: "Baby asleep, 10:45."
And you? You could sleep. You're doing dishes.
"Sleep when the baby sleeps." You chose dishes.
I'll be up at twelve-ten. I will be perfect.
And tonight we do it all again:

[Final Chorus] *(full drop, top octave)*

It's 2am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 3am and I'm crying *(I'm crying)*
It's 4am and we're crying
It's 5:40 and... good morning!
It's 11am and I'm napping

[Outro] *(beat cuts to white noise; spoken)*

Baby awake. Eleven fifty-two.
*(untz.)*

Three things I'd like your call on:

  • "You're crying" in chorus 2. It's the emotional turn of the song, but it puts a parent crying on record. Easy to swap for "and I'm still crying" again or "and you're bargaining".
  • Brand names. Hatch and Nanit are in-jokes I guessed at. Swap for whatever's actually in the nursery, or genericize to "the red light" and "the camera".
  • "Eight teeth." Change to the real count.

The file also has a reference key explaining each line's joke, a hook-only 90-second variant, and a named variant that uses the kid's name in the Nanit line. The second song (baby science facts) has a concept doc but no lyrics yet; the research agent compiling the fact sheet is still running.
