cat > songs/baby-facts/LYRICS.md <<'EOF'
# Replicate (n = 1)

Dense fact-rap from the point of view of the baby being studied. The spine is Netflix's
*Babies* (2020): the title card ("15 babies, filmed over one year, 36 world-renowned
scientists") is the chorus, each verse is a tour of the labs in episode order, and the
bridge is the replication crisis. The hook "Will it replicate?" means three things: cells
dividing, the study being reproduced, and the baby daring the scientists. The turn at the
end: the only result that always replicates is the baby.

Every fact is on `FACTS.md` with a source. Verses are 12 lines at ~96 BPM, one line per bar,
musical-theatre hip-hop patter. "this girl" in verse 3 is the narrator; swap for "this kid".

---

**[Intro]** *(spoken, documentary narrator, over a fetal heartbeat; then the beat)*
> Fifteen babies. Filmed over one year. Thirty-six world-renowned scientists.
> And me. I'm the one in the little cap.

**[Verse 1: Love]**
> Day one: skin to skin, and the oxytocin's climbing.
> Feldman swabs the spit of eighty couples, and the timing's
> identical in dads. "Fatherhood is biological."
> Forty-eight gay fathers, amygdala lit: that's data, not anecdotal.
> Tronick, '68: "This emotion stuff is not what you want to do."
> So he froze a mother's face for two minutes and watched me come unglued:
> I smile, I bid, I fuss, I cry, I chew my hands to cope.
> Then she comes back. We repair. That's the study. That's the hope.

**[Chorus]**
> I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one.
> Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done.
> Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten.
> Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
> Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
> Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year.
> Will it replicate? Ask me in a year.

**[Verse 2: Crawling]**
> Barbu-Roth did nuclear physics; now she's hanging me in air.
> Dots stream under me. I swim. "A newborn's an astronaut," I swear.
> "We're still quadrupeds inside." She strapped a skateboard to my chest:
> two days old, I crossed the mattress. Twice. Three times. Then I had a rest.
> Lampl's neighbor's kid: sixty-two point seven, then sixty-four point five.
> "I'm terrible at this," she thought. Nope. That's just how we arrive:
> up to two and a half centimeters overnight, then sixty-three days of flat.
> Ninety-five percent of babyhood is growth-free. Front page. A big name mocked her for that.
> Adolph raised the slope six degrees a go, up to a sheer drop.
> Grant approached it like the shallow ones and went straight off the top.
> Two thousand three hundred sixty-eight steps an hour, seventeen falls, no stall.
> "Crawling isn't mandatory." Bum-shuffle, bear-crawl, whatever gets you down the hall.

**[Verse 3: Words, Sleep]**
> Hirsh-Pasek splits up Cinderella, pauses in the middle of a clause.
> I turn to where it breathes right. Can't talk yet. I know the laws.
> Saffran: pabeecoo, golatoo, two minutes, forty-five reps each.
> Probability one inside a word, point three across: I'm carving speech.
> Jarvis danced six hours a day, then counted who can learn a sound in the world:
> three birds, five mammals. Parrots, bats, elephants, seals, dolphins, songbirds, hummingbirds. This girl.
> Fenton's app: a thousand babies, six million events, logged to the minute:
> one-point-five million sleeps, two-point-five million feeds, the diapers, a million and a half in it.
> Random at one month, a hint by eight, a rhythm by a year. *(He hasn't published it.)*
> Blumberg says my twitch is sonar: one ping, a thousand neurons, mapping where my limbs fit.
> Spencer: hippocampus small, so I file in bouts; the spindles move the day
> from hippocampus to cortex. Two naps and a night. That's not lazy. That's the way.

**[Chorus]**

**[Verse 4: First Steps, then Part Two]** *(double-time on the Part Two lines)*
> Dominici wires my legs at two days old: two muscle patterns, and I step;
> toddlers add two more. Rats, cats, macaques, guineafowl: same ancient rep.
> Cowgill hauled a hundred thirty pounds through fifteen museums, six hundred kids' bones in the stack.
> Reviewer 2 said "children's bones don't respond to exercise." Toddler femurs are wide ovals. Take that back.
> Walle: walkers know more words than crawlers, and they hear the exact same amount.
> It's you: "Du—" "Duck." "Duck!" Three hundred seventy-four words in five minutes. I count.
> Part Two: Hespos hangs a block in midair; I stare twice as long. I know how things fall.
> Kang Lee: six months, I tell two monkeys apart. Nine months, like you, not at all.
> Saxe scans her own son, awake: face patch, place patch, same spots as yours.
> Hamlin's puppet climbs; I reach for the helper. *(Hold that thought. It's back in the bridge, of course.)*
> Carpenter: twelve months, I point to show, not to get. You look. That's the human part.
> Warneken "drops" a cup; eighteen months, I hand it back in ten seconds. Pay me with a toy and I'll stop. Also the human part.

**[Bridge: the part you skip]** *(half-time, sparse, the baby as Reviewer 2)*
> Now the part you skip.
> The Wonder Weeks: ten leaps on a calendar. Tested on four babies by a grad student. Nothing. The man behind it lost his job in '98.
> Mozart effect: thirty-six college students, ten minutes, never once a baby. Georgia spent a hundred and five grand on CDs for newborns.
> Baby Einstein: a month of DVDs, zero new words. Disney refunded fifteen ninety-nine a disc.
> Neonatal imitation: six babies in '77 stuck their tongues out. A hundred and six in 2016 did nothing.
> The helper and the hinderer: *Nature*, 2007. ManyBabies 4: five hundred sixty-seven babies, thirty-seven labs. Forty-nine point three percent. A coin.
> Thirty million words: forty-two families, one hour a month.
> So when you ask me... will it replicate?
> *(beat drops out)*
> Here's what did.
> Me. Brain volume up a hundred and one percent in year one. Twenty-five hundred synapses a neuron, then more, then pruned. Weight tripled. Length up half.
> I'm the replication. I'm the only result that always comes in.

**[Final Chorus]**
> I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one.
> Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done.
> Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten.
> Will it replicate? *(I did.)*
> Will it replicate? *(I did.)*
> Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year.
> Will it replicate? Ask me in a year.

**[Outro]** *(spoken; the beat stops; heartbeat)*
> "Hardest problem in the universe. We should let them sleep."
> n equals one.

---

## Reference key

| Line | Source (see FACTS.md) |
|---|---|
| eighty couples, identical in dads | Gordon et al. 2010; Feldman on air, Ep 1 |
| forty-eight gay fathers, amygdala | Abraham et al. 2014, *PNAS* |
| Tronick '68 quote; two-minute still face | Ep 1 transcript; Tronick et al. 1978 |
| Barbu-Roth: physics, astronaut, dots, skateboard, mattress | Ep 3; Barbu-Roth 2009; Forma 2019 |
| 62.7 → 64.5; bursts to 2.5 cm; 63 days; 90–95% growth-free; front page; mocked | Ep 3; Lampl 1992, *Science* (contested by measurement-error critics) |
| six degrees; Grant; 2,368 steps, 17 falls; crawling isn't mandatory | Ep 3; Adolph 2012 |
| Cinderella pauses | Hirsh-Pasek 1987; Ep 4 |
| pabeecoo, 2 minutes, 45 reps, 1.0 vs 0.33 | Saffran 1996; Ep 4 |
| dancer; three birds, five mammals | Jarvis 2019; Ep 4 |
| six million events; unpublished | Fenton and Wallisch, Ep 5 (explicitly unpublished on air) |
| twitch is sonar | Blumberg, Ep 5; Blumberg 2013 |
| spindles, two naps | Spencer, Ep 5; Kurdziel 2013 |
| two muscle patterns plus two; guineafowl | Dominici 2011, *Science* |
| 130 pounds, 15 museums, 600 children; Reviewer 2; wide ovals | Cowgill, Ep 6; Cowgill 2010 |
| walkers' vocabulary; same words heard; 374 words | Walle and Campos 2014; Ep 6 |
| block in midair, twice as long | Hespos, Ep 7 |
| monkey faces at 6 vs 9 months | Pascalis 2002; Kang Lee, Ep 7 |
| Saxe scans her son | Deen 2017; Ep 7 |
| helper puppet; 49.3% | Hamlin 2007; ManyBabies 4, 2025 |
| pointing to show at 12 months | Carpenter 1998; Liszkowski 2004 |
| cup in ten seconds; toy reward backfires | Warneken and Tomasello 2006, 2008 |
| Wonder Weeks: four babies; job lost 1998 | de Weerth and van Geert 1998 |
| Mozart: 36 students, ~10 min; Georgia $105k | Rauscher 1993; Pietschnig 2010 |
| Baby Einstein: no words; $15.99 refunds | DeLoache 2010; Disney 2009 |
| 6 babies 1977 vs 106 babies 2016 | Meltzoff and Moore 1977; Oostenbroek 2016 |
| 42 families, one hour a month | Hart and Risley 1995; Sperry 2019 |
| brain +101%; 2,500 synapses; weight tripled | Knickmeyer 2008; Huttenlocher 1997 |
| "hardest problem in the universe" | Fenton's closer, Ep 5 |

## Cuts for a shorter edit (~2:45)

Drop verse 4's First Steps half (keep Part Two), and cut the bridge to Wonder Weeks, Mozart,
ManyBabies, then the turn.

# Treatment sketch: Replicate (n = 1)

One plate per lab, in the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" register: plates from an illustrated
methods section. The HUD number is `n = 1` in the corner; during the bridge it flickers
through the real sample sizes (4, 36, 6, 106, 567, 42) and in the final chorus returns to 1.

- Palette: lab-notebook paper, ink, one accent (the orange of a measuring tape). Figures
  drawn as journal figures: axes, error bars, a caption in a serif.
- The baby is the same procedural character as the 2am video, now with an EEG cap.
- Plates: oxytocin curves (Feldman); the still-face three-panel (Tronick); the newborn
  suspended over streaming dots (Barbu-Roth); the growth chart with saltations as steps and
  the 1986 notebook row 59.8 / 59.8 / 59.8 / 60.8 (Lampl); the adjustable slope rising six
  degrees per beat (Adolph); the Cinderella waveform with pauses marked (Hirsh-Pasek); the
  syllable stream with transitional probabilities (Saffran); the vocal-learner phylogeny
  (Jarvis); the six-million-event scatter resolving from noise to rhythm (Fenton); the sonar
  ping body map (Blumberg); spindles moving cards from hippocampus to cortex (Spencer); EMG
  traces, two then four (Dominici); the femur cross-sections, oval to teardrop (Cowgill);
  the LENA word counter (Walle); the floating block (Hespos); monkey faces blurring at nine
  months (Kang Lee); the scanner with a baby in it (Saxe); the puppet hill (Hamlin); the
  pointing finger (Carpenter); the dropped cup (Warneken).
- Bridge: each myth as a journal cover that gets a "RETRACTED" or "n = 4" stamp.
- Turn: a single cell dividing into a brain, the volume counter rolling to +101%.

The second song is drafted: "Replicate (n = 1)", at songs/baby-facts/LYRICS.md. The baby is the research subject touring the labs from the Netflix series in episode order. The chorus is the show's title card. The bridge is the replication crisis, and the turn is that the only result that always replicates is the baby. Every number traces to the fact sheet, which has sources and reliability flags.

[Intro] *(spoken, documentary voice, over a heartbeat)*

Fifteen babies. Filmed over one year. Thirty-six world-renowned scientists.
And me. I'm the one in the little cap.

[Verse 1: Love]

Day one: skin to skin, and the oxytocin's climbing.
Feldman swabs the spit of eighty couples, and the timing's
identical in dads. "Fatherhood is biological."
Forty-eight gay fathers, amygdala lit: that's data, not anecdotal.
Tronick, '68: "This emotion stuff is not what you want to do."
So he froze a mother's face for two minutes and watched me come unglued:
I smile, I bid, I fuss, I cry, I chew my hands to cope.
Then she comes back. We repair. That's the study. That's the hope.

[Chorus]

I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one.
Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done.
Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten.
Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year.
Will it replicate? Ask me in a year.

[Verse 2: Crawling]

Barbu-Roth did nuclear physics; now she's hanging me in air.
Dots stream under me. I swim. "A newborn's an astronaut," I swear.
"We're still quadrupeds inside." She strapped a skateboard to my chest:
two days old, I crossed the mattress. Twice. Three times. Then I had a rest.
Lampl's neighbor's kid: sixty-two point seven, then sixty-four point five.
"I'm terrible at this," she thought. Nope. That's just how we arrive:
up to two and a half centimeters overnight, then sixty-three days of flat.
Ninety-five percent of babyhood is growth-free. Front page. A big name mocked her for that.
Adolph raised the slope six degrees a go, up to a sheer drop.
Grant approached it like the shallow ones and went straight off the top.
Two thousand three hundred sixty-eight steps an hour, seventeen falls, no stall.
"Crawling isn't mandatory." Bum-shuffle, bear-crawl, whatever gets you down the hall.

[Verse 3: Words, Sleep]

Hirsh-Pasek splits up Cinderella, pauses in the middle of a clause.
I turn to where it breathes right. Can't talk yet. I know the laws.
Saffran: pabeecoo, golatoo, two minutes, forty-five reps each.
Probability one inside a word, point three across: I'm carving speech.
Jarvis danced six hours a day, then counted who can learn a sound in the world:
three birds, five mammals. Parrots, bats, elephants, seals, dolphins, songbirds, hummingbirds. This girl.
Fenton's app: a thousand babies, six million events, logged to the minute:
one-point-five million sleeps, two-point-five million feeds, the diapers, a million and a half in it.
Random at one month, a hint by eight, a rhythm by a year. *(He hasn't published it.)*
Blumberg says my twitch is sonar: one ping, a thousand neurons, mapping where my limbs fit.
Spencer: hippocampus small, so I file in bouts; the spindles move the day
from hippocampus to cortex. Two naps and a night. That's not lazy. That's the way.

[Verse 4: First Steps, then Part Two]

Dominici wires my legs at two days old: two muscle patterns, and I step;
toddlers add two more. Rats, cats, macaques, guineafowl: same ancient rep.
Cowgill hauled a hundred thirty pounds through fifteen museums, six hundred kids' bones in the stack.
Reviewer 2 said "children's bones don't respond to exercise." Toddler femurs are wide ovals. Take that back.
Walle: walkers know more words than crawlers, and they hear the exact same amount.
It's you: "Du—" "Duck." "Duck!" Three hundred seventy-four words in five minutes. I count.
Part Two: Hespos hangs a block in midair; I stare twice as long. I know how things fall.
Kang Lee: six months, I tell two monkeys apart. Nine months, like you, not at all.
Saxe scans her own son, awake: face patch, place patch, same spots as yours.
Hamlin's puppet climbs; I reach for the helper. *(Hold that thought. It's back in the bridge, of course.)*
Carpenter: twelve months, I point to show, not to get. You look. That's the human part.
Warneken "drops" a cup; eighteen months, I hand it back in ten seconds. Pay me with a toy and I'll stop. Also the human part.

[Bridge: the part you skip] *(half-time, sparse)*

Now the part you skip.
The Wonder Weeks: ten leaps on a calendar. Tested on four babies by a grad student. Nothing. The man behind it lost his job in '98.
Mozart effect: thirty-six college students, ten minutes, never once a baby. Georgia spent a hundred and five grand on CDs for newborns.
Baby Einstein: a month of DVDs, zero new words. Disney refunded fifteen ninety-nine a disc.
Neonatal imitation: six babies in '77 stuck their tongues out. A hundred and six in 2016 did nothing.
The helper and the hinderer: Nature, 2007. ManyBabies 4: five hundred sixty-seven babies, thirty-seven labs. Forty-nine point three percent. A coin.
Thirty million words: forty-two families, one hour a month.
So when you ask me... will it replicate?
*(beat drops out)*
Here's what did.
Me. Brain volume up a hundred and one percent in year one. Twenty-five hundred synapses a neuron, then more, then pruned. Weight tripled. Length up half.
I'm the replication. I'm the only result that always comes in.

[Final Chorus] *(same, but the echo answers "I did.")*

[Outro] *(spoken)*

"Hardest problem in the universe. We should let them sleep."

Two practical notes. The full song is about 6,100 characters and Suno's custom mode caps at 5,000, so the run file is a cut that drops the Dominici, Walle, Saxe and Carpenter lines and shortens the second chorus; the full version stays in the lyrics file. "This girl" in verse 3 is the narrator and swaps to "this kid" if you want it generic. The run pack has two directions: musical-theatre hip-hop patter at 96 BPM, which is the natural home for this density, and a 128 BPM club version to match the 2am video.

Still running in the background: the synth demo, the selfie-video renderer, and the alignment pipeline.

Where I departed from the plan:

  • Verse 2 is 9 bars, not 8. The lyric sheet has 16 clauses, which fill 8 bars at two per bar, so the "full bar of silence" after "It's 1am and I'm..." becomes a 9th bar. The video tool's own plan also uses 9.
  • Three other changes to match the lyric sheet and the video tool:
    • The final chorus's last bar goes quiet.
    • Intro bar 2 has 4 real kicks under the untz hits.
    • The outro is the spoken-line backing, then the camera click and the same backing, so the outro doesn't repeat the intro's untz bar.
  • Length: 1:47 under the new plan, replacing the original 2:45-3:15 target.
  • Hook rhythm: to keep "it's" on the and-of-4 when lines run back to back, "CRY-ing" is two 16ths (CRY on 4, "-ing" just after). In the final chorus "pooping again" squeezes into 32nds.
  • Melody format: it's written in song.py as syllabified lyrics plus pitch shapes per line type, rather than raw note lists; the exact notes are in the README table and song.json.
  • Spoken lines: the WAV only reserves time for "Hi. It's me. Here's my day."; there is no spoken audio. The camera clicks are rendered.

* main 9f878a3 2am-crying v3: nap tip-over and long take, pooping hold + "again" slam
# Iteration log

Each entry is one full loop: `song.py` render -> `analyze.py` -> read the
spectrogram PNGs -> change the spec/synth. Snapshots of every iteration's
spectrograms are in `out/iterations/<tag>_*.png`. Verdicts about sound are
read off spectrograms and numbers (no listening was possible in this loop);
a human should audition `out/preview_chorus.wav` and `out/preview_bridge.wav`.

Band levels are RMS dBFS per band (0 dB = full-scale square): sub <60,
bass 60-250, low-mid 250-2k, high-mid 2k-6k, air >6k.

## iter0: baseline (first full render)

What: first complete pass of all instruments, sidechain, convolution reverb,
ping-pong delay, soft clip + true-peak limiter with auto-gain.

Numbers: 198.0 s file (195.0 s of music + 3 s tail), render 10.5 s,
-10.03 LUFS, TP -1.20 dBTP, crest 10.0 dB, 0 clipped samples.
Bands: sub -16.7, bass -13.8, low-mid -19.1, high-mid -33.0, air -33.0.
Sections: intro -23.0, verse1 -10.5, build -11.7, chorus -9.4, verse2 -10.2,
bridge -9.9 (!), final -9.3, outro -15.7 LUFS (ungated).
Sync: 320/320 kicks found, median offset 0.20 ms, max 0.25 ms.

Spectrogram: everything below ~120 Hz is saturated for the whole track; the
bass/sub drive the limiter, so mids and highs are pushed down (high-mid and
air ~19 dB under the bass band). Verses are as dense as the drops, so there is
almost no lift into the chorus (1 LU). The bridge has a wall of sub energy
(sustained, un-ducked sub notes) and is as loud as a chorus, which is wrong for a
no-kick lullaby breakdown. Chorus zoom: the formant lead is clearly visible:
the fundamental runs 330-880 Hz with vibrato, scoops and the falling "CRY" wail, and
harmonics 2-3 are boosted where F1/F2 sit. Kick pitch sweeps show as the curved
streaks at every beat. Syllable labels are unreadable (white on yellow).

## iter1: low-end rebalance, sparser verse/bridge, zero-phase master HPF

Changed: bass bus 0.50 -> 0.32, bridge sub 0.45 -> 0.16, bass voice sub/mid
0.85/0.45 -> 0.7/0.55, hats +3 dB, saw leads +3 dB, verse-1 kick -1 dB and pad
-2 dB, bridge pad -3 dB. Master high-pass switched from causal Butterworth to
zero-phase `sosfiltfilt`. Analyzer: readable syllable labels, palette-quantised
PNGs.

The synth demo landed and the repo is tidy (all agent commits are on main; I deleted the stale merged branch). The track is 1:47, 57 bars at 128 BPM, structured exactly to the v3 lyric sheet and built to loop. Its song.json carries every section, beat, kick and per-syllable hook onset, so the renderer can sync against it before any Suno audio exists. The spectrogram shows the intended shape: quieter double-time verses, louder choruses, the bar of silence before the half-time bridge, biggest final chorus, then the loop seam.

The one thing no agent could do is listen. The formant-synthesized "baby cry" lead was judged only from spectrograms, so it's worth 20 seconds of your ears:

The pipeline is built and committed in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/shared/align/. On the test song, line-start error with Demucs is 15–20 ms on average, well under the 150 ms target. That test song is spoken text-to-speech (macOS say), not singing, so a real Suno vocal will do worse.

Results (EVAL.md)

Both test songs are 48 lines, 180 s, made by rendering each lyric line with say and placing it at known times. One is mixed under the synth demo WAV, the other under an ffmpeg kick/hat/pad loop. Line-start error in ms:

configurationsynth backing: mean / median / p95 / maxloop backing: mean / median / p95 / max
whisper-only248 / 169 / 813 / 1513256 / 171 / 821 / 1526
no-demucs91 / 29 / 94 / 191931 / 30 / 68 / 99
full, Demucs only (--no-karaoke)50 / 16 / 34 / 158915 / 11 / 32 / 34
full (default: Demucs + karaoke lead stem)19 / 19 / 39 / 7915 / 11 / 32 / 42
full, mp3 input20 / 21 / 34 / 7916 / 13 / 32 / 34
  • mp3 vs wav: the mp3 input lands within about 1 ms of the wav, so the encoder-delay handling works.
  • Why the karaoke stem is on by default: the synth demo has voice-like parts (a formant "untz" and a synth baby-cry singing the hook) that Demucs keeps in its vocal stem. With Demucs alone, the last line (untz.) locked onto the synth's "untz" 1.6 s late; the karaoke stem fixes that.
  • Whisper-only is a rough preview: line starts come out early because Whisper attaches the silence before a line to its first word.
  • analyze.py: tempo and beats are right on both songs (beat error 0.3–2 ms). Downbeats are 100% right on the synth song. On the loop they were 0%: every bar is identical, so nothing marks beat one.
  • Sections: on the synth song the detected boundaries hit 6 of the 8 real ones exactly, place the two build-ups 4 bars late, and add a few extra splits.
  • --sections: tested with the synth's real song.json and with a small fixture in test/fixtures/.

Commands (from the repo root)

uv sync --project shared/align
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/tools/prefetch_models.py
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/align.py --audio songs/<song>/audio/<file>.mp3 --lyrics songs/<song>/suno_lyrics_v1.txt --out songs/<song>/data --plots
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/align.py --whisper-only --audio ... --lyrics ... --out ...
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/analyze.py --audio songs/<song>/audio/<file>.mp3 --out songs/<song>/data [--sections song.json]
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/tools/make_test_vocal.py [--backing loop --out shared/align/test/vocal_loop]
uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/tools/eval_alignment.py --run --md

align.py also takes --no-demucs, --no-karaoke, --fix fixes.json (manual corrections after looking at the plots) and --pron pron.json (spoken spellings for odd words).

Runtime for a 3-minute song (M4 Max, nothing cached)

stagetime
decode0.2 s
Demucs htdemucs_ft18–21 s
karaoke lead stem63–100 s
CTC emissions~6 s
Viterbi alignment~0.4 s
refinement0.3 s
Whisper5–8 s
plots9–21 s
full align.py, total~110 s (~35 s with --no-karaoke)
--whisper-only, total~6 s
analyze.py~4 s with stems already made (22 s if it runs Demucs itself)
  • Memory: peak about 4 GB.
  • Reruns on the same file take seconds, because stems, model outputs and Whisper results are cached in work/ (about 310 MB per song).

Cache

shared/align/.cache/ is 5.1 GB and gitignored:

  • 2.4 GB: the two alignment models from torch hub (1.2 GB each)
  • 1.8 GB: Whisper large-v3-turbo plus htdemucs_ft, from Hugging Face
  • 0.9 GB: the karaoke model

The .venv adds 1.4 GB.

Substitutions and deviations

  • No fallbacks were needed. MMS_FA, wav2vec2-lv60k, Demucs and mlx-whisper all run on Python 3.12 / torch 2.14 on the GPU.
  • audio-separator installed cleanly (it needs onnxruntime listed explicitly). It is a required dependency now, and the karaoke stem is on by default.
  • Changes from the reference:
    • a small penalty on silence inside a line, so non-words like "untz"/"shh" don't get smeared across the gap before the line
    • guards so word starts can't drift into silence and word ends can't run away
    • a duration cap on the first word of each line in Whisper-only mode
    • unpronounceable tokens (a spaced "—", "...") kept in the output with zero duration
    • accents folded (café → cafe)
    • the reference's hard-coded per-song corrections replaced by the --fix JSON
  • Schema: audio.json has exactly the schema's keys. lyrics.json adds only bv. Sheet section names go in align_debug.json because the schema has no slot for them.
  • Not ported: pitch tracking and the reference's snare/hat lists.
  • Syllables come from spelling rules, not phonetics, so a split can be off by a letter.

Other things to know

  • Commit trailer: you asked for Claude Fable 5.1, but my commits (ba7b606, 3b19440, 60720a8, 787600c) carry Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5, the line my session's attribution settings specify. I can't amend them under the no-history-rewriting rule.
  • Commits: I committed with explicit path lists, so other agents' work on this shared branch wasn't touched. No audio is committed.
  • Renderer: the renderer optionally reads hats and beats_per_bar from audio.json. Neither is in the schema, so it uses its fallbacks.
  • Real Suno files: I haven't verified that Suno mp3s carry the encoder-delay tag that browsers use to trim. The mp3 field in the debug JSON shows it on the first real download.

#!/bin/bash
# Suno batch for 2026-10-17. Budget guard: never spend more than $BUDGET credits in total.
# Free v6-mini passes first (pipeline test + a cheap listen), then v6 on the main directions.
set -u
S=~/.local/bin/suno
ROOT=/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop
LOG=$ROOT/shared/suno/logs/batch-20261017.log
BUDGET=${BUDGET:-830}
START_CREDITS=2500
COST_EST=100   # replaced by the measured cost after the first v6 run

credits_left() { $S credits --json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['total_credits_left'])"; }
log() { echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') $*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

run() {  # run <outdir> <model> <title> <lyrics-file> <tags> <exclude> <style> <weird> [extra flags]
  local out=$1 model=$2 title=$3 lyr=$4 tags=$5 excl=$6 style=$7 weird=$8; shift 8
  mkdir -p "$out"
  if [ "$model" != "v6-mini" ]; then
    local left; left=$(credits_left); local spent=$((START_CREDITS - left))
    if [ $((spent + COST_EST)) -gt "$BUDGET" ]; then log "BUDGET STOP before $out: spent=$spent est=$COST_EST budget=$BUDGET"; return 2; fi
  fi
  local before; before=$(credits_left)
  log "START $out model=$model credits_before=$before"
  local attempt=0 rc=1
  while [ $attempt -lt 3 ]; do
    attempt=$((attempt+1))
    $S generate --json --headless --model "$model" --vocal female --title "$title" \
      --tags "$tags" --exclude "$excl" --style-influence "$style" --weirdness "$weird" \
      --lyrics-file "$lyr" --download "$out" "$@" > "$out/result.json" 2> "$out/stderr.log"
    rc=$?
    if [ $rc -eq 4 ]; then log "rate limited on $out, attempt $attempt; sleeping 90s"; sleep 90; continue; fi
    break
  done
  local after; after=$(credits_left)
  local cost=$((before - after))
  log "DONE $out rc=$rc cost=$cost credits_left=$after files: $(ls "$out" 2>/dev/null | grep -c mp3) mp3"
  if [ "$model" != "v6-mini" ] && [ $cost -gt 0 ]; then COST_EST=$cost; fi
  python3 - "$out/result.json" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null | tee -a "$LOG"
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
except Exception as e:
    print("  (result.json unreadable:", e, ")"); sys.exit()
print("  status:", d.get("status"))
data = d.get("data") or {}
clips = data.get("clips") or data.get("downloads") or []
for c in clips if isinstance(clips, list) else []:
    if isinstance(c, dict):
        print("  clip:", c.get("id", "")[:8], c.get("title", ""), c.get("duration") or c.get("metadata", {}).get("duration", ""), c.get("path") or c.get("file") or c.get("audio_url", "")[:60])
if d.get("status") != "success":
    print("  error:", json.dumps(d.get("error"))[:400])
PY
  return $rc
}

#!/bin/bash
# After picking a Suno clip: word-align it and analyze the beat grid into songs/<song>/data/.
# usage: shared/suno/align_keeper.sh <song-dir-name> <path/to/clip.mp3> <lyrics-sheet.txt> [--sections song.json]
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop
song=$1; mp3=$2; sheet=$3; shift 3

mkdir -p "$out"
echo "== align (Demucs + karaoke stem + CTC + Whisper cross-check) =="
uv run --project $ROOT/shared/align python $ROOT/shared/align/align.py --audio "$mp3" --lyrics "$sheet" --out "$out" --plots
echo "== analyze (beats, downbeats, kicks, sections, loudness) =="
uv run --project $ROOT/shared/align python $ROOT/shared/align/analyze.py --audio "$mp3" --out "$out" "$@"
echo "== done: $out/lyrics.json $out/audio.json (QA plots in $out/plots if produced) =="
ls -la "$out" | head -20
EOF
chmod +x shared/suno/align_keeper.sh && git add shared/suno/align_keeper.sh && git commit -qm "shared/suno: helper to align and analyze a chosen Suno clip

claude12:25 AM

Suno runs are going. Your account is Pro with 2,500 credits, and it turns out Suno's current default model is v6, with a free "v6-mini" tier. So the batch does two free v6-mini passes first (the 2am "day" song and "Replicate") as a pipeline test and a cheap first listen, then five v6 runs: the 2am song in electro-hop and in bubblegum, "Replicate" in theatre hip-hop and in club, and the v2 bright bottle version. A guard in the script measures the real per-call cost after the first paid run and stops before total spend would pass 830 credits.

Each run takes a few minutes with download. I'll report clip paths and credits used as they land. Clips go to songs/2am-crying/audio/<run>/ and songs/baby-facts/audio/<run>/.

notificationAgent "Opus: build 2am-crying video renderer" finished12:36 AM
status: completed · open the agent's thread → · jump to the call

I built the v3 selfie video ("the baby's selfie video") end to end. All 31 clip rows in TREATMENT.md are implemented, the full 540x960 draft is rendered over the synth demo audio, and both review sheets are committed.

The draft's determinism and loop checks pass: frames match when rendered out of order across workers, and the outro is the intro frame for frame. The preview page also loads cleanly in both layouts.

Synth audio. The synth agent's iteration 7 now matches my v3 plan bar for bar (57 bars, 106.875 s). So the beat grid, sections and kicks come from its song.json. Every word is timed from its sung syllables, including the "it's" pickups before the downbeats. The tool only uses the synth file when its section order fits the lyric sheet; it rejected the earlier v1 arrangement on that check.

Deliverables

  • Draft: /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/video/renders/draft-540p.mp4 (gitignored; 9:16, 30 fps, H.264 with AAC, tagged BT.709).
  • Clip sheet: /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/video/sheets/plates.png, one cell per clip plus the tip-over, long-take and grid stages.
  • 16:9 sheet: /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/video/sheets/layout-16x9.png.
  • /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/video/README.md has the commands, the data fields and the per-clip status table.

Clip status (all done)

clip typecovers
hellointro, and the outro frame-exactly so the video loops
crib2am / 3am / 4am crying with the parent going from absent to the doorway to the floor; 5am quiet; 7:45 "sleeping" with the IR monitor cut-in; 8pm to 12am sleeping; 1am black with eyes opening in the silent bar
nap11am tip-over to the ceiling fan; 3pm car seat; the bridge long take (bottle, heavy eyes, a degree of slip per beat, fan slowing)
pooping1pm held still; 2pm the identical frame plus the red "again" slam
standing5:45 flash grin with the alarm clock; 6am and 6:15 with a stopwatch; 7:30 milk-stained onesie; 7:15 naked towel run
highchair12pm spoon; eating; 8:05 throw with a splat on the lens; 6:05 tilt down to the floor
closeupbottle, book, book corner in the mouth, finger into the lens, fighting it, 5pm crying (no extra witching-hour motif)
fan10:30 whip up to the fan; 5:30 crying at it
bath7pm splashing, droplets on the lens, caption drips
rear10pm: the camera flips to a parent asleep in the armchair
gridfinal chorus as a filling 3-wide grid of the day's clips; the 1am tile goes black

Render time

  • 540p: 5.7 ms/frame wall with 10 workers (about 36 ms per frame in each worker), so the whole song took 18 s. A second run took 47 ms/frame while Spotlight, another agent's Python job and Steam were loading the machine.
  • 1080p60: I timed 4 s of the grid, the heaviest section, at 58 ms/frame wall. A full 1080p60 render should take roughly 3 to 5 minutes; that is an estimate, not a timed run.

Commands (from the repo root; set up once with npm install --prefix shared/renderer)

  • Preview: node shared/renderer/scripts/serve.mjs, then open http://localhost:8123/songs/2am-crying/video/index.html?t=23 (add &layout=16x9 for the wide layout).
  • Draft: node shared/renderer/scripts/render.mjs --song songs/2am-crying/video --out songs/2am-crying/video/renders/draft-540p.mp4 --check
  • Final 9:16: the same with --w 1080 --h 1920 --fps 60 --out songs/2am-crying/video/renders/final-1080x1920-60.mp4
  • Final 16:9: add --layout 16x9 --w 1920 --h 1080 --fps 60 --out songs/2am-crying/video/renders/final-1920x1080-60.mp4
  • Clip sheet: ... --sheet songs/2am-crying/video/sheets/plates.png. Stills: ... --stills 4.5,40.
  • Timing: node songs/2am-crying/video/tools/mock_timing.mjs (add --plan to ignore the synth).
  • Click track: node songs/2am-crying/video/tools/make_click.mjs
  • Smoke test: node shared/renderer/scripts/smoke.mjs --q t=23 --q "layout=16x9&t=40"

What I kept from v1 and what I dropped. No v1 plates were finished when the pivot came (there was only a placeholder), so there were no finished scenes to adapt.

  • Kept:
    • the whole engine (timeline, beat utilities, render script, preview), plus a new shared caption component and a layout switch;
    • the old karaoke band, still in the engine but unused by v3;
    • the mock-timing and click tools, rebuilt for v3;
    • the v1 IR monitor look, reused as the 7:45 "sleeping" cut-in.
  • Dropped:
    • the NURSERY CAM HUD;
    • the sleep-debt bar;
    • IR greyscale as the main look;
    • one module per lyric line, replaced by one module per clip type chosen from the lyric text.

Deliberate changes from the brief

  • Verse 2 is 9 bars, not 8: the extra bar is the silence after "1am and I'm...", which makes 57 bars in total.
  • There is no wide-angle edge stretch. Daytime over-saturation is carried by the time-of-day colour grade instead.
  • The 12th grid tile is a record button, because 11 final-chorus lines leave one slot in a 3x4 grid.
  • The drinking clips hold the bottle one-handed, because the other arm is always holding the phone.

Notes

  • Commit attribution: the commits end with Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5, as the system attribution instruction says, rather than the Claude Fable 5.1 line in the task; the user's CLAUDE.md doesn't specify either.
  • Shared repo: other sessions twice swept my uncommitted files into their own commits. Everything of mine is committed, the last commit being 5f970fb, but a few files first landed through their commits.
  • Timing: when the Suno vocal is aligned, its lyrics.json and audio.json drop into data/ with no other changes, because clips are chosen from the lyric text.

timeout 300000
OUT=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad/align_mini1 && mkdir -p $OUT && uv run --project shared/align python shared/align/align.py --whisper-only --audio songs/2am-crying/audio/runE-mini/it-s-2am-and-i-m-crying-10b5f1d8.mp3 --lyrics songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v3_day.txt --out $OUT 2>&1 | tail -5; ls $OUT; python3 - $OUT <<'EOF'
import json,sys,glob,os
out=sys.argv[1]
ly=json.load(open(os.path.join(out,'lyrics.json')))
lines=ly['lines']; words=[w for l in lines for w in l['words']]
confs=[w.get('conf',0) for w in words]
print('lines',len(lines),'words',len(words),'mean conf',round(sum(confs)/max(1,len(confs)),2),'words conf<0.3:',sum(c<0.3 for c in confs))
print('song span', lines[0]['start'], '->', lines[-1]['end'])
# try to show whisper transcript from debug
for f in glob.glob(os.path.join(out,'*debug*.json'))+glob.glob(os.path.join(out,'**/*whisper*.json'),recursive=True):
    d=json.load(open(f))
    txt=None
    if isinstance(d,dict):
        for k in ('whisper_text','text','transcript'):
            if k in d: txt=d[k]; break
        if txt is None and 'whisper' in d and isinstance(d['whisper'],dict): txt=d['whisper'].get('text')
    if txt: print('WHISPER:', txt[:1500]); break
else:
    print('(no whisper transcript field found; files:', os.listdir(out),')')
EOF

description Extract what Whisper heard in the first free clip
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
d=json.load(open('/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad/align_mini1/align_debug.json'))
print('keys:', list(d.keys())[:20])
def find_words(o, depth=0):
    if depth>4: return None
    if isinstance(o, list) and o and isinstance(o[0], dict) and ('word' in o[0] or 'w' in o[0]) and ('start' in o[0]):
        return o
    if isinstance(o, dict):
        for k,v in o.items():
            r=find_words(v, depth+1)
            if r: return r
    return None
w=None
for k in ('whisper','whisper_words','whisper_turbo','asr'):
    if k in d: w=find_words(d[k]); break
if w is None: w=find_words(d)
if w:
    txt=' '.join((x.get('word') or x.get('w') or '').strip() for x in w)
    print('WHISPER HEARD (%d words):'%len(w)); print(txt[:2500])
else:
    print(json.dumps(d, default=str)[:1500])
EOF

There's now a real song to hear. The free v6-mini test run produced two full clips of the "day" litany (2:37 and 2:42), and a quick Whisper pass on the first one heard nearly every line, including the stutter edits Suno added on its own in the bridge ("it's 10, 10, 10:50 and I'm drinking"). It did skip part of verse 2 between "3pm" and "7:45", which is worth checking by ear.

The video draft is also done, rendered over the synth demo. It's the full selfie-video concept at 540x960: phone status bar with the clock, lowercase caption per clip, the parent silhouette creeping from doorway to floor across 2am/3am/4am, the nap tip-over to the ceiling fan, the identical pooping frames with the red "again" slam, the 10pm flip to the sleeping parent, the 1am black frame with eyes opening, and the final chorus as a filling grid.

BashWrite a Whisper triage script, commit run metadata1:03 AM

description Write a Whisper triage script, commit run metadata
cat > shared/suno/triage.py <<'EOF'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Whisper-only triage of Suno clips: how much of the lyric sheet did each clip deliver?
usage: triage.py <lyrics-sheet> <out.md> clip.mp3 [clip.mp3 ...]
Runs shared/align/align.py --whisper-only per clip (into a scratch dir), then reports
duration, words heard, fraction of sheet lines with >=60% of their words matched, and which lines were missed."""
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, difflib
ROOT = "/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop"
sheet, out_md, clips = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]

def norm(w): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']", "", w.lower())
lines = []
for ln in open(sheet):
    ln = ln.strip()
    if not ln or ln.startswith("["): continue
    lines.append(ln)
sheet_words = [norm(w) for ln in lines for w in ln.split() if norm(w)]

rows = []
for clip in clips:
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="triage_")
    dur = float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe","-v","error","-show_entries","format=duration","-of","csv=p=0",clip],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    subprocess.run(["uv","run","--project",f"{ROOT}/shared/align","python",f"{ROOT}/shared/align/align.py","--whisper-only","--audio",clip,"--lyrics",sheet,"--out",work],capture_output=True,text=True)
    try:
        dbg = json.load(open(os.path.join(work,"align_debug.json")))
        heard = [norm(x.get("word") or x.get("w") or "") for x in dbg.get("whisper_words",[])]
        heard = [h for h in heard if h]
    except Exception as e:
        rows.append((clip,dur,0,0.0,[f"(whisper failed: {e})"])); continue
    # line coverage: for each sheet line, fraction of its words found (in order) in the heard stream via SequenceMatcher on the whole
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=sheet_words, b=heard, autojunk=False)
    matched = set()
    for a,b,n in sm.get_matching_blocks():
        for k in range(n): matched.add(a+k)
    idx = 0; covered = []; missed = []
    for ln in lines:
        ws = [norm(w) for w in ln.split() if norm(w)]
        hit = sum(1 for k in range(idx, idx+len(ws)) if k in matched)
        frac = hit/max(1,len(ws)); idx += len(ws)
        covered.append(frac)
        if frac < 0.6: missed.append(ln[:48])
    cov = sum(f >= 0.6 for f in covered)/max(1,len(covered))
    rows.append((clip,dur,len(heard),cov,missed))

with open(out_md,"w") as f:
    f.write(f"# Whisper triage: {os.path.basename(sheet)}\n\nSheet: {len(lines)} lines, {len(sheet_words)} words. Coverage = share of sheet lines with at least 60% of their words heard in order.\n\n")
    f.write("| clip | length | words heard | line coverage | missed lines |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n")
    for clip,dur,nh,cov,missed in rows:
        rel = os.path.relpath(clip, ROOT)
        f.write(f"| `{rel}` | {int(dur//60)}:{int(dur%60):02d} | {nh} | {cov*100:.0f}% | {len(missed)} |\n")
    f.write("\n## Missed lines per clip\n")
    for clip,dur,nh,cov,missed in rows:
        f.write(f"\n### {os.path.relpath(clip, ROOT)}\n")
        for m in missed[:25]: f.write(f"- {m}\n")
        if len(missed) > 25: f.write(f"- ... {len(missed)-25} more\n")
print(open(out_md).read()[:3000])
EOF
chmod +x shared/suno/triage.py && git add shared/suno/triage.py shared/suno/logs songs/*/audio/*/result.json && git commit -qm "shared/suno: batch results (6 runs, 10 credits each) and a Whisper triage script

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>" && echo committed

63:`--crf 16`, `--preset medium`, `--audio file`, `--force` (allow audio/timing length mismatch),
64-`--check` (determinism: ordered vs shuffled frames across workers; loop: outro frames equal
65:intro frames). Video is libx264 CRF 16, yuv420p, tagged BT.709; audio AAC 192k.
66-
67-## Data
68-
69:- `data/lyrics.json`: `{ lines: [{ i, text, start, end, section, words: [{ w, start, end, conf, syl? }] }], extras, notes }`
70:  (mexicat/pdoom-video schema; `section` is a convenience, the engine recomputes it from audio.json).
71:- `data/audio.json`: `{ bpm, beats, downbeats, sections: [{ name, start, end }], kicks, duration }` plus
72-  added optional fields: `beats_per_bar`, `hats` (offbeat onsets), `quiet` (silent spans: the bar
73-  after "1am and I'm..."), `risers`, `source` ("plan" or "synth (...)": render.mjs and the preview
74:  pick the audio file from it), `lyrics_sheet`.
75-
76:`tools/mock_timing.mjs` builds both. It prefers `../synth/out/song.json` when that arrangement
77-fits the lyric sheet (same section order, at least a bar per line); it then takes the beat grid,
78-sections and kicks from the synth and times every word from the synth's sung syllables
79-(`lyric_lines`, `adlibs`). Otherwise it lays the sheet out on the plan: intro 2, chorus 8,
--
83:bar). When the Suno vocal is aligned (`shared/align`), drop its `lyrics.json`/`audio.json` in
84:`data/`: clips are derived from lyric content, so nothing else changes. Watch the console for
85-`[clips] ... matched no rule` (a clause whose text drifted falls back to the closeup clip).
86-
87:Audio: the draft uses `../synth/out/2am_crying.wav` when `audio.json.source` is the synth
88:(the full-song file, chosen by duration); otherwise `audio/click.wav`, a click + kick + hats +
89:riser track generated from audio.json by `tools/make_click.mjs` (written in Node, no ffmpeg
90:filters needed). render.mjs refuses audio whose length differs from audio.json by more than a bar.

--- timeline.js ---
// The edit: scene windows anchored to lyric lines (by content) or sections, snapped to
// the beat grid. A window runs from its anchor to the next window's anchor.
//
// spec entry:
//   { plate: 'hook', params: { n: 1 },
//     at: { section: 'chorus1' }                      // section start
//       | { line: 'Seven-thirty', section?: 'verse1', nth?: 0, word?: 'bath' }  // line (or word) start
//       | { time: 0 },                                // absolute (only for the very first window)
//       | { t, why },                                 // a time a spec *function* derived from lyric content
//     snap: 'downbeat' | 'beat' | 'half' | 'none',    // default 'downbeat'
//     offsetBeats: 0,                                 // nudge after snapping
//     hero: { line, word, section, offsetBeats } | number (fraction of window)  // contact-sheet time
//   }

import { bisect } from './util.js';

export function buildTimeline(spec, { lyrics, beats }) {
  // A spec may be a function of the data, so clips can be derived from lyric content.
  if (typeof spec === 'function') spec = spec({ lyrics, beats });
  const resolveAnchor = (at, label) => {
    if (at == null) throw new Error(`timeline: plate ${label} has no anchor`);
    if (typeof at.time === 'number') return at.time;
    if (typeof at.t === 'number') return at.t;   // derived from lyric content by a spec function
    if (at.line != null || at.word != null) {
      const line = lyrics.findLine({ match: at.line ?? null, section: at.section ?? null, nth: at.nth ?? 0 });
      if (!line) throw new Error(`timeline: plate ${label}: no lyric line matches ${JSON.stringify(at)}`);
      if (at.word) {
        const w = lyrics.findWord(line, at.word, { nth: at.wordNth ?? 0, loose: at.loose ?? false });
        if (!w) throw new Error(`timeline: plate ${label}: no word "${at.word}" in line "${line.text}"`);
        return w.start;
      }
      return line.start;
    }
    if (at.section) {
      const s = beats.section(at.section);
      if (!s) throw new Error(`timeline: plate ${label}: no section "${at.section}" in audio.json`);
      return s.start;
    }
    throw new Error(`timeline: plate ${label}: cannot resolve anchor ${JSON.stringify(at)}`);
  };

  const windows = spec.map((e, idx) => {
    const label = `${e.plate}${e.params?.n ? `#${e.params.n}` : ''} (entry ${idx})`;
    const raw = resolveAnchor(e.at, label);
    let start = beats.snap(raw, e.snap ?? 'downbeat') + (e.offsetBeats || 0) * beats.beatDur;
    if (idx === 0) start = Math.min(start, 0);
    return { idx, id: `${e.plate}${e.params?.n ? e.params.n : ''}`, plate: e.plate, params: { ...(e.params || {}) }, anchor: raw, start, spec: e, label };
  });
  for (let i = 0; i < windows.length; i++) {
    windows[i].end = i + 1 < windows.length ? windows[i + 1].start : beats.duration;
    if (!(windows[i].end > windows[i].start)) {
      throw new Error(`timeline: window ${windows[i].label} is empty or out of order (${windows[i].start.toFixed(3)} -> ${windows[i].end.toFixed(3)})`);
    }
  }
  // Lines belong to the window that contains a point just inside their start (pickups
  // before a snapped downbeat still belong to the plate they open).
  for (const w of windows) w.lines = [];
  for (const l of lyrics.lines) {
    const probe = l.start + Math.min(beats.beatDur, 0.3 * (l.end - l.start));
    const w = windowAt(probe);
    if (w) w.lines.push(l);
  }
  for (const w of windows) {
    w.dur = w.end - w.start;
    w.line = (k) => w.lines[k] || null;
    /** Find a word by text in this window's lines: word(match, {line: k | 'text', nth}) */
    w.word = (match, o = {}) => {
      const pool = o.line == null ? w.lines : typeof o.line === 'number' ? [w.lines[o.line]].filter(Boolean)
        : w.lines.filter((l) => l.n.includes(lyrics.norm(o.line)));
      let n = o.nth ?? 0;
      for (const l of pool) {
        for (const wd of l.words) {
          const nw = lyrics.norm(wd.w), m = lyrics.norm(match);
          if (nw === m || nw.includes(m)) { if (n-- === 0) return wd; }
        }
      }
      if (o.loose) for (const l of pool) for (const wd of l.words) if (/\d/.test(wd.w)) return wd;
      if (o.required === false) return null;
      throw new Error(`plate ${w.label}: no word "${match}" in its lines (${w.lines.map((l) => l.text).join(' / ')})`);
    };
    /** Time of a word's start (snapped to the beat grid if snap is given). */
    w.wordTime = (match, o = {}) => {
      const wd = w.word(match, o);
      if (!wd) return o.fallback ?? w.start;
      return o.snap ? beats.snap(wd.start, o.snap) : wd.start;
    };
    w.findLine = (match) => w.lines.find((l) => l.n.includes(lyrics.norm(match))) || null;
  }

  function windowAt(t) {
    const i = bisect(windows, t, (w) => w.start);
    return windows[Math.max(0, i)];
  }

  function heroTime(w) {
    const h = w.spec.hero;
    if (h == null) return w.start + w.dur * 0.5;
    if (typeof h === 'number') return w.start + w.dur * h;
    if (typeof h === 'function') return h(w);
    let t;
    if (h.word) t = w.wordTime(h.word, { line: h.line, nth: h.nth, loose: h.loose });
    else if (h.line) { const l = w.findLine(h.line); if (!l) throw new Error(`hero: no line ${h.line} in ${w.label}`); t = l.start; }
    else t = w.start;
    return t + (h.offsetBeats || 0) * beats.beatDur + (h.offset || 0);
  }

  return { windows, windowAt, heroTime };
}

BashMake the timeline resolve snapped-window collisions instead of throwing
input
description Make the timeline resolve snapped-window collisions instead of throwing
python3 - <<'EOF'
p='shared/renderer/core/timeline.js'
s=open(p).read()
old="""  for (let i = 0; i < windows.length; i++) {
    windows[i].end = i + 1 < windows.length ? windows[i + 1].start : beats.duration;
    if (!(windows[i].end > windows[i].start)) {
      throw new Error(`timeline: window ${windows[i].label} is empty or out of order (${windows[i].start.toFixed(3)} -> ${windows[i].end.toFixed(3)})`);
    }
  }"""
new="""  // Real (aligned) vocals don't land exactly on the grid, so two consecutive clauses can
  // snap to the same downbeat. Resolve collisions by tightening the snap for the later
  // window (beat, then half-beat), and as a last resort by placing it one beat after the
  // previous window. Windows stay monotonic and non-empty instead of throwing.
  for (let i = 1; i < windows.length; i++) {
    const prev = windows[i - 1], w = windows[i];
    if (w.start > prev.start) continue;
    const tries = [beats.snap(w.anchor, 'beat'), beats.snap(w.anchor, 'half'), w.anchor];
    let fixed = tries.find((t) => t > prev.start + 1e-6);
    if (fixed == null) fixed = prev.start + beats.beatDur;
    w.collided = { from: w.start, to: fixed };
    w.start = fixed;
  }
  for (let i = 0; i < windows.length; i++) {
    windows[i].end = i + 1 < windows.length ? windows[i + 1].start : beats.duration;
    if (!(windows[i].end > windows[i].start)) {
      throw new Error(`timeline: window ${windows[i].label} is empty or out of order (${windows[i].start.toFixed(3)} -> ${windows[i].end.toFixed(3)})`);
    }
  }
  const collided = windows.filter((w) => w.collided);
  if (collided.length && typeof console !== 'undefined') {
    console.warn(`[timeline] ${collided.length} window(s) moved off a shared downbeat: ` +
      collided.slice(0, 6).map((w) => `${w.label} ${w.collided.from.toFixed(2)}->${w.collided.to.toFixed(2)}`).join('; ') + (collided.length > 6 ? ' ...' : ''));
  }"""
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,new)
open(p,'w').write(s)
print('patched')
EOF
result
patched

The page doesn't describe Clawd's design in detail. It doesn't give body shape, proportions, colors or hex codes, limbs, legs, or face, and it doesn't explain how Clawd is drawn in p5 shapes.

**What the page does say:**

- **Defining files:** [src/clawd.js](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase/blob/main/src/clawd.js) contains "views, emotions, eyes, mouths, hats, emotes, dances." The model sheets are in [docs/](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase/blob/main/docs), including emotions.jpg and views.jpg.
- **Emotions:** The project includes "31 acted emotions," shown in the emotions model sheet.
- **Style rules:** The guide ([ANIMATION_GUIDE.md](https://github.com/JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase/blob/main/ANIMATION_GUIDE.md)) calls for "a solid medium of brush strokes, flat 2D and boiling linework." It also lists rules such as "handmade, alive, one piece, no text."
- **Rendering:** Clawd is painted with p5.js and p5.brush, and watercolour fills are noted as slow on integrated graphics.

**Animation:** The page mentions emotions, emotes, dances, and a "motion" model sheet, and says the emotions are animated (emotions.webp). It doesn't mention bounce or blink specifically, though eyes are a listed category in clawd.js.

For the precise design (proportions, colors, shapes), you'd need to read src/clawd.js and the model sheets in docs/.

The search turned up several sources on Clawd's orange design, with some conflicting details.

- **Default color:** A GitHub feature request describes the mascot as orange by default and asks for a way to change it, such as to green. Currently the Claude Code mascot icon is orange.
- **Possible blue shift:** A separate GitHub issue reports that the welcome-screen mascot appeared blue around version v2.0.67, after previously being consistently orange. The issue is marked resolved, but the snippets don't include the explanation.
- **Technical color values:** A community skill lists the body color as rgb(215,119,87) / ansi:redBright, with a black background.
- **Visual style:** Stark Insider describes Clawd as a little 8-bit-style sprite straight out of the 1980s, and a Codex pet listing calls an orange version a tiny orange blocky Claude Code mascot pet with black square eyes and four little legs.
- **Customization:** Community plugins let users recolor Clawd and add seasonal themes, such as holiday or accessory variants.

The sources don't clearly say whether the blue change was intentional, and the results don't include an official Anthropic statement on the design.

  mouth: 'line',             // 'line' | 'o' | 'smile' | 'grin' | 'none' | 'press'
  mouthOpen: 1,
  brows: null,               // null | 'furrow' | 'up'
  phoneArm: 'left',          // which bottom corner the phone arm reaches for
  free: { mode: 'down' },    // free arm: 'down' | 'wave' | 'up' | 'point' | 'none'
  stain: false, tears: 0, blush: 0,
  flash: 0,                  // 0..1 hot-spot of the phone flash on the face
};

function circle(ctx, x, y, r) { ctx.beginPath(); ctx.arc(x, y, r, 0, TAU); }

function limb(ctx, pts, w0, w1, fill, line, lw) {
  // a tapered stroke through pts, drawn as a filled polygon with round ends
  const n = pts.length;
  const left = [], right = [];
  for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
    const a = pts[Math.max(0, i - 1)], b = pts[Math.min(n - 1, i + 1)];
    const dx = b[0] - a[0], dy = b[1] - a[1], d = Math.hypot(dx, dy) || 1;
    const w = lerp(w0, w1, i / (n - 1)) / 2;
    left.push([pts[i][0] - (dy / d) * w, pts[i][1] + (dx / d) * w]);
    right.push([pts[i][0] + (dy / d) * w, pts[i][1] - (dx / d) * w]);
  }
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.moveTo(left[0][0], left[0][1]);
  for (const p of left.slice(1)) ctx.lineTo(p[0], p[1]);
  const e = pts[n - 1];
  ctx.arc(e[0], e[1], w1 / 2, Math.atan2(left[n - 1][1] - e[1], left[n - 1][0] - e[0]), Math.atan2(right[n - 1][1] - e[1], right[n - 1][0] - e[0]), true);
  for (const p of right.slice(0, -1).reverse()) ctx.lineTo(p[0], p[1]);
  const s = pts[0];
  ctx.arc(s[0], s[1], w0 / 2, Math.atan2(right[0][1] - s[1], right[0][0] - s[0]), Math.atan2(left[0][1] - s[1], left[0][0] - s[0]), true);
  ctx.closePath();
  ctx.fillStyle = fill;
  ctx.fill();
  if (line) { ctx.strokeStyle = line; ctx.lineWidth = lw; ctx.stroke(); }
}

export function drawBaby(ctx, opts) {
  const o = { ...BABY_DEFAULTS, ...opts, free: { ...BABY_DEFAULTS.free, ...(opts.free || {}) } };
  const { r, C } = o;
  const lw = r * 0.028;
  const s = o.phoneArm === 'left' ? -1 : 1;
  ctx.save();
  ctx.translate(o.x, o.y);

Two changes to the 2am-crying selfie video renderer in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop (git repo; the renderer engine is shared/renderer/, the song's scenes are songs/2am-crying/video/; read songs/2am-crying/video/README.md and songs/2am-crying/TREATMENT.md first). Rules: never cd; absolute paths from the repo root; slow renders in the background; commit eagerly as normal commits (no amend/rebase), ending commit messages with Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Don't touch songs/2am-crying/synth/, songs/baby-facts/, or shared/suno/. You can view PNGs with the Read tool; use that to iterate visually (--stills and --sheet in render.mjs).

1. Bug: real-vocal timing drops the section ids, so the bridge, the final grid and the outro loop never fire

The video now runs on a real Suno vocal. Its timing lives in songs/2am-crying/video/data/lyrics.json and audio.json, produced by shared/align/align.py + analyze.py from songs/2am-crying/audio/runE2/it-s-2am-and-i-m-crying-bright-13e92be2.mp3 and the sheet songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v3_day.txt (the mock timing it replaced is kept in songs/2am-crying/video/data-mock/). The aligned lyrics.json lines have keys i, text, start, end, words but no section, while clips.js and story.js select clips by line.section with the ids intro, chorus1, verse1, chorus2, verse2, bridge, final, outro. Result in the current draft (songs/2am-crying/video/renders/draft-suno-E2-540p.mp4): no bridge long take (so no bottle during the milk verse, which the user noticed), no final-chorus grid, and the outro hello loop clip probably didn't match either. audio.json.sections from analyze.py are generic s1..s11, so they can't be used for this.

Fix it at both ends:

  • In shared/align/align.py (and common.py where the sheet is parsed), emit section on every line of lyrics.json, derived from the sheet's [Section - notes] headers with this naming: take the text before - , lowercase, drop spaces (Verse 1 → verse1), Final Chorus → final, and number repeated plain names by occurrence (Chorus, Chorus → chorus1, chorus2). Keep bv as is. Re-run the alignment for the runE2 clip (it is cached in shared/align/work/, so it takes seconds: uv run --project /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/shared/align python /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/shared/align/align.py --audio <mp3> --lyrics <sheet> --out /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/2am-crying/audio/runE2/data) and copy the new lyrics.json into songs/2am-crying/video/data/ (keep the source and lyrics_sheet fields that are already in that audio.json). Also update shared/align/README.md and EVAL.md only where they describe the schema.
  • In the renderer, make clips.js/story.js robust: if lines have no section, derive it from the sheet named in audio.json.lyrics_sheet (same naming), and log a warning. Also log at render start which plates were created from sections (bridge long take, final chorus grid, outro loop) so this silent failure can't recur.
  • Then confirm with stills that the bridge long take shows the bottle during "10:50 … 10:58 and I'm heavy", that the final chorus is the filling grid, and that the outro frame equals the intro frame (--check does the loop test).

Note: shared/renderer/core/timeline.js was just patched to resolve two clauses snapping to the same downbeat (real vocals aren't on the grid); keep that.

2. Redesign the character as baby Clawd

The user's note: "the baby is... not that cute? have we considered baby clawd?" Clawd is the Claude Code mascot and the protagonist of the earlier "I'm Upping My P(doom)" video, so a baby Clawd is the right lead for a "clawdpop" video. Reference model sheets (view them with Read): /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad/clawd_ref/views.jpg and .../emotions.jpg, plus the p5 source .../clawd.js (its comments document the geometry: body 10 units wide by 6 tall with slightly rounded corners, four stubby legs under it, two little arm nubs at the sides, eyes at (±2.5u, −6u) each 1u wide and 2u tall as dark rounded rectangles with a white highlight dot, mouth near (0, −4.3u), body colour terracotta clay around #D77757 with a darker band low on the body, dark ink outline). These are reference only; do not copy files into the repo; draw it fresh in Canvas 2D in our flat style.

Baby-fy it: chubbier, nearly square body with rounder corners; legs shorter and stubbier; eyes bigger and set lower with a bigger highlight; a tuft or single curl on top; blush; a pacifier for the quiet and sleeping moments (a round shield with a ring over the mouth position); the night outfit is a sleep sack that wraps the legs (a soft bag with a zipper line), the day outfit a onesie band across the lower body with two snaps; "naked" after the bath is the bare clay body; "towel" is a cape. One arm nub always extends toward the bottom corner holding the phone (we see the nub stretched, not the phone), as now. Expressions map onto the existing API: eyes open/half/closed/squeeze/wide/focus → eyelids and squints on the rectangular Clawd eyes; mouth line/o/smile/grin/press → Clawd's small mouth (keep the crying O; the pooping "press" is a flat line with a furrowed brow); tears, blush, flash, stain (milk on the body), look (pupil highlight shifts) must all still work. The crying face should still read as crying from across a room.

Keep drawBaby(ctx, o) and BABY_DEFAULTS as the API so every scene keeps working; change the drawing in baby.js (and the character's colours in the palette). Check every clip type on the contact sheet: crib (night, flash), standing in the crib, high chair with food, closeup with bottle and book, bath with droplets, naked towel run, nap and the bridge long take with the bottle sliding off, pooping hold, rear-camera parent (the parent can stay human or become an adult Clawd asleep in the chair; adult Clawd is the better joke), grid. The sleeping-parent silhouette in the doorway and on the floor during 2am/3am/4am should match whatever the parent becomes.

claude6:14 AM

Good catch on the bottle, and it pointed at a real bug. The aligned Suno timing didn't carry section ids, and the renderer picks the bridge long take, the final-chorus grid and the outro loop by section. So the draft you watched had none of those three: no bottle long take, no grid, and probably no clean loop. The fix is to emit section ids from the lyric sheet in the alignment output and make the renderer derive them itself if they're missing, with a start-up log so it can't fail silently again.

Baby Clawd is a yes. 1. The section bug

It failed at three points, not one:

  • Aligner: align.py wrote no section on lyrics.json lines. common.parse_sheet now gives each line a section id from the sheet headers with your naming (intro, chorus1, verse1, chorus2, verse2, bridge, final, outro), and align.py writes it. I copied the result into video/data/ and left audio.json alone. The only other caller of the parser, tools/make_test_vocal.py, is unaffected.
  • Engine: even with sections present, core/lyrics.js overwrote every line's section with audio.json's s1..s11. Now a line's own section wins; if lines have none, sections come from the sheet named in audio.json.lyrics_sheet (same naming, with a warning). audio.json is only a last resort, with a warning.
  • Logging: render.mjs never printed page warnings, because Puppeteer calls them warn, not warning. That's why the failure was silent. It now prints where the sections came from, and ok or MISSING for the bridge long take, the final chorus grid and the outro loop. A missing loop fails --check with exit code 2.
  • Side effect: verse clauses now cut on the half bar again.

=====batch.sh=====
#!/bin/bash
# Suno batch for 2026-10-17. Budget guard: never spend more than $BUDGET credits in total.
# Free v6-mini passes first (pipeline test + a cheap listen), then v6 on the main directions.
set -u
S=~/.local/bin/suno
ROOT=/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop
LOG=$ROOT/shared/suno/logs/batch-20261017.log
BUDGET=${BUDGET:-830}
START_CREDITS=2500
COST_EST=100   # replaced by the measured cost after the first v6 run

credits_left() { $S credits --json 2>/dev/null | python3 -c "import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['data']['total_credits_left'])"; }
log() { echo "$(date '+%H:%M:%S') $*" | tee -a "$LOG"; }

run() {  # run <outdir> <model> <title> <lyrics-file> <tags> <exclude> <style> <weird> [extra flags]
  local out=$1 model=$2 title=$3 lyr=$4 tags=$5 excl=$6 style=$7 weird=$8; shift 8
  mkdir -p "$out"
  if [ "$(ls "$out" 2>/dev/null | grep -c mp3)" -ge 1 ] && grep -q '"status":"success"' "$out/result.json" 2>/dev/null; then log "SKIP $out (already done)"; return 0; fi
  if [ "$model" != "v6-mini" ]; then
    local left; left=$(credits_left); local spent=$((START_CREDITS - left))
    if [ $((spent + COST_EST)) -gt "$BUDGET" ]; then log "BUDGET STOP before $out: spent=$spent est=$COST_EST budget=$BUDGET"; return 2; fi
  fi
  local before; before=$(credits_left)
  log "START $out model=$model credits_before=$before"
  local attempt=0 rc=1
  while [ $attempt -lt 3 ]; do
    attempt=$((attempt+1))
    $S generate --json --model "$model" --vocal female --title "$title" \
      --tags "$tags" --exclude "$excl" --style-influence "$style" --weirdness "$weird" \
      --lyrics-file "$lyr" --download "$out" "$@" > "$out/result.json" 2> "$out/stderr.log"
    rc=$?
    if [ $rc -eq 4 ]; then log "rate limited on $out, attempt $attempt; sleeping 90s"; sleep 90; continue; fi
    break
  done
  local after; after=$(credits_left)
  local cost=$((before - after))
  log "DONE $out rc=$rc cost=$cost credits_left=$after files: $(ls "$out" 2>/dev/null | grep -c mp3) mp3"
  if [ "$model" != "v6-mini" ] && [ $cost -gt 0 ]; then COST_EST=$cost; fi
  python3 - "$out/result.json" <<'PY' 2>/dev/null | tee -a "$LOG"
import sys, json
try:
    d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))
except Exception as e:
    print("  (result.json unreadable:", e, ")"); sys.exit()
print("  status:", d.get("status"))
data = d.get("data") or {}
clips = data.get("clips") or data.get("downloads") or []
for c in clips if isinstance(clips, list) else []:
    if isinstance(c, dict):
        print("  clip:", c.get("id", "")[:8], c.get("title", ""), c.get("duration") or c.get("metadata", {}).get("duration", ""), c.get("path") or c.get("file") or c.get("audio_url", "")[:60])
if d.get("status") != "success":
    print("  error:", json.dumps(d.get("error"))[:400])
PY
  return $rc
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Whisper-only triage of Suno clips: how much of the lyric sheet did each clip deliver?
usage: triage.py <lyrics-sheet> <out.md> clip.mp3 [clip.mp3 ...]
Runs shared/align/align.py --whisper-only per clip (into a scratch dir), then reports
duration, words heard, fraction of sheet lines with >=60% of their words matched, and which lines were missed."""
import json, os, re, subprocess, sys, tempfile, difflib
ROOT = "/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop"
sheet, out_md, clips = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2], sys.argv[3:]

def norm(w): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']", "", w.lower())
lines = []
for ln in open(sheet):
    ln = ln.strip()
    if not ln or ln.startswith("["): continue
    lines.append(ln)
sheet_words = [norm(w) for ln in lines for w in ln.split() if norm(w)]

rows = []
for clip in clips:
    work = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="triage_")
    dur = float(subprocess.run(["ffprobe","-v","error","-show_entries","format=duration","-of","csv=p=0",clip],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout.strip() or 0)
    subprocess.run(["uv","run","--project",f"{ROOT}/shared/align","python",f"{ROOT}/shared/align/align.py","--whisper-only","--audio",clip,"--lyrics",sheet,"--out",work],capture_output=True,text=True)
    try:
        dbg = json.load(open(os.path.join(work,"align_debug.json")))
        heard = [norm(x.get("word") or x.get("w") or "") for x in dbg.get("whisper_words",[])]
        heard = [h for h in heard if h]
    except Exception as e:
        rows.append((clip,dur,0,0.0,[f"(whisper failed: {e})"])); continue
    # line coverage: for each sheet line, fraction of its words found (in order) in the heard stream via SequenceMatcher on the whole
    sm = difflib.SequenceMatcher(a=sheet_words, b=heard, autojunk=False)
    matched = set()
    for a,b,n in sm.get_matching_blocks():
        for k in range(n): matched.add(a+k)
    idx = 0; covered = []; missed = []
    for ln in lines:
        ws = [norm(w) for w in ln.split() if norm(w)]
        hit = sum(1 for k in range(idx, idx+len(ws)) if k in matched)
        frac = hit/max(1,len(ws)); idx += len(ws)
        covered.append(frac)
        if frac < 0.6: missed.append(ln[:48])

import json, sys, re, numpy as np
from scipy.io import wavfile
from scipy.signal import butter, sosfiltfilt
SP = "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad"
dirs = {"238033cd":"triage_amd77h8a","1f1dc548":"triage_3af729tr","81103b6a":"triage_z1vy7bgt","4b1f92a1":"triage_2fc2l9nu"}
def norm(w): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']","",w.lower())
def kick_rate(x, sr, t0, t1):
    seg = x[int(t0*sr):int(t1*sr)]
    if len(seg) < sr: return 0.0, 0.0
    sos = butter(4, [40, 130], btype="band", fs=sr, output="sos")
    low = sosfiltfilt(sos, seg)
    hop = int(sr*0.01); env = np.array([np.sqrt(np.mean(low[i:i+hop]**2)) for i in range(0, len(low)-hop, hop)])
    env = env/ (env.max()+1e-9)
    d = np.diff(env, prepend=env[0]); d[d<0]=0
    thr = 0.25
    peaks = [i for i in range(1,len(d)-1) if d[i]>thr and d[i]>=d[i-1] and d[i]>=d[i+1]]
    # merge peaks within 150 ms
    merged=[]; 
    for p in peaks:
        if not merged or p-merged[-1] > 15: merged.append(p)
    rms = float(np.sqrt(np.mean(seg**2)))
    return len(merged)/(t1-t0), 20*np.log10(rms+1e-9)
for cid, d in dirs.items():
    dbg = json.load(open(f"/var/folders/5j/z7nytrhn2t920kt8xwk1h3580000gn/T/{d}/align_debug.json"))
    ww = dbg["whisper_words"]; dur = dbg["duration"]
    words = [norm(w["w"]) for w in ww]
    # bridge: first 'holding' ; end: first 'napping' after first 'love' after holding
    try:
        i0 = words.index("holding")
        iL = next(i for i in range(i0, len(words)) if words[i]=="love")
        i1 = max(i for i in range(iL, min(len(words), iL+40)) if words[i].startswith("napping")) if any(words[i].startswith("napping") for i in range(iL, min(len(words), iL+40))) else iL+5
    except (ValueError, StopIteration):
        print(f"\n== {cid}: bridge not found in whisper"); continue
    t0, t1 = ww[i0]["start"]-1.0, ww[i1]["end"]+0.5
    print(f"\n== {cid}  dur {dur:.1f}s  first word {ww[0]['start']:.1f}s  last word {ww[-1]['end']:.1f}s ({dur-ww[-1]['end']:.1f}s tail)")
    print(f"   bridge {t0:.1f}-{t1:.1f}s ({t1-t0:.1f}s):", " ".join(w["w"] for w in ww[i0-3:i1+6]))
    sr, x = wavfile.read(f"{SP}/v4wav/{cid}.wav"); x = x.astype(np.float32)/32768
    kb, lb = kick_rate(x, sr, t0, t1)
    # chorus reference: the first 'crying' after 'day' near start, take 20 s from there
    ic = next(i for i in range(len(words)) if words[i].startswith("crying"))
    c0 = ww[ic]["start"]-1; kc, lc = kick_rate(x, sr, c0, c0+20)
    # after-bridge final chorus 20 s
    ka, la = kick_rate(x, sr, t1+1, min(dur, t1+21))
    print(f"   kicks/s  chorus1 {kc:.2f}  bridge {kb:.2f}  final {ka:.2f}   |  level dB  chorus1 {lc:.1f}  bridge {lb:.1f}  final {la:.1f}")
    print("   outro:", " ".join(w["w"] for w in ww[-8:]))

#!/bin/bash
# After picking a Suno clip: word-align it and analyze the beat grid into songs/<song>/data/.
# usage: shared/suno/align_keeper.sh <song-dir-name> <path/to/clip.mp3> <lyrics-sheet.txt> [--sections song.json]
set -euo pipefail
ROOT=/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop
song=$1; mp3=$2; sheet=$3; shift 3
out=$ROOT/songs/$song/data
mkdir -p "$out"
echo "== align (Demucs + karaoke stem + CTC + Whisper cross-check) =="
uv run --project $ROOT/shared/align python $ROOT/shared/align/align.py --audio "$mp3" --lyrics "$sheet" --out "$out" --plots
echo "== analyze (beats, downbeats, kicks, sections, loudness) =="
uv run --project $ROOT/shared/align python $ROOT/shared/align/analyze.py --audio "$mp3" --out "$out" "$@"
echo "== done: $out/lyrics.json $out/audio.json (QA plots in $out/plots if produced) =="
ls -la "$out" | head -20

}

/**
 * Plates that exist only because of a line's section id. If the sections are wrong (e.g.
 * audio.json's detected s1..s11 instead of the sheet's ids) they silently vanish, so
 * render.mjs lists them at start-up and flags any that are MISSING.
 */
export const SECTION_PLATES = [
  { label: 'bridge long take', section: 'bridge', plate: 'nap' },
  { label: 'final chorus grid', section: 'final', plate: 'grid' },
  { label: 'outro loop', section: 'outro', plate: 'hello' },
];

/** Timeline spec function: the engine calls it with the parsed lyrics and beat grid. */
export function timeline({ lyrics, beats }) {
  const clauses = clausesOf(lyrics);
  const entries = [{ plate: 'hello', at: { time: 0 }, params: { loop: false }, hero: (w) => w.start + w.dur * 0.62 }];
  const hero80 = (w) => w.start + w.dur * 0.8;
  const fallbacks = [];
  for (const c of clauses) {
    if (c.section === 'bridge') {
      if (!entries.some((e) => e.plate === 'nap' && e.params.mode === 'long')) {
        entries.push({ plate: 'nap', params: { mode: 'long', clauses: clauses.filter((x) => x.section === 'bridge').map((x) => x.index) }, at: { t: c.start, why: 'bridge long take' }, fromSection: 'bridge long take', her
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (c.section === 'final') {
      if (!entries.some((e) => e.plate === 'grid')) {
        entries.push({ plate: 'grid', params: { clauses: clauses.filter((x) => x.section === 'final').map((x) => x.index) }, at: { t: c.start, why: 'final chorus grid' }, fromSection: 'final chorus grid', hero: (w) => w.
      }
      continue;
    }
    const rule = ruleFor(c);
    if (!rule.matched) fallbacks.push(c.text);
    entries.push({
      plate: rule.type,
      params: { ...rule.params, clause: c.index },
      at: { t: c.start, why: c.text },
      snap: /^verse/.test(c.section) ? 'halfbar' : 'downbeat',
      hero: hero80,
    });

function pickAudio(audioJson) {
  const given = opt('audio', null);
  const dur = audioJson.duration;
  const bar = (60 / audioJson.bpm) * (audioJson.beats_per_bar || 4);
  let file, why;
  if (given) { file = abs(given); why = '--audio'; }
  else if (String(audioJson.source || '').startsWith('synth')) {
    const dir = path.join(abs(songDir), '..', 'synth', 'out');
    const wavs = fs.existsSync(dir) ? fs.readdirSync(dir).filter((f) => f.endsWith('.wav')).map((f) => path.join(dir, f)) : [];
    const scored = wavs.map((f) => ({ f, d: ffprobeDuration(f) })).filter((x) => isFinite(x.d)).sort((a, b) => Math.abs(a.d - dur) - Math.abs(b.d - dur));
    if (scored.length) { file = scored[0].f; why = 'synth (closest duration to audio.json)'; }
  }
  if (!file) { file = path.join(abs(songDir), 'audio', 'click.wav'); why = 'click track (audio.json source: ' + (audioJson.source || '?') + ')'; }
  if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error(`audio ${file} not found (generate the click track: node ${songDir}/tools/make_click.mjs)`);
  const d = ffprobeDuration(file);
  if (Math.abs(d - dur) > bar && !flag('force')) {
    throw new Error(`audio ${path.relative(REPO, file)} is ${d.toFixed(2)}s but data/audio.json says ${dur.toFixed(2)}s (more than a bar apart): the timing and the audio do not match. Regenerate timing or pass --force.`);
----- boot.js sheet lookup
 * line has no `section` (older alignment output). The name may be relative to the data
 * dir, to the song root (the video dir's parent: "suno_lyrics_v3_day.txt") or to the repo
 * root ("songs/2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v3_day.txt"); the first that loads wins.
 */
export async function loadSheet(lyricsJson, audioJson, { dataBase, base }) {
  const lines = lyricsJson.lines || [];
  if (lines.every((l) => l.section)) return null;
  const name = audioJson.lyrics_sheet || lyricsJson.lyrics_sheet;
  if (!name) {
    console.warn('[lyrics] lyrics.json lines have no "section" and audio.json names no lyrics_sheet to derive them from');
    return null;
  }
  const clean = String(name).replace(/^\/+/, '');
  const tries = (clean.includes('/') ? [new URL('/' + clean, location.origin), new URL('../' + clean, base)] : [new URL('../' + clean, base), new URL('/' + clean, location.origin)])
    .concat([new URL(clean, dataBase)]);
  for (const u of tries) {
    try {
      const r = await fetch(u, { cache: 'no-store' });
      if (r.ok) return { name: clean, text: await r.text(), url: String(u) };
    } catch { /* try the next */ }
  }
  console.warn(`[lyrics] lyrics_sheet "${name}" not found (tried ${tries.map(String).join(', ')})`);
  return null;
}

    const blink = C.t < tHeavy ? 0 : 0.35 * Math.max(0, Math.sin((C.t - tHeavy) * 5)) * (1 - seg(C.t, tHeavy, tNap));
    const droop = ease.inOutCubic(seg(C.t, tHeavy, tNap + 0.6));

How the take plays now (scenes/nap.js, mode long):

  • 10:50, "you're holding me": the adult Clawd parent's body fills the background, darker and slightly blurred, with its left edge and the warm room showing. One parent nub goes behind the baby's back and one crosses its legs; the phone nub stays clear. The light is warm and soft, the breathing is slow, and nothing moves on the beat.
  • 10:52, "drinking": the bottle comes up to the mouth and the milk level drops; the baby blushes on "warm".
  • 10:55, "warm, safe, heavy": the eyes get slowly heavy, the baby settles lower and the phone droops a little.
  • 10:58, "I love you": the baby's eyes leave the phone and look up. The parent leans in until its eyes, with highlights, sit just under the status bar, and the look is held.
  • Parenthetical: the caption shows it as usual; the look holds and the eyes get heavier.
  • 11am, "napping": the eyes close and the bottle slips onto the parent's arm. The phone tips up past the parent's face to the ceiling, the fan slows to nearly still, and the frame fades toward warm light.
