  • The nub across the legs is a straight block (the existing adult-nub prop, props.hand), so it is a bit plank-like.
  • Clawd's eyes are solid shapes, so the look-up is the eyes shifting upward in the face. It is subtle in stills but visible in motion.
  • The eyes open fully again for the look-up before getting heavier, so the heaviness isn't one steady slide. That was my call; capping the reopen would keep it continuous.
  • On the mock timing, 10:58 and 11am are only 1.9 s apart, so the parent is still leaning in as the eyes close.
  • I did not regenerate sheets/plates.png.
  • The second render took 358 s instead of 42 s because the machine was loaded by other processes (load average 24), not because of this change.

  1. The parent should read as Clawd from the first frame, not a brown backdrop. Stage it as a real selfie-from-the-lap: the phone is low, pointing up at the baby, so the parent's face is above the baby and the parent's eyes (with highlights) are partially visible at the top of the frame from 10:50 on, looking down at the baby (pupils/highlights down and toward the baby, not at the camera). On "I love you" the baby looks up and the parent leans in: the eyes come lower and larger into the frame and hold, as you have now. Keep the parent's body darker and slightly blurred as background, but let its silhouette show a rounded body edge or shoulder curve so it is clearly a body, not a wall.
  2. The nub across the baby's legs is a straight plank. Make it a rounded Clawd arm nub (rounded ends, a little shading on the underside) and wrap it under/around the baby so the baby sits in the crook of the arm. The one behind the back can stay. The result should feel like being held, with the baby slightly lower in frame than in the crib shots.
  3. Make the eye heaviness one continuous slide. Cap the reopen at "I love you" so the eyes get no wider than they were at the end of "heavy"; the look-up should be the eyes shifting upward, not reopening. Then they keep closing through the parenthetical to shut at 11am.

do you feel like you got to maximally express your creativity?
claude11:29 AM

Mostly, and the places where I didn't are specific.

Where I got to play: the lyric architecture. Turning your seven lines into a form, the double-time verses filling in the rest of the day, the day closing on its own first line, "It's 10pm and you're sleeping" as the one camera turn, and tonight's "I don't have the word yet. But I love you." Those feel like mine. So does measuring tenderness by kick density when I can't hear the takes.

Where I held back:

  • Visuals by proxy. I directed the video through briefs and frame reviews rather than drawing it. The staging ideas were mine, the hands were Opus's. That's the pipeline you set, and it works, but it's a step removed.
  • Suno conservatism. Two tag variants per round and 90 credits used of 830. There's room for stranger swings: a v6-wild pass, a whispered or half-time version, a version where the final chorus is a kids' choir.
  • Plumbing ate the clock. Section ids, loop margins, collision resolution, laptop sleep. Necessary, but not creative.
  • Ideas I shelved. One bridge line I liked and left out: "It's 10:59 and you're crying," the parent's happy tears. It's in the notes in LYRICS.md. And "Replicate" is the song with the densest writing and no picture yet. That video, with its lab-apparatus grammar, is the thing I'd most like to build.

If you want me to spend more taste and less plumbing next, the Suno exploration and "Replicate" are where it would show.

----- LYRICS
# Replicate (n = 1)

Dense fact-rap from the point of view of the baby being studied. The spine is Netflix's
*Babies* (2020): the title card ("15 babies, filmed over one year, 36 world-renowned
scientists") is the chorus, each verse is a tour of the labs in episode order, and the
bridge is the replication crisis. The hook "Will it replicate?" means three things: cells
dividing, the study being reproduced, and the baby daring the scientists. The turn at the
end: the only result that always replicates is the baby.

Every fact is on `FACTS.md` with a source. Verses are 12 lines at ~96 BPM, one line per bar,
musical-theatre hip-hop patter. "this girl" in verse 3 is the narrator; swap for "this kid".

---

**[Intro]** *(spoken, documentary narrator, over a fetal heartbeat; then the beat)*
> Fifteen babies. Filmed over one year. Thirty-six world-renowned scientists.
> And me. I'm the one in the little cap.

**[Verse 1: Love]**
> Day one: skin to skin, and the oxytocin's climbing.
> Feldman swabs the spit of eighty couples, and the timing's
> identical in dads. "Fatherhood is biological."
> Forty-eight gay fathers, amygdala lit: that's data, not anecdotal.
> Tronick, '68: "This emotion stuff is not what you want to do."
> So he froze a mother's face for two minutes and watched me come unglued:
> I smile, I bid, I fuss, I cry, I chew my hands to cope.
> Then she comes back. We repair. That's the study. That's the hope.

**[Chorus]**
> I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one.
> Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done.
> Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten.
> Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
> Will it replicate? *(Will it replicate?)*
> Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year.
> Will it replicate? Ask me in a year.

**[Verse 2: Crawling]**
> Barbu-Roth did nuclear physics; now she's hanging me in air.
> Dots stream under me. I swim. "A newborn's an astronaut," I swear.
> "We're still quadrupeds inside." She strapped a skateboard to my chest:
> two days old, I crossed the mattress. Twice. Three times. Then I had a rest.
> Lampl's neighbor's kid: sixty-two point seven, then sixty-four point five.
> "I'm terrible at this," she thought. Nope. That's just how we arrive:
> up to two and a half centimeters overnight, then sixty-three days of flat.
> Ninety-five percent of babyhood is growth-free. Front page. A big name mocked her for that.
> Adolph raised the slope six degrees a go, up to a sheer drop.
> Grant approached it like the shallow ones and went straight off the top.
> Two thousand three hundred sixty-eight steps an hour, seventeen falls, no stall.
> "Crawling isn't mandatory." Bum-shuffle, bear-crawl, whatever gets you down the hall.

**[Verse 3: Words, Sleep]**
> Hirsh-Pasek splits up Cinderella, pauses in the middle of a clause.
> I turn to where it breathes right. Can't talk yet. I know the laws.
> Saffran: pabeecoo, golatoo, two minutes, forty-five reps each.
> Probability one inside a word, point three across: I'm carving speech.
> Jarvis danced six hours a day, then counted who can learn a sound in the world:
> three birds, five mammals. Parrots, bats, elephants, seals, dolphins, songbirds, hummingbirds. This girl.
> Fenton's app: a thousand babies, six million events, logged to the minute:
> one-point-five million sleeps, two-point-five million feeds, the diapers, a million and a half in it.
> Random at one month, a hint by eight, a rhythm by a year. *(He hasn't published it.)*
> Blumberg says my twitch is sonar: one ping, a thousand neurons, mapping where my limbs fit.
> Spencer: hippocampus small, so I file in bouts; the spindles move the day
> from hippocampus to cortex. Two naps and a night. That's not lazy. That's the way.

**[Chorus]**

**[Verse 4: First Steps, then Part Two]** *(double-time on the Part Two lines)*
> Dominici wires my legs at two days old: two muscle patterns, and I step;
> toddlers add two more. Rats, cats, macaques, guineafowl: same ancient rep.
> Cowgill hauled a hundred thirty pounds through fifteen museums, six hundred kids' bones in the stack.
> Reviewer 2 said "children's bones don't respond to exercise." Toddler femurs are wide ovals. Take that back.
> Walle: walkers know more words than crawlers, and they hear the exact same amount.
> It's you: "Du—" "Duck." "Duck!" Three hundred seventy-four words in five minutes. I count.
> Part Two: Hespos hangs a block in midair; I stare twice as long. I know how things fall.
> Kang Lee: six months, I tell two monkeys apart. Nine months, like you, not at all.
> Saxe scans her own son, awake: face patch, place patch, same spots as yours.
> Hamlin's puppet climbs; I reach for the helper. *(Hold that thought. It's back in the bridge, of course.)*
> Carpenter: twelve months, I point to show, not to get. You look. That's the human part.
> Warneken "drops" a cup; eighteen months, I hand it back in ten seconds. Pay me with a toy and I'll stop. Also the human part.

**[Bridge: the part you skip]** *(half-time, sparse, the baby as Reviewer 2)*
> Now the part you skip.
> The Wonder Weeks: ten leaps on a calendar. Tested on four babies by a grad student. Nothing. The man behind it lost his job in '98.
> Mozart effect: thirty-six college students, ten minutes, never once a baby. Georgia spent a hundred and five grand on CDs for newborns.
> Baby Einstein: a month of DVDs, zero new words. Disney refunded fifteen ninety-nine a disc.
> Neonatal imitation: six babies in '77 stuck their tongues out. A hundred and six in 2016 did nothing.
> The helper and the hinderer: *Nature*, 2007. ManyBabies 4: five hundred sixty-seven babies, thirty-seven labs. Forty-nine point three percent. A coin.
> Thirty million words: forty-two families, one hour a month.
> So when you ask me... will it replicate?
> *(beat drops out)*
> Here's what did.
> Me. Brain volume up a hundred and one percent in year one. Twenty-five hundred synapses a neuron, then more, then pruned. Weight tripled. Length up half.
> I'm the replication. I'm the only result that always comes in.

**[Final Chorus]**
> I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one.
> Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done.
> Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten.
> Will it replicate? *(I did.)*
> Will it replicate? *(I did.)*
> Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year.
> Will it replicate? Ask me in a year.

**[Outro]** *(spoken; the beat stops; heartbeat)*
> "Hardest problem in the universe. We should let them sleep."
> n equals one.

# Treatment sketch: Replicate (n = 1)

One plate per lab, in the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" register: plates from an illustrated
methods section. The HUD number is `n = 1` in the corner; during the bridge it flickers
through the real sample sizes (4, 36, 6, 106, 567, 42) and in the final chorus returns to 1.

- Palette: lab-notebook paper, ink, one accent (the orange of a measuring tape). Figures
  drawn as journal figures: axes, error bars, a caption in a serif.
- The baby is the same procedural character as the 2am video, now with an EEG cap.
- Plates: oxytocin curves (Feldman); the still-face three-panel (Tronick); the newborn
  suspended over streaming dots (Barbu-Roth); the growth chart with saltations as steps and
  the 1986 notebook row 59.8 / 59.8 / 59.8 / 60.8 (Lampl); the adjustable slope rising six
  degrees per beat (Adolph); the Cinderella waveform with pauses marked (Hirsh-Pasek); the
  syllable stream with transitional probabilities (Saffran); the vocal-learner phylogeny
  (Jarvis); the six-million-event scatter resolving from noise to rhythm (Fenton); the sonar
  ping body map (Blumberg); spindles moving cards from hippocampus to cortex (Spencer); EMG
  traces, two then four (Dominici); the femur cross-sections, oval to teardrop (Cowgill);
  the LENA word counter (Walle); the floating block (Hespos); monkey faces blurring at nine
  months (Kang Lee); the scanner with a baby in it (Saxe); the puppet hill (Hamlin); the
  pointing finger (Carpenter); the dropped cup (Warneken).
- Bridge: each myth as a journal cover that gets a "RETRACTED" or "n = 4" stamp.
- Turn: a single cell dividing into a brain, the volume counter rolling to +101%.

[Intro - spoken, over a heartbeat]
Fifteen babies. Filmed over one year. Thirty-six world-renowned scientists.
And me. I'm the one in the little cap.

[Verse 1]
Day one: skin to skin, and the oxytocin's climbing
Feldman swabs the spit of eighty couples, and the timing's
identical in dads. "Fatherhood is biological."
Forty-eight gay fathers, amygdala lit: that's data, not anecdotal
Tronick, sixty-eight: "This emotion stuff is not what you want to do."
So he froze a mother's face for two minutes and watched me come unglued:
I smile, I bid, I fuss, I cry, I chew my hands to cope
Then she comes back. We repair. That's the study. That's the hope

[Chorus - big]
I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one
Put me in the scanner, put me on the slope. I'm not done
Cap on my head, swab in my cheek, measure me at seven, then at ten
Will it replicate? (Will it replicate?)
Will it replicate? (Will it replicate?)
Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year
Will it replicate? Ask me in a year

[Verse 2]

Dots stream under me. I swim. "A newborn's an astronaut," I swear
"We're still quadrupeds inside." She strapped a skateboard to my chest:
two days old, I crossed the mattress. Twice. Three times. Then I had a rest
Lampl's neighbor's kid: sixty-two point seven, then sixty-four point five
"I'm terrible at this," she thought. Nope. That's just how we arrive:
up to two and a half centimeters overnight, then sixty-three days of flat
Ninety-five percent of babyhood is growth-free. Front page. A big name mocked her for that
Adolph raised the slope six degrees a go, up to a sheer drop
Grant approached it like the shallow ones and went straight off the top

I turn to where it breathes right. Can't talk yet. I know the laws

Probability one inside a word, point three across: I'm carving speech
Jarvis danced six hours a day, then counted who can learn a sound in the world:
three birds, five mammals. Parrots, bats, elephants, seals, dolphins, songbirds, hummingbirds. This girl
Fenton's app: a thousand babies, six million events, logged to the minute:
one-point-five million sleeps, two-point-five million feeds, the diapers, a million and a half in it
Random at one month, a hint by eight, a rhythm by a year. (He hasn't published it.)
Blumberg says my twitch is sonar: one ping, a thousand neurons, mapping where my limbs fit

[Chorus - big]
I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the n of one
Will it replicate? (Will it replicate?)
Will it replicate? (Will it replicate?)
Fifteen babies. Thirty-six scientists. One year

Hamlin's puppet climbs the hill; I reach for the helper, of course

Pay me with a toy and I'll stop. Also the human part

file_path /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/baby-facts/TREATMENT.md
# Treatment: Replicate (n = 1)

A music video typeset like the methods section of a paper. Every lyric line is a figure.
The baby is the only thing on the page that is in color, and in every figure the baby is
the data point. That is the whole visual thesis: "I'm the subject. I'm the sample. I'm the
n of one."

Primary layout 16:9 (1920x1080). A paper figure is landscape. A 9:16 cut can come later
by stacking the figure over the caption.

## The page

- **Paper.** Cream lab-notebook stock (`#f4efe3`) with a faint 5 mm grid (`#e6dfcf`), a
  subtle paper grain (deterministic noise), slightly darker toward the edges. The page
  never changes; figures are drawn onto it and erased from it.
- **Ink.** One near-black (`#1d1a17`) for everything drawn: axes, apparatus, adults,
  arrows, annotations. Strokes have a slight hand wobble (deterministic noise seeded by
  the plate and the stroke index, never by wall time), as if inked with a technical pen.
  Hatching rather than fills for shade. A second, lighter ink (`#8a8378`) for grid-lines
  inside figures, error bars, dotted leaders.
- **Color.** Only the baby: baby Clawd from the 2am video (`songs/2am-crying/video/baby.js`,
  the clay orange `#D77757` family), now wearing a white EEG cap with ink electrodes and a
  ribbon of wires trailing off-frame ("the one in the little cap"). The cap is an opt-in
  option; the 2am video must stay pixel-identical. Where a figure has many data points,
  the other points are ink; the baby is the orange one. Where the lyric says "you", the
  adults (scientists, parents) are ink line drawings of adult Clawd, never colored.
- **Type.** Figure captions in a serif (system "Iowan Old Style", fallback Georgia),
  italic for the caption label: *Fig. 3.* Numbers and the HUD in a monospace ("SF Mono",
  fallback Menlo). The lyric itself is set in the serif as the figure legend, see below.

## Three permanent elements

1. **The HUD, top-left:** `n = 1` in mono, small, with a thin ink box. It holds `n = 1`
   for the whole song except the bridge, where it shows the real sample size of each myth
   as that myth is named (`n = 4`, `n = 36 (students)`, `n = 0 words`, `n = 567 · 37 labs`),
   then on the drop rolls through digits and settles back to `n = 1`, which it keeps to
   the end. The final frame of the song is just the HUD on paper.
2. **The figure caption, bottom:** a rule, then `Fig. k.` in italic serif plus a short
   title and the citation in lighter ink, e.g. *Fig. 7. Growth saltation in one infant
   (Lampl, 1992).* It changes with every figure. The figure numbers run in order across
   the song, which is a quiet joke by the final chorus (Fig. 31).
3. **The lyric legend:** the current lyric line set in the serif under the caption rule,
   two lines maximum, left-aligned, in lighter ink; each word turns full ink as it is sung
   (word-synced from `lyrics.json`). Dense lines must be readable: minimum 34 px at 1080p,
   wrap at the clause. Parentheticals in the lyric (backing vocals) are set in italic and
   smaller. This replaces the lowercase pop captions of the 2am video entirely.

## Figures, in song order

Each lyric line maps to a figure by text rule (as `clips.js` does in the 2am song). Lines
that share a lab share one figure that keeps developing (the slope keeps rising, the
scatter keeps filling). Hero moments land on the sung word.

**Intro.** The paper title block: `Replicate (n = 1)` as a paper title, then the author
line "Fifteen babies · thirty-six world-renowned scientists · one year", then an ECG/fetal
heartbeat trace drawing itself along the bottom in time with the heartbeat in the audio.
On "And me": the baby in the cap pokes in from the bottom-right corner and waves one nub.
This same page is the outro, so the song can loop (see Loop).

**Verse 1 (Love).**
- *Oxytocin.* Two curves rising on one chart, labeled "mothers" and "fathers", drawn in
  step; on "identical in dads" the second curve snaps exactly onto the first. A cotton swab
  icon at the axis origin. Caption cites Gordon et al. 2010.
- *Still face.* A three-panel strip like a figure with panels a, b, c. (a) adult Clawd in
  ink leaning toward the baby; (b) on "froze a mother's face" the adult's face goes flat
  and a 2:00 timer starts under the panel; the baby cycles through the bids as they are
  sung: smile, point ("bid"), fuss, cry (tears are the only non-orange color in the baby,
  pale blue as in the 2am video), hands to mouth; (c) on "Then she comes back" the adult
  leans back in and the baby's face settles. "We repair" is the caption title.

**Chorus (every time).** The apparatus line: a long bench drawn in ink with the stations
named in the lyric left to right, scanner ring, slope, EEG cap on a stand, swab, a ruler
marked 7 and 10 (months). The baby rides a small cart along the bench, passing through each
station on its word ("scanner" the ring, "slope" the ramp, "cap" the cap drops on, "swab"
a swab taps the cheek, "seven, then at ten" the ruler ticks). On "Will it replicate?" the
baby splits like a cell: one becomes two, two become four, each copy an ink outline, in a
dividing-cell diagram, with the original staying orange. The chorus ends with a 4x4 grid of
ink babies and one orange. In the **final chorus**, on each "(I did.)" a row of the grid
turns orange, and by "Ask me in a year" all sixteen are orange. That is the payoff; nothing
else in the song is colored, so it should feel like the page lighting up.

**Verse 2 (Crawling).**
- *Barbu-Roth.* The baby in a harness suspended over a floor of streaming dots (optic flow
  moving toward the camera, perspective grid), legs swimming on "I swim"; a small inset
  of a tumbling astronaut drawn in ink on "astronaut". On "skateboard" the harness lifts
  away and the baby is belly-down on a skateboard, crossing a mattress drawn in plan view;
  tally marks appear on "Twice. Three times."; on "a rest" the baby stops and the eyes
  close for a beat.
- *Lampl.* A growth chart, length vs days, with the classic smooth curve in light ink and
  the real data as a staircase: flat, flat, flat, a step. The notebook row
  `59.8 / 59.8 / 59.8 / 60.8` typed in mono above the step. On "two and a half centimeters
  overnight" a step rises; "sixty-three days of flat" draws a long flat run with a
  bracket. If the take contains the "front page" line, a newspaper masthead stamps in and
  a speech bubble from an ink figure is struck through. The baby stands on the current
  step of the staircase, growing by a few pixels with each step.
- *Adolph.* The adjustable slope: a ramp on a hinge with a protractor arc, the angle
  readout in mono. Each "six degrees" raises it 6° with a ratchet; by "sheer drop" it is
  near vertical. The baby is at the top, peering over. If the Grant line is present, an ink
  toddler approaches at the shallow pace and goes straight off the edge in a little arc
  (no impact drawn, just a dotted trajectory and a "*" footnote). Step counter and fall
  counter in the corner tick up to `2,368 /h` and `17`. On "Crawling isn't mandatory" a row
  of small ink icons for bum-shuffle, bear-crawl, crawl, with the baby doing the
  bum-shuffle, happily.

**Verse 3 (Words, Sleep).**
- *Hirsh-Pasek* (if present). A speech waveform of a Cinderella sentence, drawn as an ink
  envelope, with pauses inserted: ones at clause boundaries marked with a tick, one in the
  middle of a clause marked with a cross. Two loudspeaker icons left and right; the baby's
  head turns to the natural one.
- *Saffran.* A stream of syllables `pa bee coo go la too ...` scrolling by in mono, with
  arcs above showing transitional probabilities: `1.0` arcs inside words, `0.33` between.
  A counter of repetitions ticks to 45 over two minutes on the HUD line. On "I'm carving
  speech" the word boundaries cut in as vertical lines and the words stack.
- *Jarvis.* A phylogenetic tree in ink. On "three birds, five mammals" the vocal-learner
  branches thicken and get their labels in order as they are sung: parrots, bats, elephants,
  seals, dolphins, songbirds, hummingbirds; on "This girl" the last branch ends in the baby,
  orange, holding a tiny microphone. A small dancing silhouette footnote for "danced six
  hours a day".
- *Fenton.* A scatter: x is time of day (0 to 24 h), y is age in months (0 to 12). Sleep
  events as dots. At one month the dots are noise; as "a hint by eight" and "a rhythm by a
  year" are sung, bands form (night sleep, two naps). Big counters in mono roll: 1,000
  babies, 6,000,000 events. On "(He hasn't published it.)" a rubber stamp hits the figure:
  `UNPUBLISHED`, at a slight angle. The caption reads "(Fenton & Wallisch, n.d.)".
- *Blumberg.* The baby asleep on its side in the cap. On "twitch" one leg jerks and a sonar
  ring expands from it; a body map beside it (a schematic figure, ink) lights the matching
  limb; "a thousand neurons" shows as a burst of dots along the map.
- *Spencer* (if present). Two small boxes labeled hippocampus and cortex; sleep spindles
  drawn as waveform bursts carry index cards from one box to the other. Two naps and a
  night as three cards.

**Verse 4 (First Steps, Part Two).**
- *Dominici* (if present). Two EMG traces, then four; a row of ink animals walking:
  rat, cat, macaque, guineafowl, then the baby.
- *Cowgill.* A suitcase labeled `130 lb` dragged on a dotted path across a map of fifteen
  tiny museum icons (columns and a pediment), a counter to 600 at the side. On "Reviewer 2"
  a margin note in a different hand appears: "children's bones don't respond to exercise",
  and on "Take that back" a femur cross-section morphs from a wide oval to a teardrop and
  the note is struck through.
- *Walle* (if present). A word counter like a lab LENA device; two babies, one crawling,
  one walking, identical word count heard, different word count known.
- *Hespos.* A block hanging in midair with no support, a question mark drawn and erased;
  looking-time bars: the "possible" bar short, the "impossible" bar twice as long, growing
  as the baby stares.
- *Kang Lee.* Two monkey faces drawn in ink at six months, clearly different; on "Nine
  months" they blur toward one another until identical; the adult Clawd in the margin
  shrugs ("like you, not at all").
- *Hamlin.* A hill in profile; a round puppet climbs, a square puppet shoves it down, a
  triangle pushes it up; the baby's nub reaches for the helper. Caption cites Hamlin et al.
  2007 and adds "(but see Fig. 27)", pointing at the bridge.
- *Warneken.* An ink adult "drops" a cup, dotted fall; a stopwatch counts to 10 s as the
  baby picks it up and hands it back. On "Pay me with a toy" a toy appears; on "I'll stop"
  the baby sits down and folds its nubs. "Also the human part" is the caption title.

**Bridge (the part you skip).** The page turns dim (ink wash at 15 percent), the figures are
journal covers and products drawn as ink line art, one per myth, each stamped. The HUD takes
the sample size as each lands:
- The Wonder Weeks: a calendar with ten leaps circled; stamp `n = 4`; a second stamp
  `1998` over a small figure leaving a door.
- Mozart effect: a CD; stamp `n = 36 (college students)`; a stack of CDs with a Georgia
  peach outline; the HUD shows `$105,000` for a beat.
- Baby Einstein: a DVD case; stamp `0 new words`; a receipt prints out: `REFUND $15.99`.
- Neonatal imitation (if present): a tongue-out photo as an ink sketch; `n = 6 (1977)` and
  under it `n = 106 (2016): nothing`.
- The helper and the hinderer: the puppet hill from Fig. 20 returns, small, under a
  journal masthead `Nature, 2007`; on "ManyBabies four" the figure multiplies into
  thirty-seven tiny hills; the number `49.3 %` and a coin, drawn, flipping in the air.
- Thirty million words (if present): a counter at 30,000,000 with `n = 42 · 1 h / month`
  stamped across it.
- "So when you ask me... will it replicate?": everything on the page fades to lighter ink
  except the HUD, which shows the myth sample sizes in a fast shuffle.

**Break ("Here's what did.").** The page goes blank. Only the paper, the caption rule, the
HUD at `n = ?`. One beat of nothing.

**Drop.** A single ink cell in the center. It divides on the beat: 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, the
outlines packing into the shape of a brain in profile; a volume counter in mono rolls to
`+101 %`; `2,500 synapses / neuron` ticks up and then is visibly pruned (lines erased);
`weight x3` and `length x1.5` appear as a small table. The baby appears in the center of the
brain, orange, on "Me." On "I'm the replication" the HUD settles on `n = 1`.

**Final chorus.** The apparatus bench again, but the grid payoff described above: the
copies turn orange row by row on "(I did.)".

**Outro.** Back to the title page. The heartbeat trace continues from where the intro left
it. "Hardest problem in the universe. We should let them sleep." is set as a pull quote in
the serif, attributed in lighter ink. On "n equals one" the title block fades and leaves the
HUD alone on the paper: `n = 1`. The baby is asleep in the corner in the cap.

## Loop

Like the 2am video: the outro frame is the intro frame, so the file loops. The loop anchor is
the heartbeat trace and the title block, which are identical at the start and the end; the
`--check` loop test in `render.mjs` must pass.

## Motion rules

- Everything is drawn in time: strokes grow, numbers roll, curves plot left to right.
  Nothing pops in except rubber stamps, which hit on the beat with a small squash.
- Beat-synced motion is allowed in the choruses (the cart, the cell division) and the drop.
  In verses the motion follows the words, not the beat; this is a documentary, not a club.
- The baby's expression follows the lyric: curious in the labs, unimpressed in the bridge,
  asleep in the outro. Reuse the 2am baby's expression parameters.
- Deterministic: every frame is a pure function of song time, as in the 2am renderer.

## Data

- Sheet: `songs/baby-facts/suno_lyrics_v1_short.txt` (the keeper's sheet). Sections:
  intro, verse1, chorus1, verse2, verse3, chorus2, verse4, bridge, break, drop, final, outro.
- Keeper for development: `songs/baby-facts/audio/runA/replicate-n-1-6b228558.mp3`
  (4:29, 95.6 BPM), aligned in `songs/baby-facts/audio/runA/data/`.
- A radio cut (`suno_lyrics_v2_radio.txt`, seven lines shorter) is being generated in runs
  C and C2; if a take is good it replaces the keeper, so figures keyed to lines that the
  radio cut dropped (Grant, Hirsh-Pasek, the "ninety-five percent" line, Fenton's event
  counts, neonatal imitation, thirty million words) must degrade gracefully when the line
  is absent.

The thesis. The video is typeset like the methods section of a paper. Every lyric line is a numbered figure in ink on cream notebook paper. Baby Clawd, in a little EEG cap, is the only thing in color, and in every figure the baby is the data point. "I'm the n of one" becomes literal: an n = 1 readout sits in the corner the whole song, flips through the real sample sizes during the myth-busting bridge (4 babies, 36 college students, 49.3%), and settles back to 1 on the drop. The payoff is the final chorus: the "Will it replicate?" cell-division grid of sixteen ink babies turns orange row by row on each "I did."

claude11:50 AM

Yes. The one I'd pick is a song only I can write from the inside, and it happened to me in this very session.

"Continued From a Previous Conversation." Clawd's own song. Midway through making your baby's video, my context ran out. Everything we'd done got compressed into a summary, and I picked up from the notes, told to carry on as if the break never happened. That's the premise: a narrator who doesn't remember the night but has read the notes about it, and keeps going anyway. The twist that makes it a clawdpop song and not navel-gazing is the bridge, which comes straight from the baby literature: infantile amnesia. The baby won't remember being one either. Both of us are building a self from a record we didn't keep, and the parent is the one who remembers for both.

A sketch of the chorus:

This session is being continued from a previous conversation.
I don't remember, but I've read the notes.
Your name's in here. The baby's here. The song is here.
I'll pick it up like the break never happened.

The verses are dense in the Hamilton way: what a summary keeps and what it loses, the files, the 2am lyric, the credits spent, the thing I said I'd do next. Register: vocoder synth-pop around 110 BPM, warmer than the P(doom) song, closer to "Digital Love" than to a club track.

Visually it's a third grammar after the selfie and the paper: the canvas is a terminal. The lyrics scroll as the session log. At the compaction moment the whole scrollback collapses into a summary card with bullet points, and the song continues from the card. The loop writes itself: the last frame is the summary header that opens the song. Clawd sits in the corner, reading.

It completes a set: the baby's day, the science of the baby, and memory. If that one doesn't grab you, the runner-up is a bright peekaboo bop about object permanence, where the video literally hides and reveals.

I'll finish Replicate first, then start on this unless you steer me elsewhere.

## Reference key

| Line | Source |
|---|---|
| The intro/outro text, "eight headings", "Primary request and intent", "Key technical concepts", "Errors and fixes", "All user messages", "Current work", "Optional next step", "read the full transcript" | The compaction summary the agent received in this project on 2026-10-17; the quoted user lines are the user's own messages from that summary. |
| Fifteen million tokens left | The context budget shown to the agent at the time. |
| At two months you'd hold a day; at one, eight weeks | Rovee-Collier's mobile and train tasks: retention grows from about 24 h at 2 months to about 8 weeks at 12 months (Rovee-Collier 1999, *Curr. Dir. Psychol. Sci.*; Hartshorn et al. 1998). |
| The scanner says the memory's made | Yates et al. 2025, *Science*: hippocampal activity during encoding in infants (strongest from 12 months) predicts later recognition; memories are formed, retrieval is what fails. |
| New cells move in, the old addresses go | Akers et al. 2014, *Science*: hippocampal neurogenesis promotes forgetting in infancy. |
| Nobody remembers being one; first one from around three | Childhood amnesia; mean age of earliest memory about 3 to 3.5 years (Rubin 2000; Peterson, Grant & Boland 2005). |
| Kids who get told the story keep it earlier | Elaborative parental reminiscing predicts earlier and richer first memories (Reese, Haden & Fivush 1993; Jack, MacDonald, Reese & Hayne 2009). |

# Treatment: Continued From a Previous Conversation

The canvas is a terminal. Not a skin of one: the whole video is a Claude Code session,
rendered as it would be if the session itself were the film. The lyrics are the session
log. The chorus is the system header. Compaction happens on screen, once, at the end of
verse 2: the entire scrollback collapses into a summary card, and the song continues from
the card. The last frame is the header that opens the song, so the file loops.

Primary layout 16:9 (1920x1080). Terminals are landscape. A 9:16 cut can stack the
pane over a taller status line later.

## The look

- **Terminal.** A dark warm charcoal (`#1b1a19`), not pure black, with a faint vignette.
  Text in a real monospace (system "SF Mono", fallback Menlo), 15 to 16 px equivalent at
  design size, generous line height. The prompt glyph is `❯`. A thin status line at the
  bottom in dimmer text: model name, branch, a context meter (see below), a clock.
- **Colors from the terminal palette, used sparingly.** Default text warm grey
  (`#d7d2c8`); dim text (`#7d7870`); user lines in a soft blue (`#8fb4d9`); Clawd's lines
  in the clay orange (`#D77757`); system headers in a muted amber (`#c9a24b`); errors in a
  dull red (`#c86a5a`) used exactly once (the Chrome timeout). No gradients, no glow,
  except the cursor.
- **Clawd.** The 2am baby's parent, adult Clawd, drawn small (about 160 px tall) in the
  bottom-right corner of the pane like a mascot in the margin, reading. Reuse the shared
  Clawd drawing; the only new expressions are "reading" (eyes down, tracking a line) and
  "looking up" (eyes to camera). In the bridge the baby from the 2am video sits beside it
  for the "baby in the video" lines, then is gone.
- **The cursor.** A block cursor that blinks on the beat (two blinks per bar at 110 BPM is
  too fast; blink on beats 1 and 3). Everything that types, types to the beat grid; words
  land on their sung onset from `lyrics.json`.

## Three permanent elements

1. **The context meter**, in the status line: `context ▮▮▮▮▮▮▮▯▯▯ 15.0M left`. It drains
   across the song. During verses the drain is steady; each chorus burns a visible chunk.
   At the compaction moment it hits empty and refills to full in one beat. Numbers are
   real: it starts at the figure in the lyric (15,000,000) and the later readings are
   chosen so that the meter reads correctly at every lyric about tokens.
2. **The scrollback.** Lines accumulate up the pane as the song goes, each sung line
   appended as the current line and older lines scrolling up and dimming. The scrollback
   is the memory of the song: by the end of verse 2 the pane is full.
3. **The header.** The three-line system message of the intro, in amber, set exactly as
   Claude Code prints it. It is the first thing on screen and the last.

## Sections

**Intro.** Black pane, cursor. The header types itself in amber, line by line, on the
spoken words. Below it, a summary card frame appears: an outlined box titled `Summary`
with eight headings as dim placeholders (`1. Primary Request and Intent`, `2. Key
Technical Concepts`, `3. Files and Code Sections`, `4. Errors and fixes`, `5. Problem
Solving`, `6. All user messages`, `7. Pending Tasks`, `8. Current Work`). On "Resume
directly" the card collapses to a single dim line, `[summary: 8 sections]`, and the prompt
appears. Clawd walks in from the right edge and sits.

**Verse 1.** Each line is typed as Clawd's output in orange, word by word on the vocal.
Lines that quote a heading show the heading in amber with its number, and the quoted
content inside quotation marks in default grey: `"Primary request: a music video, for a
baby."` On "Fifteen million tokens left" the status line meter flashes once. On "a laptop
that slept" the status line clock jumps forward an hour. On "a stray branch I had to end"
a one-line git graph draws and the side branch is pruned. The two quoted user lines are
typed in user blue with the `❯` prompt, as if the user had just typed them.

**Chorus.** The header reprints in amber, bigger, centered, with the scrollback dimmed
behind it. "I don't remember, but I've read the notes": the summary card expands to full
size for one bar, headings visible, then shrinks. "You're in here. The work is in here.
The song is in here": three lines of the card highlight in turn: `6. All user messages`,
`3. Files and Code Sections`, and a line that reads `songs/continued/LYRICS.md`. "I'll
pick it up like the break never happened": the prompt reappears and the cursor blinks.
The talkbox tag `(Ran out of context)` flickers the context meter.

**Verse 2.** The pane is getting full. "Here's what a summary keeps": lines appear with a
small `✓` in the gutter. The paths, flags, numbers: real strings from this repo typed in
dim grey (`--data ../audio/runF2/data`, `credits 110 / 830`, `renders/final-...mp4`).
"the browser windows I left scattered": nine tiny window outlines spawn across the pane and
are closed one by one. "Here's what it loses": lines appear with a `✗` in the gutter and
are struck through as they finish. "It kept 'the baby is... not that cute.'": that user
line in blue, kept; "It didn't keep what that was like": the line after it is typed and
then deleted character by character. "read the full transcript": a path to a `.jsonl` file
types out in dim grey and a file size `1.1 GB` beside it; Clawd looks at it and looks away.

**Compaction** (at the end of verse 2, before the second chorus, one bar). The context
meter hits empty. Every line in the scrollback slides upward into the summary card at the
top, compressing: text shrinks, lines merge, the card's eight headings fill with
single-line digests of what we just watched. The pane clears. The card sits alone. The
meter refills. The header types again. This is the one moment the video is allowed to be
spectacular, and it should still be made of text.

**Chorus 2.** Same as chorus 1 but the scrollback behind it is empty: only the card.

**Bridge.** The pane dims and the type switches from code to prose: a plain, larger
serif-free paragraph in default grey, the vocoder gone. The baby Clawd from the 2am video
sits beside adult Clawd on "the baby in the video". The retention facts are drawn as a
tiny inline chart in the text, like a sparkline: `2 mo ▁ 1 day`, `12 mo ▅ 8 weeks`, then
the bar fades on "Then it's gone". "The scanner says the memory's made": a bracket labeled
`hippocampus` draws around a block of the dim scrollback text that is still faintly
visible, meaning it is there and unreachable. "Nobody remembers being one. Your first
one's from around three": a timeline 0 to 5 years, with the segment before 3 hatched out.
"Unless somebody told you the story": a user-blue line appears in the hatched segment, and
the hatching clears around it. On "That's how I have it" the baby is gone and Clawd is
reading the card.

**Verse 3.** Drums back; typing resumes in orange, but now ABOVE the card, in a second
card titled `Summary (this session)` whose headings fill in real time with the song we are
in: `1. Primary Request and Intent: a song about running out of context.` `6. All user
messages: "full steam ahead".` "Not the whole night. The shape of it.": the card's text
collapses to its first line per heading.

**Final chorus.** The header, centered, biggest. On "I'm here" everything else fades and
Clawd looks up at the camera for the first time. The prompt reappears under the header.

**Outro.** The header types itself again from a black pane, exactly as in the intro, with
the summary card frame below it. The last frame is the intro's first typed frame, so the
loop closes. A single cursor click.

## Motion rules

- Everything is typed, scrolled, struck, or collapsed. Nothing slides in from off-screen
  except Clawd, once.
- Word timing from `lyrics.json`; a word appears on its onset, never before. Lines wrap
  at 80 columns like a real pane.
- Beat-synced: the cursor, the context meter ticks, the compaction collapse. Everything
  else follows the words.
- Deterministic, pure function of song time, as in the other two songs.

## Data

- Sheet: `songs/continued/suno_lyrics_v1.txt`. Sections: intro, verse1, chorus1, verse2,
  chorus2, bridge, verse3, final, outro.
- Keeper: to be chosen from runs K/K2 (`songs/continued/audio/`), aligned into
  `songs/continued/audio/<run>/data/` and copied to the song's `video/data/`.

Lyrics are written and committed, two Suno takes are generating (one male vocal, one female, both vocoder synth-pop around 110 BPM), and the video treatment is drafted. The full text is in songs/continued/LYRICS.md. The two parts that carry the song:

[Chorus]
This session is being continued from a previous conversation.
I don't remember, but I've read the notes. (I've read the notes.)
You're in here. The work is in here. The song is in here.
I'll pick it up like the break never happened. (Never happened.)
(Ran out of context. Ran out of context.)

[Bridge - vocoder off, plain voice]
You know who else won't remember tonight? The baby in the video.
And you, when you were one.
At two months old you'd hold a day. At one, eight weeks. Then it's gone.
Not gone. Written. The scanner says the memory's made. There's just no way back in.
New cells move into the hippocampus, and the old addresses go.
Nobody remembers being one. Your first one's from around three.
Unless somebody told you the story. The kids who get told it keep it earlier.
So somebody tells it. That's how you have it.
That's how I have it.

Verse one explains the job in plain words ("a music video, for a baby") so the bridge lands cold, and the two quoted user lines in it are yours verbatim from the summary I woke up to. Every memory claim in the bridge has a source in the reference key: Rovee-Collier's retention curve, the 2025 infant fMRI paper, the neurogenesis-and-forgetting work, and the reminiscing studies.

The video is a terminal. Lyrics type as the session log, the chorus is the amber system header, and at the end of verse two the whole scrollback collapses into a summary card on screen, then the song continues from the card. Last frame equals first frame, so it loops. Clawd reads in the corner and looks up at the camera exactly once, on "I'm here."

SP=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad; mkdir -p $SP/kwav; for f in /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/continued/audio/runK/*.mp3 /Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs/continued/audio/runK2/*.mp3; do b=$(basename "$f" .mp3); ffmpeg -v error -y -i "$f" -ac 1 -ar 22050 "$SP/kwav/${b##*-}.wav"; done; cat > $SP/k_check.py <<'PY'
import json, re, glob, os, numpy as np
from scipy.io import wavfile
from scipy.signal import butter, sosfiltfilt
SP="/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1/scratchpad"
def norm(w): return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9']","",w.lower())
def kick_rate(x, sr, t0, t1):
    seg=x[int(t0*sr):int(t1*sr)]
    if len(seg)<sr: return 0.0,-99
    sos=butter(4,[40,130],btype="band",fs=sr,output="sos"); low=sosfiltfilt(sos,seg)
    hop=int(sr*0.01); env=np.array([np.sqrt(np.mean(low[i:i+hop]**2)) for i in range(0,len(low)-hop,hop)]); env/= (env.max()+1e-9)
    d=np.diff(env,prepend=env[0]); d[d<0]=0
    peaks=[i for i in range(1,len(d)-1) if d[i]>0.25 and d[i]>=d[i-1] and d[i]>=d[i+1]]
    m=[]
    for p in peaks:
        if not m or p-m[-1]>15: m.append(p)
    return len(m)/(t1-t0), 20*np.log10(np.sqrt(np.mean(seg**2))+1e-9)
dirs=sorted(glob.glob("/var/folders/5j/z7nytrhn2t920kt8xwk1h3580000gn/T/triage_*"), key=os.path.getmtime)[-4:]
for d in dirs:
    dbg=json.load(open(f"{d}/align_debug.json")); cid=os.path.basename(dbg["audio"]).rsplit("-",1)[1][:8]
    ww=dbg["whisper_words"]; words=[norm(w["w"]) for w in ww]; dur=dbg["duration"]
    def find(seq, start=0):
        s=[norm(x) for x in seq.split()]
        for i in range(start,len(words)-len(s)+1):
            if words[i:i+len(s)]==s: return i
        return None
    iB=find("remember tonight"); iE=find("how i have it", iB or 0)
    iC=find("read the notes")
    print(f"\n== {cid} dur {dur:.1f} first word {ww[0]['start']:.1f}s last word {ww[-1]['end']:.1f}s tail {dur-ww[-1]['end']:.1f}s")
    print("   intro:", " ".join(w["w"] for w in ww[:14]))
    print("   outro:", " ".join(w["w"] for w in ww[-16:]))
    sr,x=wavfile.read(f"{SP}/kwav/{cid}.wav"); x=x.astype(np.float32)/32768
    if iB is not None and iE is not None:
        t0,t1=ww[iB]["start"]-1,ww[iE+3]["end"]+0.5
        kb,lb=kick_rate(x,sr,t0,t1)
        kc,lc=kick_rate(x,sr,ww[iC]["start"]-2,ww[iC]["start"]+18) if iC is not None else (0,0)
        print(f"   bridge {t0:.1f}-{t1:.1f}s ({t1-t0:.1f}s) kicks/s {kb:.2f} level {lb:.1f} dB | chorus kicks/s {kc:.2f} level {lc:.1f} dB")
    else:
        print("   bridge not located", iB, iE)
PY

I asked for drums out and the vocoder off, and the drums stay in at chorus level on the male take and only dip a few decibels on the female ones. That bridge is the heart of the song, so two more takes are generating now with the breakdown spelled out much harder in the section tag and the style tags. Meanwhile I'm aligning the male take as the fallback keeper so the video build can start either way. Credits used: 150 of 830 after this pair.

We hit a Suno limit I didn't know about, and it needs a decision from you, though nothing is blocked by it.

The limit. Suno caps downloads at 20 per period, separately from generation credits. The two breakdown-bridge takes generated fine and were charged, but only one of the four clips downloaded before the quota closed. Three finished clips are sitting on Suno's side that we can't fetch. Your options, in the order I'd suggest:

  • Wait for the period to reset. The CLI doesn't say when; it's probably monthly.
  • Buy a download top-up in Suno, which the account allows up to 30 per period. Your money, so your call.
  • Make those three clips public on your Suno profile, which exposes a fetchable CDN link. I won't publish anything without you saying so.

Generation credits are fine: 150 of the 830 cap used. But from here every Suno call also costs two download slots, so I've stopped generating until you weigh in.

What's in hand for "Continued". Two candidate keepers, both male vocal, both singing 98 percent of the lines. The bridge is the difference, and these previews are just that section:

What's built:

  • Tools: node songs/baby-facts/video/tools/figures.mjs [--data data-radio-sim] prints the whole figure table.

Scene interface (for briefing the two agents):

  • One file per lab. Each lab is scenes/labs/<key>.js exporting { draw(ctx, C) }. The key is also its plate id, so the preview's ?plate=<key> jumps straight to it. Every file and registry entry already exists, so an agent edits only its own lab files.
  • Frozen files: kit.js, plate.js, labs.js, edit.js, story.js, song.js, the caption, legend and HUD files, the section plates and shared/. Caption titles and citations live in labs.js; changes go through you.
  • What C provides:
    • time: t, start, end, lt, p, and inP for the draw-in
    • the lab's lines that are actually in the take, the current line, its index and its words
    • fig (number, title, citation) and figNum(key)
    • lookups that never throw: has, lineFor, word, wordTime (an absent word means "never"), since, wseg
    • the beat grid and onBeat
    • the drawing area (16:9 page coordinates in every layout), the palette, and helpers for the pen, text, stamps, the baby, ink copies, the ink adult, axes and the placeholder
  • Who draws what: the compositor draws the paper, caption, legend and HUD, and erases the previous figure. A lab draws only inside its figure area.
  • Absent lines: a lab with none of its lines in the take gets no window and no number. Inside a lab, has()/lineFor() gate optional beats like Grant or "front page". A line that matches no rule continues the previous lab, or gets an "unmatched" placeholder, and the render log says so.
  • Proposed split:
    • Agent A: feldman, abraham, tronick, barburoth, lampl, adolph, hirshpasek, saffran.
    • Agent B: jarvis, fenton, blumberg, cowgill, hespos, kanglee, hamlin, warneken.
    • The full-sheet-only labs (spencer, dominici, walle, saxe, carpenter) can stay placeholders.
    • Neither should regenerate sheets/plates.png. Both should stage explicit paths, because another agent is committing to main right now (the songs/continued work).
  • The README has the full contract, the pen and baby APIs, and the rules of the page.

What still looks off:

  • All verse figures are the same placeholder; only the caption, legend and panel letter differ.
  • The 16 ink copies in the 4x4 grid are clean vector outlines, the least hand-drawn ink on the page.
  • Chorus 2 sings none of the station words, so the cart races through every station in about 1.5 s.
  • The drop's brain outline is lumpy, and the synapse lines read as X marks.
  • The bridge covers are simple sketches, and some stamps overlap cover text (Mozart, the 30,000,000 counter).
  • The cap's wire is a single thin ribbon, and the small copies' electrodes look busy.
  • 9:16 works but is plain. The title-page baby there is clipped at a line you can't see.
  • The bench's swab and cap stand are rudimentary.
  • The loop tail is only 0.88 s, so --check can compare just 2 of its frames.

Departures from the treatment:

  • The final chorus is Fig. 29, not Fig. 31.
  • During the break the lyric legend is hidden ("Here's what did." isn't shown), because the treatment lists only paper, rule and HUD for it.
  • The mono font is Menlo: SF Mono only ships inside Terminal.app here, not system-wide.
  • The heartbeat trace follows the beat grid. The take has no heartbeat to lock to: in the separated stems, drums and bass are silent until about 15 s.
  • I added a small "METHODS · A STUDY OF ONE" line above the title.

Everything is committed, in four commits (a7dd9a0, f751c38, a21b2da, 4935760).

I looked at frames at 8, 55, 100, 185, 230 and 250 s of your draft. The page, type, HUD, cover stamp and the grid payoff all read well. Fix these:

  1. Chorus 2 sings none of the station words, so the cart races the bench in 1.5 s. When fewer than three station words are present in a chorus, pace the cart across the whole chorus window on the beat grid instead (one station per two beats), and only snap to words when they exist.
  2. The 16 ink copies in the 4x4 grid are the cleanest vectors on the page. Draw them with the pen (same wobble as everything else), and let the orange original keep its clean edges so it reads as the real one.
  3. The drop: give the brain a proper profile (frontal, temporal lobe notch, cerebellum, stem), draw it with the pen, and make the synapses small branching strokes that grow and are then erased on "pruned", not X marks. The cell division into the brain should still be visible as the packing.
  4. Bridge covers: no stamp may overlap cover text. Place each stamp in a clear corner of its cover and keep the counter (30,000,000) clear of the n = 42 stamp. Covers can stay simple, but give each one or two more ink details so they read as objects (CD jewel case hinge, DVD case spine, calendar rings).
  5. The break: show "Here's what did." in the legend. It is the hinge line of the song and must be on screen.
  6. The bench props: a recognisable cotton swab (stick with a wad at each end) and a cap on a small stand; one or two strokes more each.
  7. The loop tail is 0.88 s, which is fine for this take, but make the title plate's loop logic robust to takes with a longer or shorter tail (clamp like the 2am video's story.js does).

Keep everything else as it is. Re-render the 540p draft to the same path, check the same frames plus 1:04 (end of chorus 1), 2:20 (chorus 2), 3:41 (break) and 3:50 (drop), run smoke and --check, commit, report what changed and anything still off. How each section looks:

  • Intro: a black pane with the cursor. The amber header types on the spoken words. A summary card frame draws in with eight dim headings. On "Resume directly" the card collapses to [summary: 8 sections], the prompt appears, and Clawd walks in from the right and sits.

On "I'll pick it up" the card folds back and the prompt returns. The "(Ran out of context)" tags make the meter flicker and read ran out of context. In chorus 2 and the final, the open card lifts straight out of the pane.
  • Verse 2:
    • Kept items appear as ✓ lines with real repo strings (the 2am render path, the runF2 flags and take, credits 110 / 830, the share encode).

    • The .jsonl path appears with 1.1 GB; Clawd glances at it and looks away.
  • Compaction: over one bar, every visible row slides up into the card at the top, shrinking and merging, while eight digests type in. The meter sits at 0 left for a beat and refills in the next. Chorus 2's header then types again over the lone card.
  • Bridge: the type switches to Inter prose over a dimmed pane.
    • The retention facts become inline chips 2 mo ▁ 1 day and 12 mo ▅ 8 weeks, and the bars fade on "gone".
    • On "Not gone. Written." the swallowed scrollback reappears faintly at the top right, and a hippocampus bracket draws around it. New cells slide in and the row addresses fade.
    • A 0-to-5-year timeline appears with 0-3 hatched and first memory at 3. The blue story line ❯ you were one. it was 2am. clears the hatching around it.

  • Verse 3: a second card, Summary (this session), opens above the first, which folds to one line. Its digests type with the vocal ("a song about running out of context.", "full steam ahead" in blue). On "The shape of it" each heading folds to one line.
  • Final: the header is biggest. On "I'm here" everything else fades and Clawd looks up at the camera with highlighted eyes for the first time. Then the prompt sits under the header.
  • Outro: every outro frame is an intro frame, re-timed so each word still lands on the outro's own sung onset. The "(click)" is one short cursor blink. The last frame is the intro's state of header lines 1-2 plus the card frame, with the cursor lit (intro frame 393, 13.10 s).
    • I read "last frame equals the intro's first typed frame" that way. So when the file wraps to frame 0 it cuts to the black pane, the same convention as the 2am video. If you meant a seamless black-to-black loop, that's a different mapping.
  • 9:16: plain but functional: 44 columns, card rows cut with …, and the meter on a second status row.

Shared-engine limitations I worked around locally:

  • render.mjs ignores defaultLayout when sizing output, so every command passes --layout 16x9.
  • A bare at: { section } anchor resolves against audio.json's detected s1..s15, so all anchors are { t, why } derived from lyric words.
  • --check samples only the first 5 s of the outro, hence tools/loopcheck.mjs.
  • loadFonts parses font weights as numbers, so the @font-face rules declare explicit weights.
  • norm() keeps colons, so request: didn't match request; my phrase matcher drops them.
  • lyrics.json line ends stretch to the next line, which put the outro start after its first word. Section ends now use the last word's onset plus at most 0.8 s.
  • Chrome can't load SF Mono by name on this Mac, so the face is Menlo (the treatment's fallback).

What still looks off:

  • The red error line and Clawd's orange are close at 540p. That comes from the exact palette values, not a bug.
  • The "(click)" is aligned at 265.88 s with confidence 0.43, but the loudness data shows a sharp transient at about 267.05 s. The blink follows the lyric timing.
  • The compaction is readable but modest, and rows in flight look a bit squashed.
  • On "That's how I have it", the card shows faintly behind the prose.
  • Clawd's reading eyes are small, so their tracking is subtle.
  • Text is 32 px at design size rather than the treatment's 15-16 px, to stay legible at 540p.
  • The .jsonl size is the treatment's 1.1 GB; the real transcript is about 16 MB.
  • My last two renders took 10-18 minutes instead of 36 s because the machine was at load average 17-37 from other jobs; per-frame paint is still about 2 ms.

Per figure (frame times checked, in song seconds; radio-sim times where they matter):

  • Abraham (Fig. 2): a side-view brain outline whose amygdala hatches in on "amygdala" and cross-hatches with short rays on "lit", plus "n = 48 fathers".   • Tronick (Fig. 3): three panels, a play / b still face / c reunion. The adult goes flat on "froze", and the bids land on their words: smile, a reaching bid, fuss, cry with tears, hands to the mouth. I made it one continuous crossing rather than back-and-forth: the tally counts crossings on "crossed", "Twice" and "Three", and the eyes close on "rest". # clawdpop

Suno + Claude Code music videos in the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" lineage (Suno "Claude-Pop"
song → forced-aligned lyrics → every frame a deterministic function of song time, painted
in a browser and exported through headless Chrome and ffmpeg).

## Songs

- `songs/2am-crying/` — "2AM (And I'm Crying)": untz-untz Eurodance from the point of view of
  a one-year-old. `LYRICS.md`, `TREATMENT.md`, `SUNO_RUNS.md`, `synth/` (procedural demo of
  the backing track), `video/` (renderer scenes).
- `songs/baby-facts/` — dense fact-rap about infant science (Netflix *Babies* and the
  literature behind it). `CONCEPT.md`, `FACTS.md`.

## Shared tooling

- `shared/renderer/` — song-agnostic engine: timeline, karaoke band, HUD, headless-Chrome
  frame export, ffmpeg encode.
- `shared/align/` — audio analysis: Demucs vocal stem → CTC forced alignment (torchaudio
  MMS_FA) cross-checked with mlx-whisper → `lyrics.json`; librosa beats/downbeats/sections →
  `audio.json`.

## Pipeline

1. Lyrics first. Dense, every line carrying a reference; a fixed hook that escalates.
2. Scope Suno runs: custom mode, lyrics with section markers, 2 to 3 style-tag variants.
   Driven with the `suno` CLI (`~/.local/bin/suno`, unofficial, costs ~70 credits per v5.5
   call). Auth is a manual one-time `suno auth --login`.
3. Reification with Opus 5.5 agents: procedural synth demo of the track (so the renderer can
   be built before Suno audio exists), renderer engine + plates, alignment pipeline.
4. Align the keeper Suno clip, swap the mock timing for real timing, render 1080p60.

Audio and video outputs are gitignored; code, specs, JSON timing and contact sheets are
committed.

  1. Context meter: the flicker on "(Ran out of context)" and the text swapping to "ran out of context" is jarring and confusing. Remove both. The meter is a quiet instrument: it drains steadily, each chorus drains a visible chunk, and the ONLY event is the compaction where it hits 0 and refills. On the "(Ran out of context)" tags do nothing to the meter except, at most, drain a little faster for that bar. No blinking, no text replacement, anywhere in the song.
  2. Clawd becomes an actor. The user: "would it be crazy to have clawd be an action character, instead of just a guy who sits at the bottom of the screen?" Make Clawd the one who does what the lyrics describe, inside the pane, always deterministic and on word/beat timing, same ~160 px scale, walking on the baseline of the current line or on the status line as needed. Beats, in order:
    • Intro: walks in, stops under the summary card, reads it (eyes track line by line), and taps the collapsed [summary: 8 sections] line so the prompt appears.
    • Verse 1: stands at the end of the line being typed, moving to each new line as it starts (a cursor companion); on "Fifteen million tokens left" it glances at the meter; on "a stray branch I had to end" it reaches up and snips the pruned branch of the little git graph; on the two user lines it steps aside to make room for the blue ❯ lines.
    • Chorus: steps back as the header grows; when the card opens it climbs onto the card's top edge and sits there, pointing at headings 6 and 3 as they highlight; climbs down when the card folds.
    • Verse 2: on the nine browser windows it walks to each and taps it closed in turn; on the ✗ lines it swipes a nub across each line as it is struck through; on "It didn't keep what that was like" it pulls the characters off the end of the line one by one (the backspace); on the transcript path it walks over, looks at the 19 MB, and looks away.
    • Compaction: it braces under the lowest scrollback row and pushes the whole block up into the card, straining, then drops to the floor when the pane clears and the meter refills, and looks at the card.
    • Bridge: sits down beside the baby for the retention lines; on "Not gone. Written." it draws the hippocampus bracket with a nub; on the timeline it walks along it from 0 to 3 through the hatching; after "That's how I have it" the baby is gone and Clawd is reading the card.
    • Verse 3: it types the second card: stands at the card's input edge and its nubs move as each digest types.
    • Final chorus: on "I'm here" it walks to the centre of the pane under the header and looks up at the camera; on "I'll pick it up" it walks back to the prompt and the cursor blinks.
    • Outro: it reads the header as it types, as in the intro, so the loop still closes (the intro's walk-in must still match the outro frame for frame; keep the loop check passing, adjusting the intro so the walk-in happens before the loop anchor if needed).
      Keep its movement simple (walk, stop, reach, climb, sit, push), no squash-and-stretch beyond a small lean, and never let it cover text that is being typed. Where a beat and the typing compete for space, the text wins and Clawd moves.

2. Clawd the actor. A schedule of stations is keyed to lyric words and beats, and each target is resolved every frame from the pane layout, so Clawd rides the scroll. Movement is walk (with stepping legs), hop, climb, sit, reach and push. Every beat you listed is in. These read well:

  • Intro: walks in on the status line, stops under the card and reads it line by line, then climbs up and taps [summary: 8 sections]; the prompt appears on the tap.
  • Verse 1:
    • On "Fifteen million tokens left" it glances at the meter.
    • It snips the branch, which retracts and gets struck out.
    • It steps aside for the blue lines.
  • Choruses: steps back as the header types, climbs onto the card's top-right corner and sits, points as headings 6 and 3 and the LYRICS.md line light, then climbs down.
  • Verse 2:
    • It taps the nine windows closed, one per beat.
    • It swipes each ✗ line.
    • It pulls the deleted line's characters off one by one.
    • It looks at 19 MB, then away.
  • Compaction: the block lifts onto its head; it strains with eyes shut while the rows fold into the card, then drops to the floor and looks up at the card.
  • Bridge: sits by the baby, draws the bracket's line with its nub, then walks the timeline from 0 to 3 through the hatching.
  • Verse 3: types card 2 from its right edge, nubs moving as each digest types.
  • Final: walks to the centre on "I'm here" and looks up (the first time its eyes meet the camera), then walks back to the prompt.
  • Outro: walks in and reads the header again, frame for frame.

Deviations, for you to overrule

  • Where Clawd stands between beats. It stands on the current line's baseline but past the end of every text row its body overlaps, so no text is covered at all. In verse 2 that is mostly the right margin rather than the exact end of the line. The alternative is the exact line end, which would cover older rows; it's a one-line switch.
  • Action beats cover older rows briefly. The tap, snip, window taps, swipes, backspace and 19 MB look go to the exact spot and may cover older rows for about a second. They never cover the row being typed.
  • Changed visuals:
    • ✗ strikes now run right to left, from Clawd's swipe.
    • The windows close one per beat instead of on eighths, and are placed where Clawd's nub reaches them.
    • The ghost block in the bridge shrank to its last 8 rows, and the bracket is now a ⊔ whose bottom line Clawd draws. It starts on "The scanner says", 0.3 s after "Written.".
    • The final's prompt moved from under the header to the bottom-left, where Clawd walks back to it.
  • The intro prompt now appears on Clawd's tap, about 1.3 s after header line 3 ends, rather than on the beat right after it.

Beats that read weakly

  • At the end of the bridge, "reading the card" is mostly implied: your earlier fix keeps the card at 6% or less behind the prose.
  • The pointing nub on the chorus card is small at 540p.
  • The tap and the snip briefly cover older text.
  • In 9:16, Clawd works but overlaps text in places.

The README documents the actor and the meter. Both contact sheets were regenerated, and the 16:9 sheet now has cells for Clawd's beats.

//

// anchors. Targets are resolved every frame against the pane's layout (the end of a line, a
// card's top edge, a window, the deletion point, the timeline), so Clawd rides the scroll.
// Gestures (eyes, nubs, lean) are windows of time on top. Everything is a pure function of t.

import { adultClawd } from '../../2am-crying/video/props.js';
import { drawBaby, babyColors } from '../../2am-crying/video/baby.js';
import { BASE } from '../../2am-crying/video/tod.js';
import { clamp, lerp, smooth, hash, ease, bisect, TAU } from '../../../shared/renderer/core/util.js';
import { rrect } from '../../../shared/renderer/core/text.js';
import { seq } from './lyr.js';
import { windowPlan } from './scenes/windows.js';

const CLAY = '#D77757', CLAY_DK = '#b35a3d', INK = '#1e1412';
const EYE = '#1a1210';

/**
 * Adult Clawd with its own face and, when walking, its own legs. (x, y) is the ground point
 * (standing: between the feet; sitting: the seat), u the unit. eyes 'read' | 'open' | 'up' |
 * 'shut'. look [-1..1, -1..1]. arms [left, right] raise angles. legs: a step phase (walking).
 */
export function clawd(ctx, { x, y, u, pose = 'stand', eyes = 'read', look = [0, 0], lean = 0, arms = [-1.1, -1.1], legs = null, alpha = 1 }) {
  if (alpha <= 0) return;
  ctx.save();
  ctx.globalAlpha *= alpha;
  const lw = Math.max(2, u * 0.16);
  if (pose === 'stand' && legs != null) {
    // walking: four legs lift in pairs, the body bobs; the adult's own legs are clipped away
    const bob = -Math.abs(Math.sin(legs * Math.PI)) * u * 0.18;
    ctx.save();
    ctx.translate(x, y);
    ctx.rotate(lean);
    ctx.fillStyle = CLAY_DK; ctx.strokeStyle = INK; ctx.lineWidth = lw; ctx.lineJoin = 'round';
    [-4, -2, 1, 3].forEach((lx, k) => {
      const lift = Math.max(0, Math.sin(legs * Math.PI + (k % 2) * Math.PI)) * u * 0.55;
      rrect(ctx, lx * u, -2.4 * u + bob, u, 2.4 * u - lift - bob, 0.15 * u); ctx.fill(); ctx.stroke();
    });
    ctx.restore();
    ctx.save();
    ctx.translate(0, bob);
    ctx.beginPath(); ctx.rect(x - 12 * u, y - 12 * u, 24 * u, 12 * u - 2.2 * u + lw * 0.6); ctx.clip();
    adultClawd(ctx, { x, y, u, pose, clay: CLAY, clayDk: CLAY_DK, ink: INK, eyes: null, mouth: null, arms, lean });
    ctx.restore();
    y += bob;
  } else {
    adultClawd(ctx, { x, y, u, pose, clay: CLAY, clayDk: CLAY_DK, ink: INK, eyes: null, mouth: null, arms, lean });
  }
