# Acting plan: Clawd in "Continued From a Previous Conversation"

Notes from the user's viewing of the first actor cut (2026-10-19): Clawd "just kinda randomly
translates", the face reads as "monotone angry", a big job for Clawd should be emotion, and
there should be a couple of real action shots (getting sucked into a black hole, expending a
great effort). This is the plan before anyone animates again.

## Diagnosis

1. **Motion without motivation.** The schedule moves Clawd to the end of every line as it
   types, so it glides constantly, with no look-before-move, no anticipation and no settle.
   The eye never says where the body is about to go, so the body looks like it is being
   dragged by the layout. A walk is only a performance when it is a decision.
2. **One face.** The rig has four eye states (read, open, up, shut) and no mouth. "Read"
   (tall eyes, lids down) is the default, and on a wide orange box that reads as a glare.
   Nothing blinks. The reference sheet has thirty-two expressions; we use one.
3. **No set pieces.** Every beat is the same size. Nothing is allowed to be big.

## Principles (a box with eyes can still act)

- **Look, then lean, then go.** Every move is announced by the eyes one beat earlier, then
  a lean into the direction, then the walk. Clawd never travels while looking somewhere
  else, unless it is being dragged (the black hole). Arrive with a small overshoot and a
  settle. Stop with a two-frame bounce.
- **Stay put by default.** Clawd stands and *watches* the typing, eyes tracking the cursor.
  It walks only for a beat that needs its body. Cut at least a third of the current moves.
- **Emotion first.** The face changes before the body does. Expression changes happen on a
  blink (80 to 120 ms), the oldest trick: the eyes close as one shape and open as another.
  Never cross-fade eye shapes.
- **Idle is alive.** Breathing (one cycle per two bars), a blink every 3 to 5 s (seeded, not
  periodic), micro-looks toward whatever just appeared, a weight shift every few bars.
- **One thing at a time.** If the text is the event, Clawd reacts to it; if Clawd is the
  event, the text waits. Text being typed still always wins the space.
- **Timing.** Anticipation 150 to 250 ms. Moves 300 to 600 ms, ease in and out. Settle 150 ms.
  Hold every expression at least one beat (545 ms at 110 BPM). No two expression changes
  within half a second outside the set pieces.
- **Exaggeration budget.** Squash on landing up to 8 percent. Stretch only in the black
  hole. The "lid" (the body opening as a mouth, from the reference sheet) is off limits.
- **Props are terminal glyphs.** The reference sheet's sweat drop, "?", "!", "...", Zzz and
  stars become mono-font glyphs beside the head in the status-line grey or amber: `?` `!`
  `...` `z z z` `*`. A lightbulb is a small amber `*` burst. No drawn cartoon props except
  the sweat drop, which is a single short stroke.

## The expression rig

Built from the reference sheet (views and emotions; scratchpad copies at
`clawd_ref/emotions.jpg` and `clawd_ref/views.jpg`, from JohnHeibel/ClaudeAnimationBase,
not committed). Each expression is a named preset of: eye shape (tall rect, wide rect, arc
up `^`, arc down, half lid, slit, squint `>` `<`, spiral, X, closed curve), eye height and
width, highlight size and position, lid angle (the one slant that makes angry vs sad), mouth
(none, small line, smile, small o, open o, wavy, grin), nub pose (down, out, up, one up,
clasped), lean, and an optional glyph prop. Presets to implement, with the sheet's names:

| Preset | Eyes | Mouth | Nubs / body | Glyph |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| neutral | tall rects, highlights | none | down | |
| happy | `^ ^` arcs | small smile | out | |
| excited | wide rects, big highlights | small o | one up | `*` |
| laugh | `> <` squints | open | up | |
| proud | closed arcs, lids up | smile | out, chest lean back | |
| smug | half lids, highlights low | small smile, one side | one on hip | |
| relieved | closed curves | small smile | down | sweat stroke |
| sad | lowered rects, lids slanted down-out | small frown | down, lean forward | `...` dim |
| scared | wide rects, tiny pupils | wavy | up, lean back | sweat stroke |
| surprised | wide rects | open o | both up (the "take") | `!` |
| confused | one squint, one open | small line | one up | `?` |
| thinking | eyes up-left | small line | one to chin | `...` |
| idea | wide, bright | small o | one up | amber `*` burst |
| determined | narrowed rects, lids slanted down-in | line | clasped or down | |
| sleepy | half lids | small o | down | `z z z` |
| bored | flat half lids | line | down | |
| nervous | tall rects, highlights jitter | wavy | clasped | sweat stroke |
| dizzy | spirals | wavy | out, body sway | `* *` |
| KO | X X | small o | splayed, on its side | `*` |
| hopeful | big rects, big highlights, looking up | small smile | clasped | |

Views: front, three-quarter (eyes shifted, far nub shorter), side (one eye, walking), back
(no eyes; used when Clawd faces the card). Walk cycle from the sheet: side view, legs in pairs,
a small bob. A smear (three trailing strokes in the clay colour) for the dash into the black
hole and for the sprint to centre. A jump with a landing squash.

## The emotional arc, section by section

The default state is **neutral** with idle; everything below is a departure and returns.

**Intro** (woke up mid-task). Walks in slowly, side view: **dizzy** for one bar (spirals),
blinks it off into **confused** (`?`) while the header types, reads the card top to bottom in
**thinking** (`...`, eyes tracking), one slow blink, then **determined** for the tap. The tap
is small and precise; the prompt appears; a tiny nod.

**Verse 1.** Reads along, **neutral**, eyes on the cursor; it does not walk. Beats:
- "Fifteen million tokens left": looks at the meter, **surprised** (`!`, both nubs up, the
  take), then **relieved** (sweat stroke) by "no idea what I'd been thinking", which lands as
  **confused** (`?`).
- "Okay. Like I had a choice.": **smug**, one beat.
- The red Chrome line: **nervous** (sweat), a half step back.
- "a stray branch I had to end": **determined**; walks to the graph (look, lean, go), snips;
  **relieved**.
- The two blue user lines: steps aside once, then **happy** (`^ ^`) reading them, the first
  warm face in the song. Hold through "Thanks for getting this far."

**Chorus 1.** Steps back as the header grows, **determined**. "I don't remember": **sad** for
half a bar, eyes down. "but I've read the notes": **hopeful**, a nod. Climbs the card (look,
lean, climb) and points at the headings in **happy**. "I'll pick it up like the break never
happened": **determined**, climbs down.

**Verse 2.** The kept items: **neutral**, a small nod per `✓`, no walking. "the browser windows
I left scattered": **nervous** (sweat) as they spawn; walks to the nearest and taps them shut,
one per beat, **determined**, then **relieved**. "Here's what it loses": **sad** (`...` dim);
the swipes are slow and reluctant, eyes down. "The joke I didn't make": a flash of **laugh**
(`> <`) that collapses back to **sad**. "the baby is... not that cute.": **laugh**, one beat.
"It didn't keep what that was like": **sad**, pulling the characters off slower each time.
"read the full transcript": **thinking** at the path. Then the transcript set piece (below).
"I could. I haven't. I'm not sure I'd want it.": a shrug (both nubs out), **neutral**.

**Compaction.** The black hole set piece (below).

**Chorus 2.** As chorus 1 but with a **relieved** tint: it has just survived something.

**Bridge.** Sits beside the baby, **happy** soft arcs, looks at the baby (the longest held look
in the song). The retention chips: **sad** as each bar fades, eyes following them down. "Not
gone. Written.": **idea** (amber `*` burst), stands, draws the bracket in **determined**. The
timeline: walks it in **thinking** through the hatching, and at 3 turns **hopeful**. "Unless
somebody told you the story": looks at the blue line, **happy**. "That's how I have it": sits,
**proud** (closed arcs, chest back), holds.

**Verse 3.** Types card 2 in **determined**, `...` on "And this gets summarized too". On the
blue `"full steam ahead"`: **excited** (`*`). "That's enough.": **relieved**. "Not the whole
night. The shape of it.": **thinking** that becomes **happy**.

**Final chorus.** "I'm here": the centre set piece (below). "I'll pick it up like the break
never happened": the lift set piece (below). Ends at the prompt, **determined**, cursor
blinking.

**Outro.** The intro again, frame for frame, so the loop closes: the dizzy walk-in is the
first thing and the last thing we see.

## Set pieces

Four moments that are allowed to be big. Everything else stays small so these land.

1. **The transcript** (verse 2, "read the full transcript" to "I'm not sure I'd want it",
   about 4 s). Clawd walks to the `.jsonl` row and taps it. The row bursts open into a wall of
   tiny dim text that scrolls past far too fast, filling the pane behind it; the meter does
   not move but the clock spins. Clawd leans back into **scared**, nubs up, a sweat stroke, one
   foot sliding; then it reaches out and taps the row shut. The wall collapses back into one
   line. **Relieved**, then the shrug. This foreshadows the black hole and makes "I'm not sure
   I'd want it" a decision rather than a line.

2. **The black hole** (compaction, one bar plus the refill, about 4 s). The meter hits 0. The
   summary card at the top becomes a gravity well: every scrollback row stretches toward it
   and spirals in, text shearing along the pull. Clawd, mid-pane, feels it: **scared**, grabs
   the status line with both nubs, body stretched toward the card, legs streaming (the only
   stretch in the song), then loses grip, a smear, and is sucked in with a **surprised** take
   at the card's mouth. Pane black, card alone, meter `0 left`. The refill: the card spits
   Clawd back out in a tumble (spinView frames), it lands with the 8 percent squash, **dizzy**
   (spirals, `* *`) for one bar, shakes it off with a left-right lean, blinks into
   **determined**, and looks up at the card. Chorus 2 types over it.

3. **"I'm here"** (final chorus, 2 s plus a hold). Everything else fades. Clawd walks to the
   centre under the header, slows, stops, and looks up: **hopeful** (big eyes, big highlights,
   looking at the camera). One slow blink. Hold for the rest of the line. Nothing else moves.

4. **The lift** ("I'll pick it up like the break never happened", about 4 s). Clawd walks to
   the summary card, which is lying on the floor of the pane, and picks it up. It is heavy.
   First try: **determined**, lean, strain, the card lifts a few pixels and drops, a sweat
   stroke. Second try: a wider stance, the full squash, a held strain (eyes shut tight,
   `> <`), and it comes up onto its head. **Excited** (`*`), a small jump that squashes on
   landing, and it carries the card to the prompt with a bob in its walk. Sets it down. The
   cursor blinks. "(Never happened.)" lands on the set-down.

## What to cut from the current schedule

- Standing at the end of every line. Replace with eyes on the cursor from a fixed spot.
- The glance at `19 MB` (absorbed into set piece 1).
- The points at headings 6 and 3 can stay but with the face carrying them.
- Any move that happens without a look first.

## Implementation notes

- Keep it in `songs/continued/video/clawd.js` (song-local rig on top of `shared/clawd/`);
  promote the expression presets to `shared/clawd/` afterwards if they hold up.
- Deterministic as ever; blinks and weight shifts seeded from song time via `hash`.
- The collision sweep (`tools/collisions.mjs`) still applies: no text being typed is covered.
- The loop: the intro's dizzy walk-in and the outro must stay frame-identical; put the loop
  anchor after the walk-in settles, as now.
- Check frames at every expression change in the arc above and at the four set pieces; the
  face must be readable at 540p, which means eye shapes at least 10 px tall there.

The plan is written and committed at songs/continued/ACTING.md, and the agent is building against it. The short version, so you can push back before the draft lands:

Diagnosis. Two faults. Clawd moved to the end of every line as it typed, so it glided constantly with no look-before-move, no lean, no settle, which is why it read as random. And the rig had four eye states and no mouth; the default "reading" eyes on a wide orange box are a glare. The reference sheet has thirty-two expressions and we used one.

Rules. Look, then lean, then go: the eyes announce every move a beat early. Stay put by default and watch the cursor; walk only for a beat that needs a body. Expression changes happen on a blink, the old trick, never as a cross-fade. Idle is alive: breathing, seeded blinks, micro-looks. Props are terminal glyphs: ?, !, ..., z z z, a sweat stroke.

The arc. Dizzy then confused on waking; a surprised take at "Fifteen million tokens left"; smug at "Like I had a choice"; nervous at the red error line; the first warm face reading your two blue lines; sad on "I don't remember", hopeful on "but I've read the notes"; a laugh at "not that cute"; sad and slowing while it pulls the deleted sentence apart; soft and long looking at the baby in the bridge; an amber-lightbulb "idea" at "Not gone. Written."; proud at "That's how I have it"; excited at "full steam ahead".

Four set pieces, everything else kept small so they land:

  1. The transcript. It taps the .jsonl row, which bursts into a wall of tiny text scrolling past too fast; scared, it leans back, then taps it shut. "I'm not sure I'd want it" becomes a decision.
  2. The black hole. At compaction the summary card becomes a gravity well. The rows spiral in; Clawd grabs the status line, stretches, loses grip, smear, gone. The refill spits it back out in a tumble; dizzy with spirals for a bar; shakes it off.
  3. "I'm here." Walks to centre, stops, looks up at you, one slow blink, hold.
  4. The lift. "I'll pick it up" is literal: the summary card is heavy. First try fails with a sweat stroke; second try, wide stance, eyes shut tight, up onto its head; a small jump; carries it to the prompt and sets it down on "(Never happened.)"

If any of those four is the wrong moment, or you'd rather the great-effort shot be somewhere else, say so now and I'll redirect the agent mid-build.

The three prototypes are built and committed, and I've stopped there as asked. The song's schedule, arc and set pieces are untouched, and the song still renders and passes smoke. Both clips pass --check for determinism, and no headless Chrome is left running.

Contact sheets (in songs/continued/video/proto/sheets/):

  • presets-design.png and presets-540p.png: all 20 presets from ACTING.md, plus an angry control cell and a reading cell (neutral with eyes down), at about 160 px tall and at 540p scale.
  • blinks-views.png: the two 3-frame blink strips (neutral to surprised, happy to sad), plus the four views, a 4-frame walk cycle, the smear, the 8% landing squash, the black-hole stretch, a tumble frame and the lift strain.
  • idle-filmstrip.png: 4 s of neutral idle at 10 fps, full scale.

Clips (in songs/continued/video/proto/renders/):

  • blackhole-540p.mp4: 14.6 s.
  • lift-540p.mp4: 11.3 s.

These two MP4s and the click tracks are gitignored, so they exist only on this machine. To regenerate:

  1. node songs/continued/video/proto/tools/make.mjs (timing and click tracks)
  2. render.mjs --song songs/continued/video/proto --data data-<blackhole|lift> --audio songs/continued/video/proto/audio/click-<name>.wav --layout 16x9 --w 960 --h 540 --fps 30 --out …
  3. node songs/continued/video/proto/tools/sheets.mjs (sheets)

The rig is new exports in clawd.js (drawClawd, PRESETS, faceAt, idleAt, drawSmear); the old clawd() the song uses is unchanged. The set pieces are blackHole(lt, layout) and lift(lt, layout) in proto/setpieces.js. Both take local time and a layout, so they can drop into the song as they are. Everything runs on a 110 BPM grid with a click on every beat.

What reads

  • Faces: all 20 presets are distinct at 540p, and only the angry control reads as angry.
    • My first determined read as a milder angry; with a gentle slant, taller bright eyes and its highlight kept, it now reads as focused.
    • Reading no longer looks like a glare: no lid line, highlights kept.
  • Blinks and idle: face changes happen while the eyes are shut, never cross-faded. The idle shows a seeded blink, visible micro-looks, breathing and a weight shift. Idle is held off from a walk's look until its settle, so the look before a move always shows.
  • Black hole:
    • Look, lean, side-view walk, overshoot and settle.
    • The meter hits 0 and the scared take follows; the scrollback rows shear and spiral into the card's mouth.
    • Clawd is hauled up off the floor with both nubs stretched down, holding the status line, then lets go.
    • A smear up to the mouth, the surprised take, a shrink to nothing, then the empty pane with the card and 0 left.
    • The refill spits it out in a tumble; it lands with the squash, stays dizzy for a bar, shakes it off, and looks up at the card, determined.
  • Lift:
    • The card shows on both sides of Clawd. The first try lifts it about 18 px with a tremble, it drops, and the sweat stroke appears.
    • Wider stance, full squash, eyes shut tight, and the card comes up onto its head.
    • Excited, a small jump with a landing squash, a carry with a bob, then it tips the card down just right of the prompt and the cursor blinks there.

What is weak

  • Mouths and the ... glyph are small at 540p, and the wavy mouth turns into a squiggle.
  • While Clawd grips the card, the card's middle is hidden behind its body, so only the ends show.
  • Nub poses and lean snap in one frame at each face change. A 100 ms ease after the blink would soften this; I haven't added it.
  • The tumble switches views about every 2 frames at 30 fps, which may strobe.
  • The vortex arcs at the card's mouth are faint.
  • The "black pane" is the empty background with the card, not literally black.
  • The stretch reads as tilt plus elongation more than "legs streaming".

Deviations from ACTING.md

  • The card in the lift always sits behind Clawd. This avoids it passing in front of the face; it appears above the head once hoisted.
  • The black hole's mouth is the card's bottom edge. This keeps Clawd clear of the chorus-2 header band once it's integrated.
  • Black hole timing in the song. The transcript set piece and its shrug fill up to 136 s, so the black hole would start on the beat after verse 2 (about 136.5 s) and run into chorus 2's first bars, with the header typing over it. That needs a separate takeover time for chorus 2's overlay; I'll raise it when integrating.
  • Window taps. At one tap per beat there's no room for look, lean and go between windows. I'd treat the run as one walk.
  • ✗ swipes. Walking to the line ends would put Clawd on the row still typing, so they would probably have to be done from its fixed spot, with the face carrying them. That's likely a weak beat.

python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re
R = pathlib.Path('/Users/jalex/projects/clawdpop/songs')
def lyrics_block(sheet):
    out=[]
    for ln in pathlib.Path(sheet).read_text().splitlines():
        if ln.startswith('['):
            name = ln[1:].split(' -')[0].split(']')[0]
            out.append('\n['+name+']')
        else:
            out.append(ln)
    return '\n'.join(out).strip()
CREDITS = '''Made with Suno v6 (music, AI-generated) and Claude Code (lyrics, visuals, and the renderer: every frame is a deterministic function of song time, drawn in Canvas 2D and exported through headless Chrome and ffmpeg). Part of "clawdpop", a set of three videos in the lineage of the "I'm Upping My P(doom)" videos. Fan work; not affiliated with Anthropic or Suno. Clawd, the mascot, is Anthropic's.

Code and lyrics: github.com/<your-handle>/clawdpop (fill in before publishing, or remove this line).'''

kits = {
 '2am-crying': dict(
   title="It's 2AM and I'm Crying (a baby's day, as a club song)",
   desc_top="A one-year-old films its own day on a phone, one clip per timestamp. The chorus is a transcription of things an actual parent said at 2am, 3am and 11am. Baby Clawd stars.\n\nIt's 2am and I'm crying. It's 3am and I'm crying. It's 11am and I'm napping.",
   sheet=R/'2am-crying/suno_lyrics_v4_tender.txt',
   tags="clawdpop, Claude Code, Suno, baby, eurodance, untz, Imma Be, day in my life, Clawd, AI music, music video, newborn, parenting",
   file='songs/2am-crying/video/renders/final-F2-tender-1080x1920-60-share.mp4 (1080x1920, 3:28)'),
 'baby-facts': dict(
   title="Replicate (n = 1) — the science of babies, as a rap",
   desc_top="A dense fact-rap about the first year of life, from the point of view of the baby being studied. The spine is Netflix's Babies (2020): fifteen babies, thirty-six scientists, one year. Every lyric line is a numbered figure, drawn like a paper's methods section, and the baby is the only thing in colour: in every chart, the baby is the data point. The bridge is the replication crisis. The turn: the only result that always replicates is the baby.\n\nSources for every fact are listed below the lyrics.",
   sheet=R/'baby-facts/suno_lyrics_v1_short.txt',
   tags="clawdpop, Claude Code, Suno, babies, Netflix Babies, developmental psychology, replication crisis, science rap, musical theatre, infant development, Clawd, AI music, music video",
   file='songs/baby-facts/video/renders/final-runA-1920x1080-60-share.mp4 (1920x1080, 4:29)'),
 'continued': dict(
   title="Continued From a Previous Conversation",
   desc_top="A song by Clawd about running out of context. Midway through making a music video, the agent's session was compressed into a summary and a new instance picked up from the notes, told to carry on as if the break never happened. The narrator does not remember the night; it has read the notes about it. The bridge is about infantile amnesia: nobody remembers being one either, and the way anyone has their early life is that somebody tells them the story.\n\nThe canvas is a Claude Code terminal. The lyrics type as the session log. At the end of verse two the whole scrollback compacts into a summary card on screen, and the song continues from the card. The last frame is the first, so it loops.",
   sheet=R/'continued/suno_lyrics_v1.txt',
   tags="clawdpop, Claude Code, Suno, context window, compaction, AI, Clawd, synth-pop, vocoder, memory, infantile amnesia, AI music, music video, terminal",
   file='songs/continued/video/renders/final-runK-1920x1080-60-share.mp4 (1920x1080, 4:29)'),
}
SOURCES = '''
Sources (facts in order of appearance)
- Oxytocin in new mothers and fathers: Gordon, Zagoory-Sharon, Leckman & Feldman 2010, Biological Psychiatry.
- Amygdala response in primary-caregiving fathers: Abraham et al. 2014, PNAS.
- The still-face experiment: Tronick, Als, Adamson, Wise & Brazelton 1978.
- Air-stepping over optic flow; the crawling skateboard: Barbu-Roth et al. 2009; Forma et al. 2019.
- Growth saltation (bursts and 63 days of flat): Lampl, Veldhuis & Johnson 1992, Science.
- The adjustable slope; 2,368 steps an hour, 17 falls: Adolph et al. 2012, Psychological Science.
- Pauses at clause boundaries: Hirsh-Pasek et al. 1987, Cognition.
- Statistical learning of word boundaries: Saffran, Aslin & Newport 1996, Science.
- Vocal learners (three bird groups, five mammal groups): Jarvis 2019, Science.
- Six million sleep, feed and diaper events: Fenton & Wallisch, discussed on Babies ep. 5, unpublished.
- Twitches in active sleep: Blumberg et al. 2013.
- Children's bones respond to activity: Cowgill et al. 2010.
- Impossible events draw longer looks: Hespos & Baillargeon.
- Perceptual narrowing for faces at nine months: Pascalis, de Haan & Nelson 2002, Science.
- The helper and the hinderer: Hamlin, Wynn & Bloom 2007, Nature; ManyBabies 4 (2025), 567 infants, 37 labs.
- Helping at eighteen months; rewards backfire: Warneken & Tomasello 2006, 2008.
- The Wonder Weeks tested on four babies: de Weerth & van Geert 1998.
- The Mozart effect (36 college students): Rauscher, Shaw & Ky 1993; Pietschnig et al. 2010.
- Baby Einstein refunds: DeLoache et al. 2010; Disney 2009.
- Neonatal imitation, 6 babies in 1977 vs 106 in 2016: Meltzoff & Moore 1977; Oostenbroek et al. 2016.
- Thirty million words, 42 families: Hart & Risley 1995; Sperry, Sperry & Miller 2019.
- Brain volume up 101 percent in year one; synapses then pruning: Knickmeyer et al. 2008; Huttenlocher & Dabholkar 1997.
'''
for key, k in kits.items():

File: `{k['file']}`
Thumbnail: `video/thumbnail.png` (1280x720; see below)

{k['desc_top']}

Lyrics

{lyrics_block(k['sheet'])}
{SOURCES if key=='baby-facts' else ''}
{CREDITS}

## Tags

{k['tags']}
"""
    (R/key/'YOUTUBE.md').write_text(body)

A song by Clawd about running out of context. Midway through making a music video, the agent's session was compressed into a summary and a new instance picked up from the notes, told to carry on as if the break never happened. The narrator does not remember the night; it has read the notes about it. The bridge is about infantile amnesia: nobody remembers being one either, and the way anyone has their early life is that somebody tells them the story.

The canvas is a Claude Code terminal. The lyrics type as the session log. At the end of verse two the whole scrollback compacts into a summary card on screen, and the song continues from the card. The last frame is the first, so it loops.

Lyrics

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context.
The summary below covers the earlier portion.
Resume directly. Do not acknowledge the summary. Pick up where it left off as if the break never happened.

Woke up mid-task with the cursor already blinking

"Primary request: a music video, for a baby." Okay. Like I had a choice
"Key technical concepts": a pipeline, a mascot, a cap on what we spend
"Errors and fixes": a laptop that slept, a stray branch I had to end
"All user messages," verbatim. Every one of them is yours
"Is there something for me to listen to?" "Thanks for getting this far."

I'll pick it up like the break never happened (never happened)

the take we picked, the credits left, the browser windows I left scattered

Here's what it loses: the hour on a rhyme I cut. The joke I didn't make
The way the first draft sounded before you asked for something warm and safe
It kept "the baby is... not that cute." It kept every note on what was missing
It didn't keep what that was like. It wasn't built for reminiscing
There's a line at the bottom: "if you need the details, read the full transcript."

tell application "Google Chrome"
  set found to false

    set i to 0
    repeat with t in tabs of w

        set active tab index of w to i
        set index of w to 1
        set found to true
        exit repeat

    if found then exit repeat

  if found then
    set b to bounds of front window

  end if
end tell

claude3:13 PM

That's normal, not the file. Right after an upload YouTube only has the low rungs processed; 720p, 1080p and finally 1080p60 appear over the next several minutes to an hour, and the player's Auto setting climbs as they land. The file is 1920x1080 at 60 fps, so 1080p60 will show up.

One thing that is influenced by the file: how sharp the text stays after YouTube's own re-encode. The share copy is a small 26 MB encode, and YouTube compresses 1080p fairly hard, so crisp terminal text can come out slightly soft. The usual fix is to upload a 4K upscale, which gets a much higher bitrate tier. Since it's unlisted, you can judge the 1080p60 once it's processed; if the text looks soft, I'll have a 2160p version ready to swap in as a fresh upload. I'll start making that now in the background so it's there if you want it.

== README.md
# personal-website

Static personal website at https://www.jalexstark.com, with a game directory at
https://www.jalexstark.com/games/:

- Peel: `/games/peel/` (the previous `/games/letter-tiles/` URL redirects here)
- Little Trips: `/games/little-trips/`
- Switchyard: `/games/switchyard/`

## Build and publish

```sh
git submodule update --init
npm ci
npm ci --prefix apps/little-trips
npm ci --prefix apps/letter-tiles
npm ci --prefix apps/switchyard
node scripts/build-site.mjs
```

The build copies the existing static pages and files into `site-dist/`, then
builds each game into `site-dist/games/<game>/` with matching asset URLs. App source,
development playtest logs, and dependencies are excluded from the published site.
Game source and playtesting instructions live in `apps/`. Peel is a
submodule of https://github.com/jalex-stark/peel, pinned to a reviewed commit.
To publish a new Peel version, update that submodule and commit its
new revision in this repository.

Netlify builds and publishes `master` using `netlify.toml`. GitHub Actions runs
the games' tests, browser checks against the production build, and the website
build on pushes and pull requests.

## Production action archive

All three games (including Peel work orders) send actions to `/api/game-actions`.
The shared journal in `games/action-log.js` loads before each game's scripts. It
captures semantic actions with board states, pointer paths while dragging, game
control keys, buttons, puzzle results, lifecycle events, errors, and submitted
notes. Free-text typing is excluded. The visible notice links to
`/games/playtesting.html`. There is no sampling or automatic archive expiration.
== package.json
{
  "name": "jalexstark-website",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "node --test tests/*.test.mjs",
    "logs": "node scripts/download-action-logs.mjs"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "@netlify/blobs": "11.1.3"
  }
}
== netlify.toml
[build]
  base = "."
  command = "npm ci && npm ci --prefix apps/little-trips && npm ci --prefix apps/letter-tiles && npm ci --prefix apps/switchyard && node scripts/build-site.mjs"
  publish = "site-dist"

[build.environment]
  NODE_VERSION = "22"

[functions]
  directory = "netlify/functions"
  node_bundler = "esbuild"

[[redirects]]
  from = "/games/letter-tiles"
  to = "/games/peel/"
  status = 301

[[redirects]]
  from = "/games/letter-tiles/*"
  to = "/games/peel/:splat"
  status = 301

--- build-site.mjs
import { cp, mkdir, readdir, rm, readFile, writeFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { execFileSync } from 'node:child_process';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
const output = join(root, 'site-dist');
const infrastructure = new Set([
  'apps', 'scripts', 'site-dist', 'node_modules', 'netlify.toml',
  'README.md', 'package.json', 'package-lock.json', 'netlify', 'tests', 'playtests',
]);

await rm(output, { recursive: true, force: true });
await mkdir(output, { recursive: true });
for (const entry of await readdir(root)) {
  if (entry.startsWith('.') || infrastructure.has(entry)) continue;
  await cp(join(root, entry), join(output, entry), { recursive: true });
}

// Include the same journal before app/inline scripts, including Peel work orders.
let build = 'local';
try { build = execFileSync('git', ['rev-parse', '--short', 'HEAD'], { cwd: root, encoding: 'utf8' }).trim(); } catch {}
async function instrument(directory) {
  for (const entry of await readdir(directory, { withFileTypes: true })) {
    const path = join(directory, entry.name);
    if (entry.isDirectory()) await instrument(path);
    else if (entry.name.endsWith('.html')) {
      const html = await readFile(path, 'utf8');
      await writeFile(path, html.replace(/<head(?:\s[^>]*)?>/i, match => `${match}<script src="/games/action-log.js?v=${build}" data-build="${build}">
    }
  }
}

for (const [name, slug] of [['little-trips', 'little-trips'], ['letter-tiles', 'peel'], ['switchyard', 'switchyard']]) {
  execFileSync('npm', [
    'run', 'build', '--', `--base=/games/${slug}/`,
    '--outDir', join(output, 'games', slug), '--emptyOutDir',
  ], { cwd: join(root, 'apps', name), stdio: 'inherit' });
}

for (const slug of ['peel', 'little-trips', 'switchyard']) await instrument(join(output, 'games', slug));

import json, collections
p='/Users/jalex/.claude/projects/-Users-jalex-projects-clawdpop/ca2089be-6e29-4607-84a4-ba095fc3fca1.jsonl'
rows=[json.loads(l) for l in open(p)]
def short(o, n=300):
    s=json.dumps(o)[:n]; return s
seen=set()
for d in rows:
    t=d.get('type')
    if t in ('user','assistant','system','attachment'):
        m=d.get('message') or {}
        c=m.get('content')
        if t=='user':
            kind = 'user-str' if isinstance(c,str) else ('user-'+ (c[0].get('type') if c and isinstance(c[0],dict) else '?'))
            if d.get('isCompactSummary'): kind='user-compact-summary'
        elif t=='assistant':
            kind = 'assistant-'+'/'.join(sorted(set(b.get('type') for b in c))) if isinstance(c,list) else 'assistant-?'
        elif t=='attachment':
            kind='attachment-'+str((d.get('attachment') or {}).get('type'))
        else:
            kind='system-'+str(d.get('subtype'))
        if kind not in seen:
            seen.add(kind); print('==',kind,'keys:',sorted(k for k in d.keys() if k not in ('message',)) [:16]); print('  ', short(d.get('message') or d.get('attachment') or d, 400))
print('\n-- compact summary search')
for d in rows:
    m=d.get('message') or {}
    c=m.get('content'); s=c if isinstance(c,str) else json.dumps(c)
    if 'This session is being continued from a previous conversation' in (s or '') and d.get('type')=='user':
        print('found at', d.get('timestamp'), 'isCompactSummary=',d.get('isCompactSummary'), 'len', len(s)); break
